STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r11.claim: The surah gives prominence to Israelite history and stresses God's blessings upon the Israelites throughout their history.
STUDYQURAN:2:intro/r11.anchor: The history of the Children of Israel figures prominently in this sūrah. Stressed are the blessings of God upon the Israelites throughout their history

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r1.claim: A Persian couplet compares human beings to a child who cries for a compassionate nurse's milk: one must cry and listen so that divine bounty may flow.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r1.anchor: طفل يك روزه همي داند طريق كه بكيرم تارسد دايه شفيق

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r2.claim: After Adam's descent, God promised that inspiration and revelation would continue for him and his descendants through prophets, revelation, and revealed books.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r2.anchor: أن الله تعالى لما ابتلى آدم بالهبوط إلى الأرض بشره بأن إلهامه ووحيه لا ينقطع عنه

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r8.claim: The plural address Banu Israel covers males and females when mixed; Israel is Jacob, and the Hebrew elements mean servant of God.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r8.anchor: البنون اسم للذكور والإناث إذا اجتمعوا وإسرائيل اسم يعقوب عليه السلام ومعناه عبد الله

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r9.claim: The address targets Jews around Medina, including Banu Qurayza and Banu al-Nadir, descendants of Jacob; they are singled out as exceptionally blessed yet especially ungrateful.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r9.anchor: والخطاب لليهود المعاصرين للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الذين كانوا حوالي المدينة من بني قريظة والنضير

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r10.claim: Remembering with the first vocalization of dhikr means retaining blessings in the heart; the other vocalization includes spoken remembrance, so the command calls for inward preservation and verbal thanks.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r10.anchor: الذكر بضم الذال بالقلب خاصة بمعنى الحفظ الذي يضاد النسيان والذكر بكسر الذال يقع على الذكر باللسان

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r11.claim: The singular word for favor is a collective noun, as in the verse about being unable to count God's favors; the phrase bestowed upon you implies they had forgotten the favors entirely.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r11.anchor: لأن النعمة اسم جنس بمعنى الجمع

BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r12.claim: Mentioning favors bestowed on them counters natural envy: people should not look at those with greater worldly wealth and despise their own blessings, but should see their own gifts and give thanks.
BURSEVI:v1p90#2/r12.anchor: لأن الإنسان غيور حسود بالطبع فإذا نظر إلى ما أنعم الله على غيره حمله الغيرة والحسد

BURSEVI:v1p91/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r1.speaker: أرباب المعاني
BURSEVI:v1p91/r1.claim: The people of spiritual meanings say God linked Israel to remembering favors, while Muhammad's community is told to remember God; other nations look from blessing to Benefactor, whereas this community looks from Benefactor to blessing, and a blessing must not veil its Giver.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r1.anchor: قال أرباب المعاني ربط سبحانه وتعالى بني إسرائيل بذكر النعمة وأسقطه عن أمة محمد

BURSEVI:v1p91/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r2.claim: Fulfilling the covenant means completing it without neglect; the covenant accepted at the primordial pact covers faith, obedience, prohibitions, commandments, and specifically Israel's Torah pledge to follow Muhammad.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r2.anchor: الذي قبلتم يوم الميثاق وهو عام في جميع أوامره

BURSEVI:v1p91/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r3.claim: Covenant also means a pledge or testament that must be preserved continually; here God's covenant is grammatically annexed to its agent.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r3.anchor: والعهد حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا فحالا والمراد منه الموثق والوصية والعهد هنا مضاف إلى الفاعل

BURSEVI:v1p91/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r4.claim: God fulfills their covenant by completing their reward through gracious acceptance and entry into Paradise; His covenant with them was established through proofs, messengers, revelation, and promised recompense for good works.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r4.anchor: أتمم جزاءكم بحسن الإثابة والقبول ودخول الجنة والعهد يضاف إلى المعاهد

BURSEVI:v1p91/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r5.claim: The first human fulfillment is uttering the two testimonies, and God's first fulfillment is protecting life and property; the highest human fulfillment is absorption in unity, answered by God's everlasting encounter.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r5.anchor: وأول مراتب الوفاء منا هو الإتيان بكلمتي الشهادة ومن الله حقن المال والدم

BURSEVI:v1p91/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r6.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v1p91/r6.claim: Al-Qushayri reads fulfilling the covenant as keeping it in the realm of veiling, while God's fulfillment brings nearness, intimacy, and vision in the realm of union.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r6.anchor: كما قال القشيري {وأوفوا بعهدى} في دار الحجبة {أوف بعهدكم} في دار القربة

BURSEVI:v1p91/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r7.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v1p91/r7.claim: Al-Qushayri also hears the worshipper say continually, My Lord, and God answer continually, My servant.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r7.anchor: وأوفوا بعهدي بقولكم أبدا ربي ربي أوف بعهدكم بجوابكم أبدا عبدي عبدي

BURSEVI:v1p91/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r8.claim: The object-fronted phrase means fear Me: the verb's object is already supplied, the final ya is dropped for ease and rhyme, and the conditional fa implies that if anyone is feared, God alone is to be feared.

BURSEVI:v1p91/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p91/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p91/r9.claim: Fear includes guarding oneself; the verse combines promise and warning, requires gratitude and covenant fidelity, and teaches believers to fear God alone through the exclusive fronting of Me.
BURSEVI:v1p91/r9.anchor: والرهبة خوف معه تحرز والآية متضمنة

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r1.claim: Israel is Jacob's epithet; the author records several readings of the name and reports Hebrew meanings including God's chosen one or servant of God.

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r2.claim: The name Israel is said in Hebrew to mean God's chosen one or servant of God.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r2.anchor: İbranî’de bunun mânası safvetullah veya abdullah demek olduğu beyan olunuyor.

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r3.claim: Addressing the Jews as descendants of a chosen servant of God is meant to spur the people of Torah to believe.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r3.anchor: Allah’ın güzide bir kuluna evlâdlıkla muzâf olan ehl-i Tevrât!

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r4.claim: Remembering God's blessing includes recollection in the heart and on the tongue; the Israelites sought blessings yet had forgotten even the blessing itself.

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r5.claim: The foremost blessing is guidance through scripture and prophethood, culminating in awareness of Muhammad's mission and the divine guidance brought by the Hijra to Medina.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r5.anchor: bunlardan başlıcası فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى mazmûnunca kitap ve nübüvvete işarettir

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r6.claim: The covenant made since Adam's descent and confirmed through the Torah required following, believing, and obeying the source of guidance God would send, especially the final Prophet Moses foretold.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r6.anchor: Mûsâ’nın haber verdiği Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ’ya iman edecektiniz.

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r7.claim: Following Muhammad fulfills God's covenant, and God in turn fulfills theirs by admitting them among those without fear or grief.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r7.anchor: Resûlüm Muhammed’e ittibâ‘ile îfa ediniz ki

ELMALILI:2:40-46/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r11.claim: The command to fear God alone in verse 40 addresses common people and elites, while verse 41's command to take refuge in God is directed particularly to elites.
ELMALILI:2:40-46/r11.anchor: onun avam ve havâssa umûmî ve bunun havâssa husûsî bir hitâbı istihdaf etmesi

ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r15.claim: This address recalls Israel's past blessings and deprivation, summons them to Islam, promises a more glorious future if they accept, and warns of dire consequences if they refuse and pursue petty gains.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#3/r15.anchor: Benî İsrâil’i yâd-ı ni‘metle İslâm’a davet eden bu hitâbı takviye ve teyid etmek, diğer taraftan da mâzîde nâil oldukları nimetleri ihtar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r1.claim: After the opening discussion of polytheists and hypocrites, the surah turns through verse 123 mainly to Israelite history, religious and moral decline, and their attitude toward Islam, while touching other topics too.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r1.anchor: Sûrenin buraya kadar olan bölümünde müşrikler ve münafıklar hakkında açıklamalar yapılıp uyarılarda bulunulduktan sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r2.claim: Because many Arabian Jews lived in and around Medina, al-Baqara, the first long Medinan surah, calls them to Islam, proves Islam's truth, and explains their religion and ancestors' history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r2.anchor: Arap yarımadasındaki yahudilerin önemli bir kısmı Medine ve civarında yaşadığı için Medine’de inen uzun sûrelerin ilki olan Bakara sûresinde Allah onları İslâm’a davet etmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r3.claim: Judaism is the oldest pre-Islamic revealed religion whose law and scripture remain, though altered; its character as a law-based religion, unlike Christianity, increases its importance in the Qur'an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r3.anchor: Yahudilik, İslâm’dan önceki semavî dinler arasında –tahrife uğramış da olsa– şeriatı ve kutsal kitabı halen yaşamakta olan en eski dindir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r4.claim: Jewish migration from Palestine from the first century under Roman pressure and their relations with Muslims also explain the Qur'an's attention to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r4.anchor: Romalılar’ın baskısı sebebiyle milâdî I. yüzyıldan itibaren Filistin’den buralara göç etmiş olan geniş bir yahudi topluluğu yaşamakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r5.claim: Moses is named 136 times in 34 surahs; several surahs give detailed accounts of his teaching and mission and the hostile responses of Israelites, Pharaoh, Korah, and Haman.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r5.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın ismi otuz dört sûrede 136 defa anılmış;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r6.claim: Israel occurs twice as the name of Jacob, grandson of Abraham through Isaac, and forty times as the designation Children of Israel for Jews.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r6.anchor: İsrâil kelimesi iki âyette (Âl-i İmrân 3/93; Meryem 19/58) Hz. İbrâhim’in Hz. İshak’tan torunu olan Hz. Ya‘kub’un ismi olarak geçmekte;

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r7.claim: The word's etymology and original meaning are uncertain, though “strengthened by God” is judged highly probable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r7.anchor: Kelimenin etimolojisinin ve asıl anlamının belirsiz olduğu ileri sürülmekle birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r8.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r8.claim: Tabari's history explains Israel as “one who goes to God at night.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r8.anchor: Taberî’nin Tarîhu’l-ümem ve’l- mülûk’ünde (I, 192) İsrâil kelimesinin “gece vakti Allah’a giden” anlamına geldiği ifade edilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r9.claim: Other cited accounts give Hebrew meanings including “God's sword,” “one striving in God's path,” “a person chosen by God,” and “God's servant.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r9.anchor: Aynı ismin İbrânîce’de “Allah’ın kılıcı”, “Allah yolunda cihad eden”, “Allah’ın seçkin kıldığı insan” veya “Allah’ın kulu” anlamına geldiği de bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r10.claim: The twelve Jewish tribes were called Israel; after Solomon their name designated the northern kingdom, then came to denote Jews as an entire ethnic group.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r10.anchor: On iki yahudi kabilesi de İsrâil adıyla anılır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r11.claim: In Jewish belief God gave Jacob the name Israel; Judaism is viewed as a national religion, Yahova as a national god, and Israelites as a chosen people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r11.anchor: Yahudi inancına göre Hz. Ya‘kub’a İsrâil ismi Tanrı tarafından verilmiştir; Yahudilik millî bir din, Yahova da millî bir tanrı kabul edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r12.claim: The people were called Hebrews before settling Palestine, Israelites there, and Children of Israel after exile; Hebrew and Jew were also common names.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r12.anchor: Filistin’e yerleşmeden önce İbrânî, Filistin’de İsrâilî, sürgünden sonra ise İsrâiloğulları diye anılmaktaydı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r13.claim: This is the Qur'an's first mention of Children of Israel; the address targets Jews of Muhammad's time, especially religious scholars, and recalls a favor they already knew, so it is not specified.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r13.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de Benî İsrâil isminin ilk defa geçtiği konumuz olan âyette özellikle, başta din bilginleri olmak üzere, Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki yahudilere hitap edilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r14.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r14.claim: Tabari identifies the favor as God's sending Israelite prophets and scriptures, saving them from Pharaoh and his oppressive people, and settling them in the holy land; others add further favors.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r14.anchor: Taberî bu nimeti, Allah Teâlâ’nın geçmişte İsrâiloğulları arasından peygamberler göndermesi, onlara kitaplar indirmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r15.claim: Recalling these favors is meant to remind the Israelites of their duty to give thanks.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r15.anchor: Bu nimetleri anmaktan maksat, onlara şükretme görevlerini hatırlatmaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r16.claim: ʿAhd can mean requiring fulfillment, promising, agreement, contract, or a covenant; in the Qur'an it can describe promises between people or a compact between God and servants, and can also imply oath or time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r16.anchor: Bir şeyin yerine getirilmesini emretmek, söz vermek” veya “ittifak, anlaşma, sözleşme” gibi mânalara gelen ahid kelimesi Kur’an’da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r17.claim: The Qur'an also uses mīthāq and waʿd for related meanings; the Old and New Testaments are named covenants because they contain divinely set duties and accounts of covenants with prophets and communities, including Israel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r17.anchor: Kur’an’da yer yer aynı anlamda mîsâk, vaad gibi başka kelimelerin kullanıldığı da görülür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r18.claim: The Qur'an says God took Israel's pledges to hold fast to the Torah, pray, give zakat, believe in prophets, lend to the needy for God's sake, and not conceal but recite scripture.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r18.anchor: Allah’ın İsrâiloğulları’ndan değişik konularda, meselâ Tevrat’a sımsıkı sarılacaklarına (Bakara 2/63), namazı kılacaklarına, zekâtı vereceklerine, peygamberlere inanacaklarına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r19.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r19.claim: Most exegetes understand the covenant in this verse in a general sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r19.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğu konumuz olan âyetteki ahdi genel anlamda yorumlamışlardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r20.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r20.claim: Tabari specifically takes the covenant as Israel's pledge to recognize Muhammad's prophethood, already described in their scriptures, believe him, and disclose this truth to others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r20.anchor: Taberî ise buradaki ahdi, özellikle Allah’ın yahudilere, onların kutsal kitaplarında kendisi hakkında bilgi verilmiş bulunan Hz. Muhammed’in peygamberliğini tanıyıp ona inanmalarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r21.speaker: Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r21.claim: The author finds al-Manar's account more plausible: Israel pledged to worship God alone, believe messengers who brought proof, submit to divine rulings, and especially believe Muhammad, a descendant of Ishmael; the pledge also includes humanity's natural duty to reason and act responsibly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r21.anchor: Ancak bu ahid hakkında el-Menâr’da (Reşîd Rızâ, I, 290) verilen bilgiler daha mâkul görünmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r22.claim: Most commentaries explain God's promised return as help, reward for good deeds, and admission to paradise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:40/r22.anchor: Âyetin, “Ben de size vaad ettiklerimi vereyim” kısmındaki vaad ise tefsirlerin çoğunda

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r1.claim: Arabic usage can mix morphological patterns even within native vocabulary; Ruʾba, Labīd, and ʿAlqama provide examples of such irregular forms.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r1.anchor: وإذا جاز للعرب أن تخلط في العربي وهو من لغتها، فكيف يكون -ليت شعري- فيما ليس من لغتها؟!

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r2.speaker: الزهري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم with the doubled form.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الزهري: "وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم"3 مشددة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r3.claim: The doubled فعل form is more emphatic than أفعل, so the reading promises abundant fulfillment for a little given, like the tenfold reward for a good deed.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r3.anchor: لأن فعلت أبلغ من أفعلت؛ فيكون على "أوفوا بعهدي" أبالغ في توفيتكم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r4.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads يذبحون أبناءكم with the light form.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن محيصن: "يذبحون أبناءكم"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r5.claim: The light فعل form can convey repeated action because a verb carries its verbal noun’s generic breadth; examples show that singular forms can express many instances of a kind.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p80/r5.anchor: وجه ذلك أن فعلت بالتخفيف قد يكون فيه معنى التكثير؛ وذلك لدلالة الفعل على مصدره، والمصدر اسم الجنس

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r1.claim: Mujahid lists the moved yāʾs at each surah's end to make the reading rule easier for readers unfamiliar with it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r1.anchor: وقد بينت في آخر كل سورة ما حرك فيها ليقرب مأخذه على من لم تكن قراءته عادته

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r2.claim: The yāʾ is not vowelled before a following alif with ḍamma; Mujahid illustrates this with examples from al-Araf and al-Maida.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r2.anchor: ولا يحرك الياء التي ذكرت لك عند الألف المضمومة كقوله ﴿ عذابي أصيب به ﴾ الأعراف 156

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r5.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r5.claim: Nafi generally vowels an added yāʾ after kasra before alifs of any vowel or alif waṣl, except for specified forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r5.anchor: وكان نافع يحرك ياء الإضافة المكسور ما قبلها عند الألف المكسورة والمفتوحة والمضمومة وألف الوصل إلا في حروف قد ذكرتها لك

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r9.speaker: ابن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r9.claim: They leave the yāʾ unvowelled before a separate alif with a non-jussive verb, including بعهدي أوف, أني أوفي الكيل, and في ذريتي إني.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r9.anchor: ومما لم يحرك ياءه عند الألف المقطوعة وهو مع فعل غير مجزوم فيما ذكر ابن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر قوله ﴿ بعهدي أوف ﴾ البقرة 40

QIRAAT-ER:2:40:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:3#1/r1.claim: Isrāʾīla has a variant treatment of hamza among the ten canonical readings; no semantic difference is stated.
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:3#1/r1.anchor: Hamza treatment variant within ten canonical readings

QIRAAT-ER:2:40:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:19#1/r1.claim: Some ten-reader traditions retain the yāʾ of the object pronoun in the full form fa-rhabūnī.
QIRAAT-ER:2:40:19#1/r1.anchor: Yāʾ retained (full form) — some ten-reader traditions preserve the object pronoun yāʾ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r1.claim: The final radical of ibn is deleted, and scholars dispute its underlying letter and morphological pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r1.anchor: ابن: محذوف اللام، وقيل: الياء خلاف، وفي وزنه على كلا التقديرين خلاف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r2.claim: Those deriving ibn from yāʾ connect it to building: a son is a branch set upon his father; they treat banūwa as anomalous like fatūwa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r2.anchor: فمن زعم أن أصله ياء جعله مشتقا من البناء، وهو وضع الشيء على الشيء. والابن فرع عن الأب، فهو موضوع عليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash derives the word from wāw, citing banūwa and the greater frequency of deleted wāw as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r3.anchor: ومن زعم أن أصله واو، وإليه ذهب الأخفش، جعل البنوة دليلا على ذلك، ولكون اللام المحذوفة واوا أكثر منها ياء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r4.claim: The broken plural is abnāʾ, while banūn is an irregular sound plural because it does not preserve the singular form; Arabic sometimes treats it like a broken plural in verb agreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r4.anchor: وجمع ابن جمع تكسير، فقالوا: أبناء، وجمع سلامة، فقالوا: بنون، وهو جمع شاذ، إذ لم يسلم فيه بناء الواحد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r5.speaker: النابغة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r5.claim: Al-Nābigha's line uses a feminine verb with Banū ʿĀmir, illustrating the plural's treatment like a broken plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r5.anchor: قال النابغة: قالت بنو عامر خالو بني أسد ... يا بؤس للجهل ضرارا لأقوام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r6.speaker: يسدد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r6.claim: A diminutive plural ending in wāw and nūn is also attested, though Abū Ḥayyān calls it irregular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r6.anchor: وقد سمع الجمع بالواو والنون فيه مصغرا، قال يسدد: أبينوها الأصاغر خلتي وهو شاذ أيضا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r7.claim: Israel is a foreign proper name and is indeclinable because of proper-name status and foreign origin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r7.anchor: إسرائيل: اسم عجمي ممنوع الصرف للعلمية والعجمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r8.claim: One etymology makes Israel a Hebrew compound meaning servant of God, with Isra meaning servant and Il a divine name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r8.anchor: فكأنه عبد الله، وذلك باللسان العبراني، فيكون مثل: جبرائيل، وميكائيل، وإسرافيل، وعزرائيل، قاله ابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r9.claim: A second etymology takes Isra as chosen and Il as God, yielding God's chosen one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r9.anchor: معنى إسرا: صفوة، وإيل: الله تعالى، فمعناه: صفوة الله. روي ذلك عن ابن عباس وغيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r10.claim: Another account derives Isra from binding or fastening and understands Israel as one whom God firmly formed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إسرا مشتق من الأسر، وهو الشد، فكأن إسرائيل معناه: الذي شده الله وأتقن خلقه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r11.claim: Another explanation says he was named Israel because he traveled by night as a migrant to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: أسرى بالليل مهاجرا إلى الله تعالى فسمي بذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r12.speaker: كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r12.claim: Kaʿb reports that Jacob captured a jinn named Il who extinguished the Temple lamps; Jacob served the Temple, entering first and leaving last.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r12.anchor: وكان أول من يدخل، وآخر من يخرج، قاله كعب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r13.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r13.claim: A long account says Jacob was called Israel after traveling by night while fleeing his brother Esau to his maternal uncle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: أسرى بالليل هاربا من أخيه عيصو إلى خاله، في حكاية طويلة ذكروها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān judges the foregoing popular etymologies of Israel to be weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r14.anchor: وهذه أقاويل ضعاف، وفيه تصرفات للعرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r15.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r15.claim: The majority read Israel with a hamza after the alif and a yāʾ after it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r15.anchor: إسرائيل بهمزة بعد الألف وياء بعدها، وهي قراءة الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r16.speaker: أبو جعفر والأعشى وعيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r16.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the form with two yāʾs after the alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r16.anchor: وإسراييل بياءين بعد الألف، وهي قراءة أبي جعفر والأعشى وعيسى بن عمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r17.speaker: ورش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r17.claim: A reading attributed to Warsh uses a hamza after the alif followed by lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r17.anchor: وإسرائيل بهمزة بعد الألف ثم لام، وهو مروي عن ورش.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r18.claim: Other transmitted forms include Israel with an open or kasra hamza after rāʾ, and Isrāl with either imāla or no imāla and a light lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p277#2/r18.anchor: وإسراءل بهمزة مفتوحة بعد الراء ولام، وإسرئل بهمزة مكسورة بعد الراء، وإسرال بألف ممالة بعدها لام خفيفة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r1.speaker: أمية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r1.claim: Umayya's verse uses the form Isrālā, witnessing the variant pronunciation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r1.anchor: لا أرى من يعيشني في حياتي ... غير نفسي إلا بني إسرالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r2.speaker: خارجة عن نافع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r2.claim: A form Isrāl is reported from Khārija from Nāfiʿ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r3.speaker: الحسن والزهري وابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and others read Isrāʾīn, replacing lām with nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري وابن أبي إسحاق وغيرهم: وإسرائين بنون بدل اللام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r4.claim: A poet's line uses Isrāʾīnā, providing an example of the nūn variant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: يقول أهل السوء لما جينا ... هذا ورب البيت إسرائينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r5.claim: The lām-to-nūn exchange has parallels such as Sijjīl/Sijjīn, Rifl/Rifn, and Jibrīl/Jibrīn, while nūn also alternates with lām in Aṣīlān/Aṣīlāl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r5.anchor: كما قالوا: سجيل، وسجين، ورفل، ورفن، وجبريل، وجبرين، أبدلت بالنون كما أبدلت النون بها في أصيلان قالوا: أصيلال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r6.claim: Israel has broken plurals Asārīl, Asārila, and Asāril.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r6.anchor: وإذا جمعته جمع تكسير قلت: أساريل، وحكي: أسارلة وأسارل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r7.claim: Dhikr with kasra and ḍamma are both used with the same basic meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r7.anchor: الذكر: بكسر الذال وضمها لغتان بمعنى واحد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r8.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes tongue-based dhikr with kasra, opposed to silence, from heart-based dhikr with ḍamma, opposed to forgetfulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي: يكون باللسان، والذكر بالقلب فبالكسر ضده: الصمت، وبالضم ضده: النسيان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r9.claim: Niʿma names the thing bestowed; many verbal nouns can name the object acted upon, but this usage is not productive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r9.anchor: النعمة: اسم للشيء المنعم به، وكثيرا ما يجيء فعل بمعنى المفعول: كالذبح، والنقض، والرعي، والطحن، ومع ذلك لا ينقاس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r10.claim: Awfā, wafā, and waffā are three verbs with the same meaning, though awfā can also mean to rise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r10.anchor: أوفى، ووفى، ووفى: لغى ثلاث في معنى واحد، وتأتي أوفى بمعنى: ارتفع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r11.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r11.claim: The cited line uses awfaytu to mean ascending to a height.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r11.anchor: قال: ربما أوفيت في علم ... ترفعن ثوبي شمالات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r12.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r12.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports that the Hijaz says awfaytu and Najd says wafaytu without an alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: أهل الحجاز يقولون: أوفيت، وأهل نجد يقولون: وفيت بغير ألف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r13.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj accepts both wafā bi-l-ʿahd and awfā bihi for fulfilling a covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r13.anchor: وقال الزجاج: وفى بالعهد، وأوفى به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r14.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r14.claim: The cited poet uses awfā in the sense of keeping a pledge, alongside wafā for the camel-driver completing his duty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r14.anchor: قال الشاعر: أما ابن طوق فقد أوفى بذمته ... كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba allows wafaytu bi-l-ʿahd, awfaytu bihi, and only awfaytu al-kayl with a direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r15.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: يقال وفيت بالعهد، وأوفيت به، وأوفيت الكيل لا غير.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r16.speaker: أبو الهيثم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r16.claim: Abū al-Haytham says wafā means completion; wafā or awfā the measure means to complete it, and wāfin means complete.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r16.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم. وفى الشيء: تم، ووفى الكيل وأوفيته: أتممته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r17.claim: Rahb, ruhb, rahab, and rahba mean fear; rahba is associated with the breastbone affected by fear, and rahb can mean a spearhead because it inspires fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r17.anchor: الرهب، والرهب، والرهب، والرهبة: الخوف، مأخوذ من الرهابة، وهو عظم الصدر يؤثر فيه الخوف. والرهب: النصل، لأنه يرهب منه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p278/r18.claim: Rahba, khashya, and makhāfa are near-synonyms.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r2.claim: The address to the Children of Israel begins a distinct address to Jews and Christians after the surah has introduced the Book, disbelievers, hypocrites, general worship, the Qurʾān's inimitability, and Adam's story.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r2.anchor: يا بني إسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم هذا افتتاح الكلام مع اليهود والنصارى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r3.claim: Jews and Christians are singled out here because they are People of Scripture who profess following messengers and earlier revelation; the address follows the general call to worship and earlier discussion of polytheists and hypocrites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r3.anchor: وكانت هاتان الطائفتان: أعني اليهود والنصارى، أهل كتاب، مظهرين اتباع الرسل والاقتداء بما جاء عن الله تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r4.claim: Their Adam narrative is apt because Torah and Gospel gave them clear evidence to fulfill the covenant and believe in the Qurʾān, yet they did the opposite by rejecting it and its messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r4.anchor: وناسب الكلام معهم قصة آدم، على نبينا وعليه الصلاة والسلام، لأنهم بعد ما أوتوا من البيان الواضح والدليل اللائح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r5.claim: The vocative is meant to stir them to hear the ensuing commands and prohibitions, as in the earlier addresses to all people and to Adam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r5.anchor: وأقبل عليهم بالنداء ليحركهم لسماع ما يرد عليهم من الأوامر والنواهي، نحو قوله: يا أيها الناس اعبدوا، ويا آدم اسكن .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r6.claim: Calling them descendants of Israel (Jacob) rather than Jacob's children invokes the best senses of Israel, God's servant or chosen one, to urge them to emulate a righteous ancestor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r6.anchor: وأضافهم إلى لفظ إسرائيل، وهو يعقوب، ولم يقل: يا بني يعقوب، لما في لفظ إسرائيل من أن معناه عبد الله أو صفوة الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r7.claim: People naturally love to follow their ancestors, even when that is not praiseworthy; the cited ancestral-tradition verses illustrate the tendency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r7.anchor: لأن الإنسان يحب أن يقتفي أثر آبائه، وإن لم يكن بذلك محمودا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r8.claim: Bani Israel shows that someone may be called a child of a distant ancestor through many intermediaries, as with Bani Adam and Abraham being called their father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r8.anchor: وفي قوله: يا بني إسرائيل دليل على أن من انتمى إلى شخص، ولو بوسائط كثيرة، يطلق عليه أنه ابنه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r9.claim: The lineage title honors them through Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, the Friend of the Merciful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r9.anchor: وفي إضافتهم إلى إسرائيل تشريف لهم بذكر نسبتهم لهذا الأصل الطيب، وهو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r10.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r10.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī reports that no prophet other than Muḥammad had two names except Jacob, who is also Israel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r10.anchor: ونقل عن أبي الفرج بن الجوزي: أنه ليس لأحد من الأنبياء غير نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم اسمان إلا يعقوب، فإنه يعقوب، وهو إسرائيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r11.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r11.claim: Al-Jawharī says al-Masīḥ is a proper name for Jesus and has no derivation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r11.anchor: ونقل الجوهري في صحاحه: أن المسيح اسم علم لعيسى، لا اشتقاق له.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r12.speaker: البيهقي عن الخليل بن أحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r12.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from al-Khalīl five prophets with two names: Muḥammad/Aḥmad, ʿĪsā/al-Masīḥ, Israel/Yaʿqūb, Yūnus/Dhū al-Nūn, and Ilyās/Dhū al-Kifl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p280/r12.anchor: وذكر البيهقي عن الخليل بن أحمد خمسة من الأنبياء ذو واسمين: محمد وأحمد نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم، وعيسى والمسيح، وإسرائيل ويعقوب، ويونس وذو النون، وإلياس وذو الكفل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r1.claim: Favors given to Israel's ancestors also benefit their descendants by producing their lineage, and descent from honored ancestors is itself an honor for children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r1.anchor: وهذه النعم، وإن كانت على آبائهم، فهي أيضا نعم عليهم، لأن هذه النعم حصل بها النسل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r2.speaker: عارف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r2.claim: A gnostic says many serve the favors they receive, but few serve the Benefactor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r2.anchor: قال بعض العارفين: عبيد النعم كثيرون، وعبيد المنعم قليلون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r3.claim: The passage's contrast suggests the superiority of Muḥammad's community: God names Himself as Benefactor and says He remembers those who remember Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r3.anchor: ولما آل الأمر إلى أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر المنعم فقال: فاذكروني أذكركم ، فدل ذلك على فضل أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r4.claim: The wording niʿmatī uses a rhetorical shift from the plural first-person expression in bi-āyātinā to the singular first person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: نعمتي، نوع التفات، لأنه خروج من ضمير المتكلم المعظم نفسه في قوله: بآياتنا إلى ضمير المتكلم الذي لا يشعر بذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r5.claim: Attributing the favor directly to God signals its great worth, breadth of beneficence, and good effect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r5.anchor: وفي إضافة النعمة إليه إشارة إلى عظم قدرها وسعة برها وحسن موقعها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r6.claim: The yāʾ in niʿmatī can be vowelless or carry fatḥa, but all seven canonical readers use fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r6.anchor: ويجوز في الياء من نعمتي الإسكان والفتح، والقراء السبعة متفقون على الفتح.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r7.claim: Anʿamta is the relative clause of allatī, with an omitted resumptive pronoun: the favor that I bestowed it upon you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r7.anchor: وأنعمت: صلة التي، والعائد محذوف، التقدير: أنعمتها عليكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r8.claim: The covenant was previously discussed linguistically in the verse about those who break God's covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r8.anchor: العهد: تقدم تفسيره لغة في قوله: الذين ينقضون عهد الله ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r9.claim: The annexation of covenant may refer either to the party making the covenant or to the party with whom it is made.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r9.anchor: ويحتمل العهد أن يكون مضافا إلى المعاهد وإلى المعاهد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r10.claim: One interpretation makes God's covenant the pledge to believe in Him and His messengers, and Israel's covenant the promised Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r10.anchor: أحدها: الميثاق الذي أخذه عليهم من الإيمان به والتصديق برسله، وعهدهم ما وعدهم به من الجنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets God's covenant as what He commanded and Israel's covenant as what He promised them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r11.anchor: الثاني: ما أمرهم به وعهدهم ما وعدهم به، قاله ابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r12.claim: A report from Abū Ṣāliḥ on Ibn ʿAbbās reads God's covenant as the Torah's description of the Messenger and Israel's as the promised Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r12.anchor: ما ذكر لهم في التوراة من صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وعهدهم ما وعدهم به من الجنة، رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r13.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r13.claim: Another view takes God's covenant as performing the obligations and Israel's as their acceptance and reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r13.anchor: الرابع: أداء الفرائض وعهدهم قبولها والمجازاة عليها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r14.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r14.claim: Another view takes God's covenant as avoiding major sins and Israel's as forgiveness of minor sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r14.anchor: الخامس: ترك الكبائر وعهدهم غفران الصغائر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r15.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r15.claim: Another interpretation pairs reforming religion with God's promised reform of the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r15.anchor: السادس: إصلاح الدين وعهدهم إصلاح آخرتهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r16.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r16.claim: Another interpretation pairs striving against the self with God's promised assistance in that effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r16.anchor: السابع: مجاهدة النفوس وعهدهم المعونة على ذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r17.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r17.claim: Another interpretation pairs reform of inward secrets with God's reform of outward conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r17.anchor: الثامن: إصلاح السرائر وعهدهم إصلاح الظواهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r18.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the covenant as the command to take what God gave them with strength.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r18.anchor:
التاسع: خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة»
، قاله الحسن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r19.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r19.claim: Another interpretation invokes God's covenant with the People of Scripture to explain the revelation clearly and not conceal it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r19.anchor: العاشر: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r20.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r20.claim: Another interpretation takes God's covenant as sincerity in worship and Israel's as being brought to the stations of divine care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p282/r20.anchor: الحادي عشر: الإخلاص في العبادات وعهدهم إيصالهم إلى منازل الرعايات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r1.claim: Another interpretation takes God's covenant as belief in and obedience to the Messenger, and Israel's as the promised good reward for good deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r1.anchor: الإيمان به وطاعته، وعهدهم ما وعدهم عليه من حسن الثواب على الحسنات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r2.claim: Another interpretation pairs preserving outward manners with God's preservation of inward secrets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r2.anchor: الثالث عشر: حفظ آداب الظواهر وعهدهم في السرائر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī reports God's pledge through Moses to send a prophet from Ishmael's descendants; those who follow him and believe his light receive forgiveness, Paradise, and double reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r3.anchor: غفرت له وأدخلته الجنة وجعلت له أجرين اثنين، قاله الكلبي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r4.claim: Another interpretation pairs the condition of servitude with God's condition of lordship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r4.anchor: الخامس عشر: شرط العبودية وعهدهم شرط الربوبية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r5.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r5.claim: Al-Thawrī depicts keeping God's inviolability in the testing abode through service, answered by nearness and vision in the abode of blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r5.anchor: أوفوا في دار محنتي على بساط خدمتي بحفظ حرمتي، أوف بعهدكم في دار نعمتي على بساط كرامتي بقربي ورؤيتي، قاله الثوري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r6.speaker: إسماعيل بن زياد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r6.claim: Ismāʿīl ibn Ziyād interprets God's covenant as not fleeing battle, with Paradise as its reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r6.anchor: لا تفروا من الزحف أدخلكم الجنة، قاله إسماعيل بن زياد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj links the covenant to God's covenant with Israel and His sending a messenger, with Paradise as Israel's covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r7.anchor: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا الآية، قاله ابن جريج، وعهدهم إدخالهم الجنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r8.claim: The majority take God's covenant as His commands, prohibitions, and injunctions, including mention of Muḥammad in the Torah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r8.anchor: أوامره ونواهيه ووصاياه، فيدخل في ذلك ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي في التوراة، قاله الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r9.speaker: أبو عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r9.claim: Abū ʿUthmān reads the covenant as reliance on God and God's response as meeting people's pressing needs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r9.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في التوكل أوف بعهدكم في كفاية المهمات، قاله أبو عثمان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r10.claim: Another interpretation pairs keeping God's limits outwardly and inwardly with His guarding their secrets from awareness of anyone else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r10.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في حفظ حدودي ظاهرا وباطنا أوف بعهدكم بحفظ أسراركم عن مشاهدة غيري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r11.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r11.claim: Al-Qushayrī interprets God's covenant as preserving direct knowledge of Him and the reciprocal covenant as conveying that knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r11.anchor: عهده حفظ المعرفة وعهدنا إيصال المعرفة، قاله القشيري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r12.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r12.claim: Another interpretation pairs fulfilling the covenant accepted on the day of the primordial pledge with God's promised fulfillment on the day of encounter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r12.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي الذي قبلتم يوم أخذ الميثاق أوف بعهدكم الذي ضمنت لكم يوم التلاق.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r13.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r13.claim: Another interpretation reads God's covenant as being content with Him alone and His as being pleased with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r13.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي اكتفوا مني بي أوف بعهدكم أرض عنكم بكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the broad sense: fulfill what you committed to God, and He will fulfill His promise reciprocally, presenting His grace as a pledged obligation to motivate fidelity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r14.anchor: والذي يظهر، والله أعلم، أن المعنى طلب الإيفاء بما التزموه لله تعالى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r15.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r15.claim: The Prophet says that a person has a covenant with God that He will admit him to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283/r15.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فإن له عهدا عند الله أن يدخله الجنة» .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r1.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r1.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads awfū bi-ʿahdikum with shadda; the doubled form may intensify the promise or simply equal the unaugmented form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: أوف بعهدكم مشددا. ويحتمل أن يراد به التكثير، وأن يكون موافقا للمجرد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r2.claim: If the doubled reading is intensive, it emphasizes God giving much in return for little, as in the tenfold reward for a good deed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r2.anchor: فإن أريد به التكثير فيكون في ذلك مبالغة على لفظ أوف، وكأنه قيل: أبالغ في إيفائكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن بن خروف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r3.claim: One grammatical account says the imperative clause itself includes a conditional sense, so a following jussive is licensed without an omitted conditional clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r3.anchor: فذهب بعضهم إلى أن جملة الأمر ضمنت معنى الشرط، فإذا قلت: اضرب زيدا يغضب، ضمن اضرب معنى: إن تضرب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r4.speaker: الفارسي والسيرافي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r4.claim: Another account says the imperative replaces an omitted conditional clause; the implied condition is the true governor, and al-Fārisī and al-Sīrāfī adopt this analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن جملة الأمر نابت مناب الشرط، ومعنى النيابة أنه كان التقدير: اضرب زيدا، إن تضرب زيدا يغضب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه عن الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r5.claim: Sibawayhi, citing al-Khalīl, explicitly states that the true governor on the second analysis is the implied conditional clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحقيقة، العمل إنما هو للشرط المقدر، وهو اختيار الفارسي والسيرافي، وهو الذي نص عليه سيبويه عن الخليل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r6.claim: The detached object pronoun iyyāya is governed by an omitted imperative, with al-Sajawandī instead estimating an imperative after it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r6.anchor: إياي: منصوب بفعل محذوف مقدرا بعده لانفصال الضمير، وإياي ارهبوا، وحذف لدلالة ما بعده عليه وتقديره قبله، وهم من السجاوندي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r7.claim: Using an accusative pronoun suits the preceding command and adds emphasis by casting the expression as two clauses; nominative would lose both effects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r7.anchor: وفي مجيئه ضمير نصب مناسبة لما قبله، لأن قبله أمر، ولأن فيه تأكيدا، إذ الكلام مفروغ في قالب جملتين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r8.claim: The yāʾ suffix is omitted in fārhabūn as a verse-ending form, while Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads it with yāʾ according to the underlying form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r8.anchor: وحذفت الياء ضمير النصب من فارهبون لأنها فاصلة، وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق بالياء على الأصل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says iyyāya fārhabūn signals restriction more strongly than iyyāka naʿbudu because the first is two clauses by estimation and the second one clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهو أوكد في إفادة الاختصاص من إياك نعبد. ومعنى ذلك أن الكلام جملتان في التقدير، وإياك نعبد، جملة واحدة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's stated basis because he does not accept that fronting the object alone yields restriction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p283#2/r10.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام معه في ذلك، وأنا لا نذهب إلى ما ذهب إليه من ذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r1.speaker: ابن خروف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r1.claim: Ibn Khurūf treats every man who comes to you, so strike him as equivalent to Zayd, so strike him; the verbal description of an indefinite noun supplies a conditional sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r1.anchor: يأتيك فاضرب، بمنزلة زيدا فاضرب، إلا أن هنا معنى الشرط لأجل النكرة الموصوفة بالفعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says he cannot see Ibn Khurūf's explanation beyond its claim that the construction is preferable, and cites the Qurʾānic and poetic pattern with an initial object and fāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r2.anchor: ولا يظهر لي وجه إلا حسنية التي أشار إليها ابن خروف، والذي يدل على أن هذا التركيب، أعني: زيدا فاضرب، تركيب عربي صحيح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r3.claim: The cited verse-like line, 'Do not worship Satan; worship God,' is another example of an object followed by fāʾ and an imperative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ولا تعبد الشيطان والله فاعبدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r4.claim: One analysis makes the underlying order 'pay attention, then strike Zayd'; after deleting the attention command, the noun is fronted to repair the expression beginning with fāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r4.anchor: قال بعض أصحابنا: الذي ظهر فيها بعد البحث أن الأصل في: زيدا فاضرب، تنبه: فاضرب زيدا، ثم حذف تنبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r5.claim: The verse can be parsed with an implied 'fear Me; pay attention, then fear Me,' so fāʾ answers the command without being displaced by fronting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون التقدير وإياي ارهبوا، تنبهوا فارهبون، فتكون الفاء دخلت في جواب الأمر، وليست مؤخرة من تقديم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r6.claim: Alternatively, an omitted tanabbah precedes fārhabūn; when the object is fronted, the conjunction and response fāʾ meet, so fāʾ is advanced and the object is repeated for emphasis and cadence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r6.anchor: والوجه الثاني: أن يكون التقدير وتنبهوا فارهبون، ثم قدم المفعول فانفصل، وأخرت الفاء حين قدم المفعول وفعل الأمر الذي هو تنبهوا محذوف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r7.claim: On the second parse, iyyāya is governed by the spoken verb, and the detached pronoun can be reinforced by the attached pronoun, as in ḍarabtuka iyyāka.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا التقدير الأخير لا يكون إياي معمولا لفعل محذوف، بل معمولا لهذا الفعل الملفوظ به، ولا يبعد تأكيد الضمير المنفصل بالضمير المتصل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command as fear lest God inflict on them the known punishments that befell their ancestors, including metamorphosis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r8.anchor: والمعنى: ارهبون أن أنزل بكم ما أنزلت بمن كان قبلكم من آبائكم من النقمات التي قد عرفتم من المسخ وغيره، وهذا قول ابن عباس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r9.claim: Another interpretation understands 'fear Me' as a command not to break God's covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r9.anchor: وقيل معنى فارهبون: أن لا تنقضوا عهدي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r10.claim: The command to fear is a forceful warning and a genuine demand, unlike 'do whatever you will,' which is not an actual request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r10.anchor: وفي الأمر بالرهبة وعيد بالغ، وليس قول من زعم أن هذا الأمر معناه التهديد والتخويف والتهويل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r11.claim: One mystical distinction makes fear of punishment the temporary share of outward practitioners and awe of majesty the enduring share of the people of the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r11.anchor: وقيل: الخوف خوفان، خوف العقاب، وهو نصيب أهل الظاهر، ويزول، وخوف جلال، وهو نصيب أهل القلب، ولا يزول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r12.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r12.claim: Al-Sulamī defines fear as the heart's apprehension of corrupt thoughts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r12.anchor: وقال السلمي: الرهبة: خشية القلب من رديء خواطره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r13.speaker: سهل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r13.claim: Sahl reads 'fear Me' as the station of certainty through knowing God, and 'be mindful of Me' as the station of prior knowledge and of danger from divine stratagem and gradual enticement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p285/r13.anchor: وقال سهل: وإياي فارهبون، موضع اليقين بمعرفته، وإياي فاتقون، موضع العلم السابق وموضع المكر والاستدراج.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r1.claim: The passage opens with blessings and closes with submission to their giver, while the intervening duties cover belief, bodily acts, and financial acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r1.anchor: فكان افتتاح هذه الآيات بذكر النعم واختتامها بالانقياد للمنعم، وما بينهما تكاليف اعتقادية وأفعال بدنية ومالية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r2.claim: This opening, sequence, and ending illustrate God's speech's excellence over other speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r2.anchor: وبنحو ما تضمنته هذه الآيات من الافتتاح والإرداف والاختتام يظهر فضل كلام الله على سائر الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r3.claim: Although phrased specifically to Israel, these commands apply generally: every accountable person must remember God's blessing, keep the covenant, and fulfill the ensuing duties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293/r3.anchor: وإن كانت خاصة في الصورة ببني إسرائيل، فإنهم هم المخاطبون بها هي عامة في المعنى، فيجب على كل مكلف ذكر نعمة الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r1.claim: God’s covenant is preserving knowledge of Him; the servant’s covenant is receiving forgiveness.

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r2.claim: God’s covenant is guarding what He loves; its fulfillment is His subtle reward.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r2.anchor: عهده حفظ محابه وعهدنا لطف ثوابه

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r3.claim: God’s covenant is remaining present at His door, and His fulfillment is abundant return.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r3.anchor: عهده حضور الباب وعهدنا جزيل المآب

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r4.claim: Keeping the covenant means guarding the secret; God fulfills it with beautiful righteousness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r4.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بحفظ السر أوف بعهدكم بجميل البر

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r5.claim: The human pledge was accepted on the day of the primordial covenant, and God’s response is promised on the day of return.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r5.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي الذي قبلتم يوم الميثاق أوف بعهدكم الذي ضمنت لكم يوم التلاق

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r6.claim: The servant must prefer no one over God, and God will not withhold His kindness or good.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r6.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في ألا تؤثروا علي غيري أوف بعهدكم في ألا أمنع عنكم لطفي وخيري

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r7.claim: Servants keep the covenant by caring for the trusts planted within them; God fulfills it through enduring flashes of illumination.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r7.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي برعاية ما أثبت فيكم من الودائع أوف بعهدكم بما أديم لكم من شوارق اللوامع

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r8.claim: Preserving God’s secrets is answered by His beautiful recompense.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r8.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بحفظ أسراري أوف بعهدكم بجميل مباري

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r9.claim: Sustaining knowledge of God is answered by the continued renewal of His beneficence.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r9.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي باستدامة عرفاني أوف بعهدكم في إدامة إحساني

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r10.claim: Serving God is answered by His favor in accepting that service.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r10.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في القيام بخدمتي أوف بعهدكم في المنة عليكم بقبولها منكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r11.claim: Good spiritual striving and conduct are answered by lasting communion and direct witnessing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r11.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في القيام بحسن المجاهدة والمعاملة أوف بعهدكم بدوام المواصلة والمشاهدة

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r12.claim: Disclaiming one’s own power and merit is answered by God’s abundant favor and generosity.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r12.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بالتبري عن الحول والمنة أوف بعهدكم بالإكرام بالطول والمنة

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r13.claim: The covenant asks for preference and reliance; God fulfills it by sufficiency and favor.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r13.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بالتفضيل والتوكل أوف بعهدكم بالكفاية والتفضل

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r14.claim: Sincere love is answered by complete nearness to God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r14.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي بصدق المحبة أوف بعهدكم بكمال القربة

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r15.claim: Being satisfied with God alone is answered by God’s being satisfied with the servants.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r15.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي اكتفوا مني بي أوف بعهدكم أرضي بكم عنكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r16.claim: In the realm of absence, servants obey and exert themselves in service; in proximity, God grants intimacy, vision, His address, and perfect nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r16.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في دار الغيبة على بساط الخدمة

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r17.claim: Giving up desires in response to spiritual demands is met by God’s sufficing the servants in those demands.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r17.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي في المطالبات بترك الشهوات أوف بعهدكم بكفايتكم تلك المطالبات

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r18.claim: The servant continually says ‘My Lord,’ and God answers by addressing the servant as ‘My servant.’

QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r19.claim: Fear God alone, since only He has power to create; no one without power or favor is rightly feared.
QUSHAYRI:v1p41/r19.anchor: أي أفردوني بالخشية لانفرادي بالقدرة على الإيجاد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r1.claim: The address targets a particular group of unbelievers contemporary with the Prophet after a general address and proofs of God’s unity, prophethood, the afterlife, and divine favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r1.anchor: خطاب لطائفة خاصة من الكفرة المعاصرين للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بعد الخطاب العام وسقامة دلائل التوحيد والنبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r2.claim: The Israelites are addressed after Adam’s story because they had received clear proofs and calls to follow the unlettered Prophet, whom they found written about, yet turned away from faith and did not accept the revealed words; the call urges them to hear what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r2.anchor: وجعله سبحانه بعد قصة آدم لأن هؤلاء بعد ما أتوا من البيان الواضح والدليل اللائح وأمروا ونهوا وحرضوا على اتباع النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عنده

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r3.claim: Banū is the broken plural of ibn, which changes in the plural; hence its verb can take feminine singular agreement, as in the example of Banū ʿĀmir.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r3.anchor: لتغير مفرده ولذا أحلق في فعله تاء التأنيث ك قالت بنو عامر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r4.claim: The word specifically denotes male sons, but in an annexed phrase common usage includes both sons and daughters; that broader sense is intended here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r4.anchor: وهو مختص بالأولاد الذكور وإذا أضيف عم في العرف الذكور والإناث فيكون بمعنى الأولاد وهو المراد هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r5.speaker: الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r5.claim: Al-Sālikūtī says the literal sense is lineal sons, while using it for all offspring is figurative, as established in legal theory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r5.anchor: وذكر الساليكوتي أنه حقيقة في الأبناء الصلبية كما بين في الأصول واستعماله في العام مجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r6.speaker: ابن درستويه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r6.claim: Ibn Durustawayh derives ibn from a yāʾ-root connected to building: a son is a branch built upon his father, as an artifact may be attributed to its maker.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r6.anchor: فذهب إلى الأول ابن درستويه وجعله من البناء لأن الابن فرع الأب ومبنى عليه ولهذا ينسب المصنوع إلى صانعه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r7.claim: The author notes that an earlier law called some creatures God’s children metaphorically in the sense of being made by Him, but that usage was prohibited once ignorant people misconstrued it as biological generation; uttering it became unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r7.anchor: ولهذا ينسب المصنوع إلى صانعه فيقال للقصيدة مثلا : بنت الفكر وقد أطلق في شريعة من قبلنا على بعض المخلوقين أبناء الله تعالى بهذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r8.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash derives ibn from a wāw-root, citing the form banūwah and the greater frequency of deleted wāw.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r8.anchor: وذهب إلى الثاني الأخفش وأيده بأنهم قالوا : البنوة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r9.speaker: الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r9.claim: Al-Jawharī considers the yāʾ derivation likelier; al-Ālūsī agrees that banūwah does not prove wāw because fatāwah is also a yāʾ-root, and frequency is not decisive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r9.anchor: قال الجوهري : ولعل الأول أصح لا دلالة في البنوة لأنهم قالوا أيضا : الفتوة ولا خلاف في أنها من ذوات الياء وأمر الأكثرية سهل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r10.claim: Israel is a foreign name and a title of Jacob; it is said to combine īl, a divine name, with isrā, variously glossed as servant, chosen one, human being, or migrant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r10.anchor: و ( إسرائيل ) أسم أعجمي وقد ذكروا أنه مركب من إي لأسم من أسمائه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r11.claim: The majority read the name as Isrāʾīl, with hamza after the alif and then yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r11.anchor: فقد قالوا : ( إسرائيل ) بهمزة بعد الألف وياء بعدها وبه قرأ الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and others read Isrāyīl with two yāʾ letters after the alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r12.anchor: وإسراييل بياءين بعد الألف وبه قرأ أبو جعفر وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r13.speaker: ورش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r13.claim: A form written Isrāʾil without the post-alif yāʾ is transmitted from Warsh.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r13.anchor: وإسرائل ولام وهو مروى عن ورش

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r14.speaker: الحسن وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r14.claim: Other transmitted pronunciations vary the hamza after rāʾ, use a light lām, or replace the lām with nūn; al-Ḥasan and others read the final-nūn form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r14.anchor: وإسرأل بهمزة مفتوحة ومكسورة بعد الراء ولام وإسرأل بألف ممالة بعدها لام خفيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r15.claim: A cited line illustrates the form Isrāʾīnā, with nūn in place of lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p241/r15.anchor: إسرائين ) بنون بدل اللام كما في قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r1.claim: Addressing them by their ancestor’s title is meant to spur obedience: invoking a righteous father encourages more than invoking an unrelated person, and good or bad conduct carries greater weight in a prophetic family.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r1.anchor: وأضاف سبحانه هؤلاء المخاطبين إلى هذا اللقب تأكيدا لتحريكهم إلى طاعته فإن في ( إسرائيل ) ما ليس في اسمه الكريم يعقوب وقولك : يا ابن الصالح أطع الله تعالى أحث للمأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r2.claim: Dhikr with kasra or ḍamma can mean remembering by tongue or heart; al-Kisāʾī differentiates the two vowels by assigning one to the tongue and one to the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r2.anchor: أمر من الذكر بكسر الذال وضمها بمعنى واحد ويكونان باللسان والجنان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r3.claim: If dhikr covers both tongue and heart, it may be a homonym for both or one general meaning embracing both; the author considers the homonym analysis apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r3.anchor: فأما أن يكون مشتركا بينهما أو موضوعا لمعنى عام شامل لهما والظاهر هو الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r4.claim: The command aims at gratitude and fulfillment of the favors’ claims, not mere recollection in the heart or utterance by the tongue.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r4.anchor: والمقصود من الأمر بذلك الشكر على النعمة والقيام بحقوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r5.claim: Attributing the favor to God honors it and requires that gratitude be directed exclusively to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r5.anchor: وإضافة النعمة إلى ضميره تعالى لتشريفها وإيجاب تخصيص شكرها به سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r6.speaker: some verifying scholars
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r6.claim: Some scholars say the unqualified singular “My favor” is comprehensive, with no prior referent, and suits the call to faith by including universal favors and those specific to the Israelites.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r6.anchor: وقد قال بعض المحققين : إنها تفيد الاستغراق إذ لا عهد ولمناسبته بمقام الدعوة إلى الإيمان فهي شاملة للنعم العامة والخاصة بالمخاطبين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r7.claim: Saying the favor was bestowed upon them makes gratitude especially compelling, since people are naturally envious and possessive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r7.anchor: وفائدة التقييد بكونها عليهم أنها من هذه الحيثية أدعى للشكر فإن الإنسان حسود غيور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r8.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r8.claim: Qatāda says the favor includes what God bestowed on their forefathers and what He bestowed on them, especially their living in the time of the noblest Prophet and being included in his mission’s audience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة : أريد بها ما أنعم به على آبائهم مما قصه سبحانه في كتابه وعليهم من فنون النعمة التي أجلها إدراك زمن أشرف الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r9.claim: Treating ancestral favors as theirs through shared religious inheritance or inclusive reference resolves the address; there is no need to combine literal and figurative meanings as some mistakenly claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r9.anchor: ويحتاج تصحيح الخطاب حينئذ إلى اعتبار التغليب أو جعل نعم الآباء نعمهم فلا جمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز كما وهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r10.claim: The yāʾ in niʿmatī may be read with sukūn or fatḥa, though all seven canonical readers agree on fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r10.anchor: ويجوز في الياء من ( نعمتي ) الإسكان والفتح والقراء السبعة متفقون على الفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r11.claim: Anʿamtu is an adjectival clause for allatī with its object pronoun omitted, understood as anʿamtuhā.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r11.anchor: صلة ( التي ) والعائد محذوف والتقدير أنعمتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r12.claim: Awfū and its light or doubled forms can both mean fulfilling; Ibn Qutayba distinguishes them by allowing awfaytu with a covenant and with measure, but waffaytu only with a covenant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r12.anchor: وقال إبن قتيبة : يقال : أوفيت بالعهد ووفيت به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r13.claim: A line of poetry uses awfaytu to mean rising or ascending.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r13.anchor: وجاء أو فى بمعنى أرتفع كقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r14.speaker: author
