ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r14.claim: The apparent parsing makes “My covenant” a covenant initiated by God and “your covenant” one owed by Him: He commands belief and deeds through proofs and promises reward, so their fulfillment is faith and obedience and His is recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242/r14.anchor: والظاهر هنا أن الأول مضاف إلى الفاعل والثاني إلى المفعول فإنه تعالى أمرهم بالإيمان والعمل وعهد إليهم بما نصب من الحجج العقلية والنقلية الآمرة بذلك ووعدهم بحسن الثواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r1.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r1.claim: A view understood from Qatāda and Mujāhid treats both covenants as object-genitives: fulfill the faith and obedience you pledged to God, and He fulfills the promised reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r1.anchor: وقيل : وهو المفهوم من كلام قتادة ومجاهد أن كليهما مضاف إلى المفعول والمعنى أوفوا بما عاهدتموني من الإيمان والتزام الطاعة أوف بما عاهدتكم من حسن الإثابة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r2.claim: This reading is detailed by the covenant with the Children of Israel and God’s promise to admit them to gardens; it requires counting the forefathers’ covenant as that of their descendants through their shared religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r2.anchor: وتفصيل العهدين قوله تعالى : ( ولقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل ) إلى قوله سبحانه : ( ولأدخلنكم ) إلخ ويحوج هذا إلى اعتبار أن عهد الآباء عهد الأبناء لتناسبهم في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r3.claim: If īfāʾ means completing a covenant, both annexations can be object-genitives; if it means observing it, the first is subject-genitive and the second object-genitive, though the author sees a problem in this account.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن فسر الإيفاء بإتمام العهد تكون الإضافة إلى المفعول في الموضعين وإن فسر بمراعاته تكون الإضافة الأولى للفاعل والثانية للمفعول وفيه تأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r4.claim: Covenant-keeping spans ranks: outwardly, humans begin with the confession of faith and God with protection of life and property; at the highest mystical rank, humans pass beyond self-annihilation and God adorns them with the lights of names and attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r4.anchor: فأول المراتب الظاهرة منا الإتيان بكلمتي الشهادة ومنه تعالى حقن الدماء والمال وآخرها منا الفناء حتى عن الفناء ومنه تعالى التحلية بأنوار الصفات والأسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r5.claim: Reports on covenant-keeping vary in authenticity and correspond to the many intermediate ranks; a mystical scheme makes the human levels unity of acts, then attributes, then essence, while God grants each level its fitting knowledge and character.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r5.anchor: فما روى من الآثار على إختلاف أسانيدها صحة وضعفا في بيان الوفاء بالعهدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r6.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads ūfi with a doubled fāʾ; if intensive, as the author inclines to think, it signals God’s abundant generosity in giving much for little, as in the tenfold reward for a good deed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ( أوف ) بالتشديد فإن كان موافقا للمجرد فذاك وإن أريد به التكثير والقلب إليه يميل فهو إشارة إلى عظيم كرمه وإحسانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.claim: The answer verb is jussive because it follows a command, either directly or through an implied condition; al-Fārisī chooses the latter, while Sibawayh states the direct analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r7.anchor: وإنجزام الفعل لوقوعه في جواب الأمر والجزم إما به نفسه أو بشرط مقدر وهو اختيار الفارسي ونص سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.claim: Rahba means fear generally; another definition adds guarded caution, distinguishing it from taqwā, which is self-protection against what is feared. The author favors this usage distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r8.anchor: الرهبة الخوف مطلقا وقيل : مع تحرز وبه فارق الأتقاء لأنه مع حزم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.claim: The distinction assigns fear itself to ordinary people and careful guarding to spiritual leaders.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r9.anchor: ولهذا كان الأول للعامة والثاني للأئمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.claim: The command to fear is a serious warning, not an empty threat like “do what you will,” because commanded fear is genuinely desired.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r10.anchor: وفي الأمر بها وعيد بالغ وليس ذلك للتهديد والتهويل كما في ( اعملوا ما شئتم ) كما وهم لأن هذا مطلوب وذاك غير مطلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.speaker: some grammarians
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.claim: Iyyāya is an accusative detached pronoun governed by an omitted verb explained by the following verb; some parse the fa as conditional, shifted from the omitted condition to its answer or as explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r11.anchor: ( وإياي ) ضمير منفصل منصوب المحل بمحذوف يفسره المذكور والفاء عند بعضهم جزائية زحلقت من الجزاء المحذوف إلى مفسره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.speaker: صاحب المفتاح
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.claim: The author of al-Miftāḥ instead takes the fa to coordinate an omitted verb with what precedes, making the overt command explain it and express continued fear or ascent to a higher degree of fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r12.anchor: واختار صاحب المفتاح أنها للعطف على الفعل المحذوف فإن أريد التعقيب الزماني أفادت طلب استمرار الرهبة في جميع الأزمنة بلا تخلل فاصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.claim: The fa cannot be a simple conjunction joining the overt verb, since that would combine two conjunctions; interpreting it as coordination after ellipsis remains possible because the explained verb need not be identical in every respect.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r13.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون عاطفة لئلا يجتمع عاطفان وأختار صاحب المفتاح أنها للعطف على الفعل المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.speaker: some later scholars
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.claim: Some later scholars prefer al-Miftāḥ’s analysis for its subtle meaning; another intermediary account says the fa was originally coordinate and became conditional after ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r14.anchor: واستحسن هذا بعض المتأخرين لاشتماله على معنى بديع خلت عنه الجزائية وقال بعضهم كالمتوسط في المسألة : إنها عاطفة بحسب الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.claim: The verse emphasizes exclusive fear more strongly than the wording of 1:5 through the fronted detached pronoun, delayed attached pronoun, fa, paired explicit and implicit verbs, repetition, and conditional force.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r15.anchor: وعلى كل تقدير فالآية الكريمة آكد في إفادة التخصيص من ( إياك نعبد ) وعد من وجوه التأكيد تقديم الضمير المنفصل وتأخير المتصل والفاء الموجبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.claim: The object of fear is omitted to generalize it to all actions; another view restricts it to breaking the covenant, plausibly because the command follows that covenant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r16.anchor: وحذف متعلق الرهبة للعموم أي أرهبوني في جميع ما تأتون وتذرون وقيل : أرهبون في نقض العهد ولعل التخصيص به مستفاد من ذكر الأمر بالرهبة معه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.claim: Fear of punishment belongs to outward practitioners, while fear of awe belongs to people of the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r17.anchor: ثم الخوف خوفان خوف العقاب وهو نصيب أهل الظاهر وخوف إجلال وهو نصيب أهل القلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the warning as fear that God will inflict on them the punishments He inflicted on their ancestors, including transformation; this suits the outwardly focused addressees.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r18.anchor: وما روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المعنى أرهبون أن أنزل بكم ما أنزلت بمن كان قبلكم من آبائكم من النقمات التي قد عرفتم من المسخ وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.claim: The yāʾ of the object pronoun is dropped in arhibūn for verse-final rhyme; Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads it with the yāʾ in its original form.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p242#2/r19.anchor: وحذفت ياء الضمير من أرهبون لأنها فاصلة وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق بالياء على الأصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r3.claim: “Children of Israel” means the descendants of Jacob.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r4.claim: Israel means “servant of God”; another view says it means God’s chosen one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r4.anchor: ومعنى إسرائيل: عبد الله، "وإيل" هو الله تعالى، وقيل صفوة الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: إسرائيل بغير همز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r6.claim: “Remember” means preserve; remembrance can occur in the heart or on the tongue.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r6.anchor: {اذكروا} احفظوا، والذكر: يكون بالقلب ويكون باللسان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes “remember” to mean give thanks.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says remembering a blessing means thanking for it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r9.claim: The singular “blessing” has a plural meaning, as in the verse saying God's blessings cannot be counted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r9.anchor: {نعمتي} أي: نعمي، لفظها واحد ومعناها جمع (4)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r10.claim: The blessings were bestowed on the Israelites' ancestors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r10.anchor: {التي أنعمت عليكم} أي على أجدادكم وأسلافكم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r11.claim: Qatada identifies the special blessings as the sea's parting, rescue from Pharaoh, shade in the wilderness, manna and quail, and the Torah, among many others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r11.anchor: قال قتادة: هي النعم التي خصت بها بنو إسرائيل: من فلق البحر وإنجائهم من فرعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r12.claim: Another view is that the verse means all blessings God gives His servants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r12.anchor: وقال غيره: هي جميع النعم التي لله عز وجل على عباده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r13.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant means obeying His command; His fulfilling theirs means acceptance and reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r13.anchor: {وأوفوا بعهدي} أي بامتثال أمري {أوف بعهدكم} بالقبول والثواب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r14.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r14.claim: Qatada and Mujahid identify the covenant with the Israelite covenant in the Table (5:12), including God's promise to forgive their sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r14.anchor: قال قتادة ومجاهد: أراد بهذا العهد ما ذكر في سورة المائدة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r15.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r15.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the covenant with the pledge at Sinai to uphold the Torah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r15.anchor: وقال الحسن هو قوله "وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة" (63-البقرة)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r16.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r16.claim: Muqatil identifies the covenant as the pledge that the Israelites worship none but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r16.anchor: وقال مقاتل هو قوله "وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله" (83-البقرة)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r17.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r17.claim: Al-Kalbi says God promised through Moses to send an unlettered prophet from Ishmael's line; whoever follows him and believes his light will be forgiven, enter Paradise, and receive a double reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p86#3/r17.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عهد الله إلى بني إسرائيل على لسان موسى: إني باعث من بني إسماعيل نبيا أميا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r1.claim: Israel is to fear God if they break the covenant.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r2.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r2.claim: Yaʿqub writes the final yāʾs omitted in the written form in “fear Me,” “be mindful of Me,” and “fear Me”; the other readers omit them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p87/r2.anchor: وأثبت يعقوب الياءآت المحذوفة في الخط مثل فارهبوني، فاتقوني، واخشوني،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r1.claim: The Children of Israel are Jacob's descendants; ibn is linked to building because a child is built by his father, as artifacts are attributed to makers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r1.anchor: أي أولاد يعقوب، والابن من البناء لأنه مبني أبيه، ولذلك ينسب المصنوع إلى صانعه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r2.claim: Israel is Jacob's title, interpreted in Hebrew either as God's chosen one or as God's servant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r2.anchor: وإسرائيل لقب يعقوب عليه السلام ومعناه بالعبرية: صفوة الله، وقيل: عبد الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r3.claim: Reported readings include Isrāʾil with the yāʾ omitted, Isrāl with both letters omitted, and Isrāyīl with hamza changed to yāʾ.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r4.claim: Remembering the blessing means reflecting on it and fulfilling gratitude for it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r5.claim: The blessing is attributed to the addressees because people naturally envy others, whereas seeing one's own blessings encourages contentment and gratitude.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r5.anchor: وتقييد النعمة بهم لأن الإنسان غيور حسود بالطبع، فإذا نظر إلى ما أنعم الله على غيره حمله الغيرة والحسد على الكفران والسخط

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r6.claim: Alternatively, the blessing refers to their ancestors' rescue from Pharaoh and pardon for the calf, and their own chance to live in Muhammad's time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r6.anchor: وقيل أراد بها ما أنعم الله به على آبائهم من الإنجاء من فرعون والغرق، ومن العفو عن اتخاذ العجل، وعليهم من إدراك زمن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r7.claim: A reading gives udhkurū; the form's original is idh-takirū.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r7.anchor: { اذكروا } والأصل إذتكروا. ونعمتي بإسكان الياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r8.claim: One recitational practice leaves the yāʾ of niʿmatī still at pause but drops it in connected speech, for speakers who do not vocalize a yāʾ preceded by kasra.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40/r8.anchor: ونعمتي بإسكان الياء وقفا وإسقاطها درجا هو مذهب من لا يحرك الياء المكسور ما قبلها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant means faith and obedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.claim: God fulfills His covenant by granting an excellent reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.anchor: { أوف بعهدكم } بحسن الإثابة والعهد يضاف إلى المعاهد والمعاهد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.claim: He tentatively reads the first covenant as active and the second as passive: God required faith and good works through proofs and books and promised reward for good deeds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.anchor: ولعل الأول مضاف إلى الفاعل والثاني إلى المفعول، فإنه تعالى عهد إليهم بالإيمان والعمل الصالح بنصب الدلائل وإنزال الكتب، ووعد لهم بالثواب على حسناتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.claim: The levels of reciprocal fidelity range from profession of faith and God's protection of life and property to absorption in monotheism and God's gift of everlasting encounter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.anchor: فأول مراتب الوفاء منا هو الإتيان بكلمتي الشهادة، ومن الله تعالى حقن الدم والمال، وآخرها منا الاستغراق في بحر التوحيد بحيث يغفل عن نفسه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets Israel's duty as following Muhammad and God's fulfillment as lifting burdens and shackles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أوفوا بعهدي في اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أوف بعهدكم في رفع الآصار والإغلال.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.speaker: غيره
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.claim: Another reported interpretation makes the duty performing obligations and avoiding major sins, with forgiveness and reward as God's response.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.anchor: وعن غيره أوفوا بأداء الفرائض وترك الكبائر أوف بالمغفرة والثواب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.claim: A further interpretation is steadfastness on the straight path in return for honor and lasting bliss, viewed through the intermediaries.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.anchor: أو أوفوا بالاستقامة على الطريق المستقيم، أوف بالكرامة والنعيم المقيم، فبالنظر إلى الوسائط.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, both covenants are objective: fulfill what you pledged to God in faith and obedience, and He fulfills His pledge of reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.anchor: وقيل كلاهما مضاف إلى المفعول والمعنى: أوفوا بما عاهدتموني من الإيمان والتزام الطاعة، أوف بما عاهدتكم من حسن الإثابة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.claim: The covenant is elaborated in al-Māʾida 5:12, including the promise to admit them to gardens with rivers flowing beneath.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.anchor: وتفصيل العهدين في سورة المائدة في قوله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.claim: A reading with a doubled wāw intensifies the command.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.claim: Fear God in all actions, especially in breaking the covenant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.anchor: فيما تأتون وتذرون وخصوصا في نقض العهد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.claim: The emphatic exclusive command is stronger than al-Fātiḥa 1:5 because it both fronts and repeats the object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.anchor: وهو آكد في إفادة التخصيص من إياك نعبد لما فيه مع التقديم من تكرير المفعول

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r3.claim: The prefixed fa has a conditional force: if you fear anything, then fear Me.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r3.anchor: والفاء الجزائية الدالة على تضمن الكلام معنى الشرط كأنه قيل: إن كنتم راهبين شيئا فارهبون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r4.claim: Rahba means fear accompanied by caution.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r5.claim: The verse combines promise and threat, requires gratitude and covenant-keeping, and teaches believers to fear only God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:40#3/r5.anchor: والآية متضمنة للوعد والوعيد دالة على وجوب الشكر والوفاء بالعهد، وأن المؤمن ينبغي أن لا يخاف أحدا إلا الله تعالى.

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r1.claim: One view says Israel is told to recall blessings, while Muhammad's community is told to remember God directly: earlier peoples look from blessing to Benefactor, his community from Benefactor to blessings.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ربط بني إسرائيل بذكر النعم ، وأسقط عن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك ودعاهم إلى ذكره فقال ﴿ فاذكروني أذكركم ﴾

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r2.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r2.claim: Sahl says Muhammad's community received an added distinction, as their Prophet did: Abraham was shown the heavenly kingdom, while Muhammad's inner secret and vision were set apart from others.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r2.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله : أراد الله أن يخص أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بزيادة على الأمم كما خص نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم بزيادة على الأنبياء

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r3.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r3.claim: Some Baghdadis interpret the covenant as the primordial pledge of assent and command believers to seek nothing from anyone but God.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r3.anchor: قال بعض البغداديين : أوفوا بعهدي الذي عهدتم في الميثاق الأول بلفظة ' بلى ' ، فلا ترجعوا في طلب شيء إلى غيري .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r4.claim: One view interprets keeping God's covenant as guarding His trusts and disclosing them only to their proper recipients; God then opens His treasuries and nearness to them.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : أوفوا بعهدي احفظوا ودائعي عندكم ، لا تظهروها إلا عند أهلها ، أوف بعهدكم أبح لكم مفاتيح خزائني وقربي

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r5.claim: Another view says fulfilling the covenant means performing obligatory duties according to the Sunna and sincerely; God fulfills His side by accepting and rewarding them.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r5.anchor: وقيل أوفوا بعهدي في أداء الفرائض على السنة والإخلاص ، أوف بعهدكم بقبولها منكم ومجازاتكم عليها .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r6.claim: Ibn Ata interprets the covenant as guarding one's bodily life outwardly and inwardly, with God protecting one's secrets from witnessing created things.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : أوفوا بعهدي في حفظ الجلود ظاهرا وباطنا ، أوف بعهدكم بحفظ أسراركم عن مشاهدة الأعيان .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r7.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r7.claim: Sahl says the covenant is striving against one's lower self, and God's fulfillment is helping believers in that struggle.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r7.anchor: وقال سهل : أوفوا بعهدي في مجاهدة أنفسكم ، أوف بعهدكم لمعاونتكم عليها .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r8.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r8.claim: Abu Uthman interprets the covenant as preserving proper outward manners, while God adorns the believer's inner secrets.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : أوفوا بعهدي في حفظ آداب الظواهر ، أوف بعهدكم بتزين سرائركم .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r9.claim: Another view makes reliance on God the covenant and God's fulfillment the sufficiency of believers' needs.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أوفوا بعهدي في التوكل ، أوف بعهدكم بكفاية مهماتكم .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r10.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r10.claim: Some Iraqis read the pledge as being God's created servants, with God being their Real Lord in return.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r10.anchor: وقال بعض العراقيين : أوفوا بعهدي كونوا لي خلقا ، أوف بعهدكم أكن لكم حقا .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r11.speaker: أبو الحسن الوراق
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r11.claim: Al-Warraq says fulfilling the covenant means worship, and God's fulfillment is bringing worshippers to the stations of supplication.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r11.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الوراق : أوفوا بعهدي في العبادات ، أوف بعهدكم أوصلكم إلى منازل الدعايات .

SULAMI:v1p57#3/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r12.speaker: الثوري
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r12.claim: Asked about the verse, al-Thawri describes the covenant as service in the abode of love while keeping God's sanctity; its fulfillment is nearness and joy in beholding Him.
SULAMI:v1p57#3/r12.anchor: سئل الثوري عن فهم هذه الآية أوفوا بعهدي قال : أوفوا بعهدي في دار محبتي على بساط خدمتي بحفظ حرمتي

SULAMI:v1p58/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p58/r1.claim: The author defines awe as the heart's fear concerning the course of its thoughts.
SULAMI:v1p58/r1.anchor: الرهبة : هي خشية القلب من روى خواطره

SULAMI:v1p58/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p58/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p58/r2.claim: Sahl says awe belongs to the station of certainty and gnosis, while piety concerns prior knowledge and the danger of divine stratagem or gradual entrapment.
SULAMI:v1p58/r2.anchor: وقال سهل : وإياي فارهبون موضع اليقين ومعرفته وإياي فاتقون ، موضع العلم السابق وموضع المكر والاستدراج .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r1.claim: God begins by recalling favors that Israel met with ingratitude and His forbearance and pardon, then commands covenant-keeping, especially following Muhammad and believing his Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r1.anchor: ابتدأ سبحانه بتذكيرهم بما خصهم به عن النوع الآدمي من النعم التي كانوا يقابلونها بالكفران

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r2.claim: Israel is the one whom God honored, and whose children He honored for his sake.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r2.anchor: أي الذي شرفته وشرفت بنيه من أجله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r3.claim: Remembering may be by tongue or heart; the author transmits al-Kisa'i's distinction that kasra is tongue and damma is heart, whose opposites are silence and forgetfulness respectively.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r3.anchor: وقال الكسائي : هو بالكسر باللسان وبالضم بالقلب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r4.claim: Al-Harali defines remembrance as bringing to mind something previously forgotten.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r4.anchor: من الذكر وهو استحضار ما سبقه النسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r5.claim: A blessing gives a person what suits body and soul, including what suits the inner and outer self and its household relations.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r5.anchor: وهي إنالة الشخص ما يوافق نفسه وبدنه وعند المتفطن ما يوافق باطنه وظاهره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r6.claim: Al-Harali draws a subtle distinction in the form of allati: its initial element signals an inward, descending, imagined, ambiguous meaning clarified by its relative clause.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r6.anchor: تي منها إشارة لباطن نازل متخيل مبهم تفسره صلته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r7.claim: The special blessing was guidance through scriptures and messengers, saving Israel from humiliation in this world and the next.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r7.anchor: وتلك النعمة الشريفة هي الإتيان بالهدى من الكتب والرسل الذي استنقذتكم به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r8.claim: Al-Harali explains fulfilling a covenant as an act that follows prior knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r8.anchor: من الوفاء وهو عمل لاحق بمقتضى تقدم علم سابق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r9.claim: Israel's covenant is adherence to revelation and following Muhammad and those whom they were instructed to follow after him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r9.anchor: الذي أخذته عليكم في لزوم ما أنزل إليكم من متابعة نبيكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r10.claim: Al-Harali defines covenant as a prior, private undertaking in a matter assigned to someone.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r10.anchor: والعهد التقدم في الشيء خفية اختصاصا لمن يتقدم له فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r11.speaker: الأصفهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r11.claim: Al-Isfahani defines covenant as preserving and tending something continually.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r11.anchor: وقال الأصفهاني : حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا فحالا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r12.speaker: الخليل
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r12.claim: Al-Khalil says the root sense of covenant is protecting something and renewing the pledge to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r12.anchor: قال الخليل : أصله الاحتفاظ بالشيء وإجداد العهد به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r13.claim: God's fulfillment of their covenant includes making them free of fear and grief through abundant livelihood and victory over enemies, as the Torah states elsewhere.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r13.anchor: أي في جعلكم ممن لا خوف عليهم و لا حزن بسعة العيش والنصر على الأعداء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r14.claim: They must fear God alone and not stray into the fate of unbelievers; rahba is the soul's fear of expected harm from what it would flee.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r14.anchor: والرهب حذر النفس مما شأنها منه الهرب لأذى تتوقعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r15.claim: Al-Harali says the extended argument suits learned deniers and stubborn opponents, who resist what they know.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r15.anchor: وأطال سبحانه في حجاجهم جريا على قانون النظر في جدال العالم الجاحد وخطاب المنكر المعانج

BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r16.claim: Believing the revealed Qur'an, which confirms their scripture, reaffirms the truth of that Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p114/r16.anchor: تقرير لذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r1.claim: Al-Harali links the opening severe command to the sudden harshness of the Hour, pairing the first warning blows of command with the first blows of creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r1.anchor: وهي أول قوارع الأمر كما أن فجاءة الساعة أول قوارع الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r2.claim: The warned person either flees from the rebuke like wild donkeys from a lion or turns away arrogantly after reflection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r2.anchor: إما أن ينفر عند الزجرة توحشا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r3.claim: Umar says that minds are as if their Maker has undermined them; the author connects this to arrogant people being diverted from God's signs as punishment for pride.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r3.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : لكنها عقول كادها باريها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r4.claim: The warning also teaches the attentive person to avoid public and hidden acts harmful in the afterlife, including exploitation, adultery, and intercourse during menstruation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r4.anchor: تمام هذا المعنى ينهى المتأنس المحاصر عن الفواحش الظاهرة والباطنة الضارة في العقبى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117/r5.claim: The warning reaches conduct people regard as worldly cleverness, including consuming wealth unjustly, usury, spying, backbiting, and mockery.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.claim: The prohibitions include falsely denying a believer's faith for worldly gain and preventing charitable giving by people of virtue and means.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r1.anchor: ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.claim: The discipline extends to refusing excess beyond sufficiency, including arrogance and coveting others' worldly display, because every surplus is a trial.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r2.anchor: لأن كل زائد على الكفاف فتنة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.claim: Mastery of this prohibition passage underlies later knowledge, action, steadfastness, and acceptance when tested.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r3.anchor: ولا تصح الوجوه والحروف التي بعده أي وهي سائر الحروف علما وعملا وثباتا وقبولا عند التمحيص إلا بحسب الإحكام في قراءة هذا الحرف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.claim: The upright religion asks little in commands but requires strong abstention from limitless prohibitions, whose many avenues bring harm after death; people struggle because they mistake forbidden excess for worldly necessity.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r4.anchor: لأن الملة الحنيفية مبنية على الاكتفاء باليسير من المأمورات والمبالغة في الحمية من عموم ما لا يتناهى من المنهيات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.claim: Abstinence is the foundation of treatment: worship without giving up prohibitions is like taking medicine without a diet, wasting the remedy and worsening the illness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p117#2/r5.anchor: والحمية أصل الدواء , فمن لم يحتم عن المنهيات لم ينفعه تداويه بالمأمورات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r1.claim: People may perform great acts of worship yet lose their effort because they pursued worldly desires and sins; worship without abstinence is treatment without a necessary diet.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r1.anchor: وكانوا يصومون ويصلون ويأخذون وهنا من الليل لكن ذلك تداو بغير حمية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r2.claim: One who abstains has fulfilled the prohibition passage; the most beloved worship includes leaving worldly status and wealth's temptations, while the quoted sayings praise prophetic simplicity and adherence to the Sunnah.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r2.anchor: أحب العبادات إلى الله ترك الدنيا وحمية النفس من هوى جاهها ومالها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r3.claim: The Qur'an is evidence for the person who acts on it and leads him to Paradise, but becomes evidence against one who neglects it, driving him toward a terrifying pit of Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r3.anchor: والقرآن حجة لمن عمل به فصار إمامه يقوده إلى الجنة . وحجة على من لم يعمل به

BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r4.claim: The Qur'an is a light by which God guides some and misguides others, and may increase wrongdoers' loss; the passage closes with a supplication seeking refuge in God's forgiveness and pleasure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r4.anchor: ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r5.claim: Keeping the commands and prohibitions that govern worldly welfare builds a virtuous habit that eases the afterlife's commands and prohibitions; belief in the unseen trades passing worldly goods for the promised lasting reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p118/r5.anchor: فكل الحلال ما عدا الكفاف بالسنة متجر للعبد , إن أنفقه ربحه وأبقاه فقدم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Worldly wealth is profitable when given away for the hereafter, as shown by the wish to give charity before death and the command to spend what one loves.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون

BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: The lawful sphere is broad so gratitude may be shown, while prohibitions restrict it to cultivate patience, making the servant both grateful and patient.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: حرف النهي مضيق لمتسع حرف الحلال ليحصل به الصبر

TUSTARI:2:40/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r1.claim: Fear of God is the light of the soul perceived by the heart's sight and the heart's comprehensive gnosis, reached through struggle and striving in faith.
TUSTARI:2:40/r1.anchor: أراد موضع نور النفس من بصر القلب والمعرفة من كلية القلب، لأن المكابدة والمجاهدة في الإيمان

TUSTARI:2:40/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r2.claim: When the heart settles in piety and tawhid, the light of certainty is unveiled and the servant reaches God in faith.
TUSTARI:2:40/r2.anchor: فإذا سكن القلب من التقوى إلى الغير انكشف نور اليقين، ووصل العبد ساكنا بالإيمان لله توحيدا على تمكين

TUSTARI:2:40/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r3.claim: This connection to God is through tawhid and obedience, not indwelling, union, or literal joining; its measure follows one's vision of God.
TUSTARI:2:40/r3.anchor: لا بمعنى الحلول، ولا بمعنى الجمع، ولا بمعنى الاتصال، ولكن معنى اتصال العبد بمولاه من موضع توحيده وطاعته بالله ورسوله

TUSTARI:2:40/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r4.claim: The root of piety is separation from the lower self, refusing its pleasures and unfulfilled desires.
TUSTARI:2:40/r4.anchor: وأصل التقوى: مباينة النفس، فيباينها في ذلك، ولا يساكنها شيئا من ملاذ هواها

TUSTARI:2:40/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r5.claim: People's standing on the Resurrection scales corresponds to their light of certainty: the weightier certainty weighs more.
TUSTARI:2:40/r5.anchor: يتفاضلون في القيامة على قدر نور يقينهم، فمن كان أوزن يقينا كان أثقل ميزانا

TUSTARI:2:40/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:40/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:40/r6.claim: Sound certainty is recognized by strong trust in God and good expectation of Him; trust is witnessing through certainty, whose perfection is arrival to God.
TUSTARI:2:40/r6.anchor: بقوة ثقته بالله تعالى، وحسن ظنه به، فالثقة بالله مشاهدة باليقين، وعين اليقين وكليته وكماله ونهايته الوصول إلى الله

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r1.claim: An unattributed dialogue maps the addressee's book to tattooing, reading to poetry, messengers to soothsayers, food to what lacks God's name, drink to intoxicants, truth to lies, house to bathhouse, snares to women, caller to flute, and mosque to markets.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r1.anchor: قال: فما كتابي قال: كتابك الوشم وقراءتك الشعر ورسلك الكهنة وطعامك ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Israel as Jacob.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إسرائيل يعقوب

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r3.claim: Ibn Masud also identifies Israel as Jacob.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إسرائيل هو يعقوب

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r4.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r4.claim: Abu Majliz recounts that Jacob wrestled an angel, then demanded a name after seizing him; the angel named him Israel.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r4.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال: كان يعقوب رجلا بطيشا فلقي ملكا فعالجه فصرعه الملك فضربه على فخذيه

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: Abu Majliz notes that Israel, Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael are among angelic names.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: قال أبو مجلز: ألا ترى أنه من أسماء الملائكة إسرائيل وجبريل وميكائيل وإسرافيل

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r6.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says the prophets were Israelites except ten named prophets, and that only Israel and Jesus had two names: Jacob and the Messiah.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كانت الأنبياء من بني إسرائيل إلا عشرة نوح وهود وصالح ولوط وشعيب وإبراهيم وإسماعيل واسحق ومحمد

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r7.claim: Israel, Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael are names formed like Abd Allah.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن إسرائيل وميكائيل وجبريل وإسرافيل كقولك عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن الحرث البصري
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r8.claim: Abdullah b. al-Harith al-Basri says the Hebrew word eil means God.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحرث البصري قال ايل الله بالعبرانية

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r9.claim: Bani Israel addresses the Jewish scholars; remembering God's favor means recalling blessings to them and their ancestors, including rescue from Pharaoh and his people.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يا بني إسرائيل} قال: للأحبار من اليهود {اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم} أي آلائي عندكم وعند آبائكم لما كان نجاهم به من فرعون وقومه

DURR-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: Their covenant was to believe and follow the Prophet when he came; God's fulfillment would remove their burdens and fetters, while fearing God means fearing punishment like that of their forebears.
DURR-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: من فرعون وقومه {وأوفوا بعهدي} الذي أخذت بأعناقكم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ جاءكم {أوف بعهدكم}

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: The covenant requires obedience and avoidance of disobedience, in relation to the Prophet and other matters; God's fulfillment is approval and entry into Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وأوفوا بعهدي} يقول: ما أمرتكم به من طاعتي ونهيتكم عنه من معصيتي في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وغيره {أوف بعهدكم} يقول: أرض عنكم وأدخلكم الجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: Ibn Masud gives the same interpretation of the covenant as Ibn Abbas.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود مثله

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the covenant as the pledge taken from the Israelites in the covenant passage of al-Maida.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} قال: هو الميثاق الذي أخذ عليهم

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: Qatada likewise links the pledge to al-Maida 5:12, including God's promise to admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} قال: العهد الذي أخذ الله عليهم وأعطاهم الآية التي في سورة المائدة

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says they must fulfill what God obligated and God will fulfill the promised reward He undertook.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} قال: أوفوا بما افترضت عليكم أوف لكم بما رأيت الوعد لكم به على نفسي

DURR-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the covenant as obeying God, with Paradise as the reward.
DURR-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} قال: أوفوا بطاعتي أوف لكم بالجنة

AKHFASH:v1p76/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p76/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p76/r7.claim: Before an added alif-lām, the yāʾ may be dropped to avoid two silent letters or opened; fatḥa is best, and this is the reading he follows.
AKHFASH:v1p76/r7.anchor: وكذلك اذا لقيتها الف ولام زائدتان فان شئت حذفت الياء لاجتماع الساكنين وان شئت فتحتها كيلا يجتمع حرفان ساكنان. الا ان احسن ذلك الفتح

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r1.claim: The Prophet asked Jewish visitors whether Israel was Jacob; they affirmed it, and he told them to bear witness to their admission.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r1.anchor: حضرت عصابة من اليهود نبي الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال لهم : هل تعلمون ان اسرائيل يعقوب ؟ فقالوا : اللهم نعم قال النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم : اشهد عليهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r2.claim: Addressed to Jewish scholars, remembering God's favor means recalling His beneficence to them and their ancestors in saving them from Pharaoh and his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r2.anchor: يا اهل الكتاب ، للاحبار من يهود : اذكروا نعمتي التي انعمت عليكم اي بلائي عندكم وعند ابائكم ; لما كان نجاهم به من فرعون وقومه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r3.claim: God's favor included making prophets and messengers from them and sending them scriptures.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال : نعمته ان جعل منهم الانبياء والرسل وانزل عليهم الكتب .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r4.claim: God's favors to the Israelites included what was named and other blessings: splitting the rock, sending manna and quails, and rescuing them from Pharaoh's bondage.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : يا بني اسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي انعمت عليكم فنعمة الله التي انعم بها على بني اسرائيل فيما سمى وفيما سوى ذلك ، فجر لهم الحجر وانزل عليهم المن والسلوى وانجاهم من عبودية ال فرعون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r5.claim: The covenant is obedience to what God commanded and avoidance of what He prohibited, concerning the Prophet and others.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : واوفوا بعهدي يقول : ما امرتكم به من طاعة ونهيتكم عنه من معصية في النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم وغيره .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r6.claim: The author reports that al-Rabi' ibn Anas gave a similar explanation of the covenant.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r6.anchor: وروى عن الربيع بن انس نحو ذلك من رواية حاتم ابن اسماعيل عن أبي جعفر .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r7.claim: Another report says the covenant was the pledge taken from them concerning the Prophet when he came.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : اوفوا بعهدي الذي اخذت في اعناقكم للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - اذ جاءكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r8.claim: Al-Aliyah says God's covenant was to worship Him through Islam and follow it.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : واوفوا بعهدي قال عهده إلى عبادة دينه الاسلام ان يتبعوه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r9.claim: The author says al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' also gave al-Aliyah's explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p94#2/r9.anchor: وروى عن الضحاك ، وقتادة والسدى ، والربيع نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r1.claim: God fulfills His covenant by being pleased with them and admitting them to Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : اوف بعهدكم يقول : ارضى عنكم وادخلكم الجنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r2.claim: God fulfills the promise by granting what He pledged for believing and following the Prophet, and removing the burdens imposed for their earlier sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : اوف بعهدكم انجز لكم ما وعدتكم عليه بتصديقه واتباعه ، فوضع عنكم ما كان عليكم من الاصر والاغلال التي كانت في اعناقكم بذنوبكم التي كانت من احداثكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r3.claim: The author says Abu al-Aliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' reported a similar promise to al-Dahhak's account from Ibn Abbas.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r3.anchor: وروى عن أبي العالية والضحاك والسدى والربيع بن انس نحو ما ذكرنا عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r4.claim: Fear of God means fearing that He will send the calamities inflicted on their forefathers, including transformation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : واياي فارهبون ان انزل بكم ما انزلت بمن كان قبلكم من ابائكم من النقمات التي قد عرفتم من المسخ وغيره .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r5.claim: Al-Aliyah glosses “fear Me” simply as “be afraid of Me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية واياي فارهبون فاخشون .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r6.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r6.claim: The author says al-Suddi, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Qatada gave the same gloss, “be afraid of Me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p96/r6.anchor: قال : أبو محمد وكذا روي عن السدى والربيع ابن انس وقتادة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur takes the covenant as all the pledges God repeatedly made Israel undertake: establish the religion, support messengers, avoid shedding one another's blood, and believe in the whole religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r1.anchor: والصحيح عندي أن المراد بالعهد هو العهد الذي أخذه الله على بني إسرائيل غير مرة من إقامة الدين وتأييد الرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r2.claim: God's covenant with Israel and its breach are reiterated in 5:12–13, including the curse for breaking the pact.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r2.anchor: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا إلى قوله : فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r3.claim: The covenant and Israel's later deafness and blindness are also recalled in 5:70–71.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r3.anchor: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r4.claim: The covenant included a prohibition on bloodshed, which Israel violated by killing one another and rejecting parts of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r4.anchor: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم لا تسفكون دماءكم إلى قوله : ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون أنفسكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r5.claim: Israel's own scriptures condemn breaking God's covenants and use covenant as a title for the Mosaic law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r5.anchor: بل إن كتبهم قد صرحت بعهود الله تعالى لهم وأنحت عليهم نقضهم لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r6.claim: Calling the transgressors covenant-breakers signals that the intended transgressors are the Jews, already condemned by their scriptures and prophets; this points to the covenant recalled in 2:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r6.anchor: ولما كان قوله : { الذين ينقضون عهد الله } الآية وصفا للفاسقين وكان المراد من الفاسقين اليهود كما علمت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r7.claim: The word covenant powerfully hints at the intended subject, like a key solving a riddle, and anticipates the covenant in 2:40.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r7.anchor: فكان لاختيار لفظ العهد هنا وقع عظيم يتنزل منزلة المفتاح الذي يوضع في حل اللغز ليشير للمقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r8.claim: The pronoun refers to the covenant: the phrase means after the covenant has been confirmed and strengthened.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r8.anchor: والضمير للعهد أي من بعد توكيد العهد وتوثيقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r9.speaker: الخفاجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r9.claim: Al-Khafaji reads mīthāq as an intensified form of mifʿal; Ibn Ashur says its source-noun sense is more likely here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r9.anchor: قال الخفاجي كأنه إشباع للمفعل ، وللمصدر أيضا نحو الميلاد والميعاد وهو الأظهر هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r10.claim: Because the covenant is unspecified and covers all pledges, its confirmation can concern a prior or subsequent pledge, like the confirmed oaths in 16:91; the mīthāq is another covenant treated as reinforcing one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p370/r10.anchor: ولما كان المراد بالعهد عهدا غير معينن ، بل كل ما عاهدوا عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r1.claim: The conjunction introduces fearing God as the next step after recalling blessings and fulfilling the covenant: fear of God completes the command by resisting leaders who would block adherence to the promised messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وإياي فارهبون } عطفت الواو جملة { وإياي } على الجمل المتقدمة من قوله : { وأوفوا بعهدي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r2.claim: Israel should have answered its chiefs and scholars as the believers told Pharaoh at Moses' mission, rather than letting them prevent fulfillment of the covenant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r2.anchor: فكانوا أحرياء بأن يخاطبوا سادتهم وأحبارهم بمثل ذلك الخطاب عند البعثة المحمدية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r3.claim: Fronting 'Me' makes the command exclusive: fear God and, by implication, no one else; fear of the rabbis had obstructed keeping the covenant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r3.anchor: فتقديم المفعول هنا متعين للاختصاص ليحصل من الجملة إثبات ونفي واختير من طرق القصر طريق التقديم دون ما وإلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r4.claim: Fronting an object whose verb resumes it with a pronoun conveys exclusivity more emphatically than fronting before a verb without resumption; al-Kashshaf contrasts this with 'You alone we worship.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p454/r4.anchor: وتقديم المفعول مع اشتغال فعله بضميره آكد في إفادة التقديم الحصر من تقديم المفعول على الفعل غير المشتغل بضميره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects al-Sakkaki's claim that the fronted object in an occupied-verb construction can equally mark emphasis or exclusivity depending on where one imagines the omitted verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r1.anchor: لا التفات إلى ما وجه به صاحب ( المفتاح ) أن احتمال المفعول في الاشتغال التخصيص والتقوي باق على حاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r2.claim: The imagined position of an omitted verb is inaccessible to listeners; they attend to the observable fronting and repeated reference, which usually marks exclusivity, though some examples do not.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r2.anchor: فإنه بناه على حالة موقع الفعل المقدر مع أن تقدير الفعل اعتبار لا يلاحظه البلغاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Zuhayr's verse continuation to show the cited fronting construction does not express exclusivity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r3.anchor: فكلا أراهم أصبحوا يعقلونه صحيحات مال طالعات بمخرم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r4.claim: The fāʾ after the fronted object adds emphasis because it signals an omitted general condition; Ibn Ashur cites al-Zamakhshari's reading of 'So magnify your Lord' as 'whatever happens, magnify Him.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r4.anchor: لأن الفاء كما في هذه الآية مؤذنة بشرط مقدر ولما كان هذا الشرط لا دليل عليه إلا الفاء تعين تقديره عاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r5.claim: Thus the sense is: fulfill My covenant and I will fulfill yours; whatever happens, fear Me. The condition is universal and guarantees its result, and the fāʾ is shifted after the conjunction to avoid two adjacent particles.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r5.anchor: فالمعنى هنا وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم ومهما يكن شيء فإياي ارهبوني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur considers this construction a distinctive Qur'anic stylistic innovation that he has not found in Arabic speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p455/r6.anchor: وأحسب أن مثل هذا التركيب من مبتكر أساليب القرآن ولم أذكر أني عثرت على مثله في كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r1.claim: Following al-Zamakhshari's reading through Sibawayh, the fa after a fronted object signals an understood condition, often after a command or prohibition semantically opposed to the following command.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r2.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r2.claim: The poet's line illustrates an implied condition: if one worships anything, then worship God, with the fa marking the consequence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r3.speaker: صاحب ( الكشاف )
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lists emphases in ‘You alone, so fear Me’: the detached pronoun precedes the verb, its attached pronoun is repeated, fa adds force, and the wording implies a condition and repeated fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r3.anchor: عن صاحب ( الكشاف ) أنه قال : إن في قوله تعالى : { وإياي فارهبون } وجوها من التأكيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r4.claim: Fronting expresses exclusivity, itself an intensifier, while repeating the subject in the attached pronoun reinforces predication; here the author ranks this phrasing among four increasingly emphatic patterns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r4.anchor: في التعبير عن مثل هذا الاختصاص في كلام البلغاء مراتب أربع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r5.claim: In al-Zamakhshari's phrase ‘conjoined and conjoining,’ the terms mean what precedes and follows in ordinary language, not syntactic coordination, which would not work here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p456/r5.anchor: العطف اللغوي أي معقبا ومعقبا به لا العطف النحوي إذ لا يستقيم هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r1.claim: Most of the ten canonical readers omit the first-person yāʾ after the protective nūn in both connection and pause; Yaʿqūb retains it in both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r1.anchor: وحذفت ياء المتكلم بعد نون الوقاية في قوله : { فارهبون } للجمهور من العشرة في الوصل والوقف وأثبتها يعقوب في الوصل والوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r2.claim: Arab dialects differ: most omit the yāʾ only at pause, Hudhayl omits it in both positions, and Hijaz retains it in both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r2.anchor: وجمهور العرب يحذفونها في الوقف دون الوصل وهذيل يحذفونها في الوقف والوصل وأهل الحجاز يثبتونها في الحالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r3.claim: The majority's omission in connected reading follows the codex spelling and recitation; the verse ending is treated like pause, as Sibawayh says endings and rhyme permit deletion. Yaʿqūb follows Hijazi usage and his transmitted reading; the comparable non-final form keeps yāʾ in 2:186.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p457/r3.anchor: لأن كلمة { فارهبون } كتبت في المصحف الإمام بدون ياء وقرئت كذلك في سنة القراءة

FARRA:v1p29/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p29/r1.claim: The form ادكروا corresponds to تذكروا elsewhere and to the everyday instruction اذكر مكاني من أبيك.

FARRA:v1p29/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p29/r2.claim: The speaker’s yāʾ has both a still and a vowelled form; before the definite article, Arabs prefer the vowelled form to avoid losing the yāʾ at the article’s initial sukūn.
FARRA:v1p29/r2.anchor: فإن كل ياء كانت من المتكلم ففيها لغتان

FARRA:v1p29/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p29/r3.claim: Sukūn remains permissible before alif-lām; يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا was read both with a still yāʾ and with its vowelled form.
FARRA:v1p29/r3.anchor: وقد يجوز إسكانها عند الألف واللام وقد قال الله

FARRA:v1p29/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p29/r4.claim: When the yāʾ is absent, as in فبشر عباد, it cannot be vowelled; this rule applies to comparable Qurʾanic forms.
FARRA:v1p29/r4.anchor: فلا تنصب ياؤها وهي محذوفة وعلى هذا يقاس كل ما في القرآن منه

FARRA:v1p29/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r5.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v1p29/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says Arabs prefer a vowelled yāʾ before any hamza except alif-lām, as in إني أخاف الله; al-Farrāʾ says he did not observe this usage.
FARRA:v1p29/r5.anchor: زعم الكسائي أن العرب تستحب نصب الياء عند كل ألف مهموزة سوى الألف واللام

FARRA:v1p29/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p29/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ generally heard the yāʾ left still before hamza; he allows vowelled forms in the rare phrases بي أخواك and لي ألفان, while keeping the same underlying analogy.
FARRA:v1p29/r6.anchor: عندي أبوك بتحريك الياء إلا أن يتركوا الهمز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.claim: The vocative yā carries an attention-getting sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: يا حرف نداء مضمن معنى التنبيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl says the vocative’s governing verb is implicit, as though the speaker says “I want” or “I call.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: والعامل في المنادى فعل مضمر كأنه يقول: أريد أو أدعو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says the vocative particle takes the work of an implicit verb and thereby governs; he argues it is the only particle that independently combines with nouns.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: العامل حرف النداء عصب به معنى الفعل المضمر فقوي فعمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.claim: Israel is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham; the Hebrew name means “servant of God,” since Isra means servant and El is God’s name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.anchor: وإسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم عليهم السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.claim: The name has several Arabic forms, including a Tamīmī form Israʾīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.anchor: وهو اسم أعجمي يقال فيه إسراءل وإسرائيل وإسرائيل، وتميم تقول إسرائين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawī offers another derivation: Isra refers to strength in captivity, as if God tightened and strengthened Jacob’s constitution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.anchor: إسرا- مأخوذ من الشدة في الأسر كأنه الذي شد الله أسره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.speaker: نافع والحسن والزهري وابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read Israʾīl without the hamza in Isra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن نافع والحسن والزهري وابن أبي إسحاق ترك همز إسراييل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r8.claim: Dhikr here means recollection in the heart, the opposite of forgetting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r8.anchor: وهذا منها ذكر القلب الذي هو ضد النسيان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.claim: Niʿma is grammatically singular but collective in meaning; its final yā is vowelled before the article, though it may be quiescent and elided, and the vowel is preferable because it preserves a written letter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r9.anchor: والنعمة هنا اسم الجنس فهي مفردة بمعنى الجمع، وتحركت الياء من نعمتي لأنها لقيت الألف واللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives examples of Israel’s favor: prophets from among them, manna and quails, rescue from Pharaoh’s torture, and water gushing from the rock.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.anchor: بعثة الرسل منهم وإنزال المن والسلوى، وإنقاذهم من تعذيب آل فرعون، وتفجير الحجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.claim: Another explanation identifies the favor as granting them the lifetime of Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.anchor: النعمة هنا أن دركهم مدة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.claim: Others identify the favor as granting Israel knowledge of the Torah and making them its people and bearers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.anchor: هي أن منحهم علم التوراة وجعلهم أهله وحملته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats the specific favors as examples and prefers the general meaning of the word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r13.anchor: وهذه أقوال على جهة المثال، والعموم في اللفظة هو الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r14.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r14.claim: Makkī says the address targets only Israelites who believed in Muḥammad, since an unbeliever cannot receive God’s favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r14.anchor: أن المخاطب من بني إسرائيل بهذا الخطاب هم المؤمنون بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، لأن الكافر لا نعمة لله عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وجمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most scholars say the address includes all Israelites living in the Prophet’s time, believers and unbelievers; “you” refers to their ancestors by an Arabic usage that addresses descendants for ancestral acts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r15.anchor: بل الخطاب لجميع بني إسرائيل في مدة النبي عليه السلام، مؤمنهم وكافرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r16.claim: If the address is restricted to believers in Muḥammad, “you” is direct and the commands that follow call for continued commitment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p132#2/r16.anchor: استقام الضمير في عليكم ويجيء كل ما توالى من الأوامر على جهة الاستدامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: “Fulfill My covenant and I will fulfill yours” is a command followed by its response.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r1.anchor: وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم أمر وجوابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r2.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl says the command’s response is jussive because the command carries a conditional sense; fulfilling a covenant means committing to the stipulated act.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r2.anchor: جزم الجواب في الأمر من معنى الشرط، والوفاء بالعهد هو التزام ما تضمن من فعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r3.speaker: الزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads awfi with an open wāw and doubled fāʾ, conveying intensification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r3.anchor: قرأ الزهري: «أوف» بفتح الواو وشد الفاء للتكثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r4.claim: The majority take God’s covenant broadly as all His commands, prohibitions, and instructions, including the Torah’s mention of Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r4.anchor: ذلك عام في جميع أوامره ونواهيه ووصاياه فيدخل في ذلك ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في التوراة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r5.claim: Another view identifies the covenant with God’s command to take what He gave them firmly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r5.anchor: العهد قوله تعالى: خذوا ما آتيناكم بقوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the covenant as God’s pledge to the Children of Israel; their covenant is His promise to admit them to Paradise, and their fulfillment signifies His fulfillment rather than causing it, since a cause cannot precede its effect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r6.anchor: العهد قوله تعالى: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r7.claim: In “Me alone fear,” iyyāya is a noun followed by the first-person pronoun, or the whole form is itself the noun; it is accusative after an implied verb delayed for emphasis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r7.anchor: الاسم ايا والياء ضمير ككاف المخاطب، وقيل إياي بجملته هو الاسم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r8.claim: A preceding verb would require a light attached pronoun, so the implied verb is delayed; the yā after nūn is dropped at the verse ending.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r8.anchor: وامتنع أن يتقدر مقدما لأن الفعل إذا تقدم لم يحسن أن يتصل به إلا ضمير خفيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r9.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p133/r9.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads the final yā in fārhabūnī.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r1.claim: Israel must fulfill the commands and prohibitions it had accepted from God.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r1.anchor: أوفوا لي بما قبلتموه من أمري ونهيي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r2.claim: God will fulfill the reward He promised them for doing so.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47/r2.anchor: أوف لكم بما وعدتكم على ذلك من الجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r1.claim: Israel is Jacob, and Israel is a foreign name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r1.anchor: اسرائيل هو يعقوب وهو اسم أعجمي قال ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r2.anchor: ومعناه عبد الله وقد لفظت به العرب على اوجه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r3.claim: Arabic speakers used several forms of the name: Israʾīl, Isrāl, al-Isrāʾīl, and Isrāʾīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r3.anchor: وقد لفظت به العرب على اوجه فقالت إسرائل واسرال والسرائيل واسرائين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r4.speaker: أمية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r4.claim: Umayya’s poem uses Isrāl, witnessing an Arabic pronunciation of Israel.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r5.speaker: أعرابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r5.claim: A Bedouin’s verse uses Isrāʾīnā for Israel in a saying about the market.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r5.anchor: يقول أهل السوق لما جينا هذا ورب البيت إسرائينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r6.claim: Niʿma means favor or benefaction, while niʿmāʾ is a synonym; with fatḥa on the nūn, niʿmah means luxuriance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r6.anchor: والنعمة المنة مثلها النعماء والنعمة بفتح النون التنعم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r7.claim: The singular favor denotes many favors, as Arabic may use a singular for a collective plural.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r7.anchor: وأراد بالنعمة النعم فوحدها لأنهم يكتفون بالواحد من الجميع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r8.claim: One interpretation identifies the favor as the Torah’s promise describing the Messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r8.anchor: أنها ما استوعدهم من التوراة التي فيها صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the favor as the Torah’s promise describing the Messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r9.anchor: من التوراة التي فيها صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r10.speaker: الحسن، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r10.claim: A second interpretation is the favors bestowed on Israel’s ancestors, including rescue from Pharaoh, the enemy’s destruction, and the Torah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r10.anchor: ما أنعم به على أبائهم وأجدادهم إذ أنجاهم من آل فرعون وأهلك عدوهم واعطاهم التوراة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r11.claim: The descendants can be credited with gifts to their ancestors because ancestral honor and shame extend to descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r11.anchor: لأن فخر الآباء فخر للأبناء وعار الآباء عار على الأبناء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r12.claim: A third interpretation takes the favor as a collective of blessings across changing circumstances.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r12.anchor: والثالث انها جمع نعمة على تصريف الأحوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r13.claim: Remembering the favor means giving thanks; without gratitude, one has not truly remembered it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p72/r13.anchor: والمراد من ذكرها شكرها إذ من لم يشكر فما ذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r1.claim: The Hijaz dialect says awfaytu, while Najd says wafaytu without the initial alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r1.anchor: أهل الحجاز يقولون اوفيت واهل نجد يقولون وفيت بغير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj accepts both wafā bi-l-ʿahd and awfā bihi as idiomatic forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r2.anchor: يقال وفى بالعهد واوفى به وأنشد أما ابن طوق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r3.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r3.claim: The cited line pairs awfā with a covenant and wafā with the camels’ keeper, as lexical evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r3.anchor: أما ابن طوق فقد اوفى بذمته كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba allows wafaytu bi-l-ʿahd and awfaytu bihi, but says only awfaytu is used for measuring out fully.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r4.anchor: يقال وفيت بالعهد وأوفيت به واوفيت الكيل لا غير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r5.claim: The covenant is the Torah’s description of Muhammad, which Israel was charged to fulfill.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r5.anchor: انه لما عهده إليهم في التوراة من صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes the covenant obedience to commands and avoidance of prohibitions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r6.anchor: أنه امتثال الأوامر واجتناب النواهي رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r7.claim: A third interpretation identifies the covenant as Islam.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r8.claim: A fourth interpretation is the covenant described when God took Israel’s pledge and appointed twelve chiefs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا ﴾ المائدة 13 قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r1.claim: God fulfills His covenant by admitting Israel into Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ أوف بعهدكم ﴾ قال ابن عباس أدخلكم الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p73#2/r2.claim: The command to fear God means to fear Him alone.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r1.claim: God commands the Israelites to enter Islam and follow Muhammad, urging them to emulate their forefather Israel, the prophet Jacob, in following truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى آمرا بني إسرائيل بالدخول في الإسلام، ومتابعة محمد عليه من الله أفضل الصلاة والسلام، ومهيجا لهم بذكر أبيهم إسرائيل، وهو نبي الله يعقوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir links this appeal to the description of those carried with Noah as descendants, citing the parallel address in 17:3.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك أيضا قوله تعالى: {ذرية من حملنا مع نوح إنه كان عبدا شكورا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet asked a group of Jews whether Israel was Jacob, they affirmed it, and he called God as witness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن عباس قال: حضرت عصابة من اليهود نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لهم: "هل تعلمون أن إسرائيل يعقوب؟ ". قالوا: اللهم نعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r4.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas explains Israel as a name meaning the same as saying Abdullah, servant of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241/r4.anchor: وقال الأعمش، عن إسماعيل بن رجاء، عن عمير مولى ابن عباس، عن عبد الله بن عباس؛ أن إسرائيل كقولك: عبد الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
