IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies God's blessings as those named and others, including making the stone gush, sending manna and quail, and saving Israel from Pharaoh's bondage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: نعمة الله التي أنعم بها عليهم فيما سمى وفيما سوى ذلك، فجر لهم الحجر، وأنزل عليهم المن والسلوى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God blessed them by making prophets and messengers among them and revealing scriptures to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: نعمته أن جعل منهم الأنبياء والرسل، وأنزل عليهم الكتب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir equates this with Moses' reminder that God made Israel prophets and kings and gave them gifts unmatched in their time, citing 5:20.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r3.anchor: وهذا كقول موسى عليه السلام لهم: {يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn Ishaq, calls the blessing God's favor to them and their ancestors in rescuing them from Pharaoh and his people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم} أي: بلائي عندكم وعند آبائكم لما كان نجاهم به من فرعون وقومه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the covenant was the pledge taken from Israel to follow the Prophet when he came.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's fulfillment of the covenant as fulfilling His promise if they affirm and follow the Prophet, lifting the burdens imposed for their sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r6.anchor: {أوف بعهدكم} أي: أنجز لكم ما وعدتكم عليه بتصديقه واتباعه، بوضع ما كان عليكم من الإصر والأغلال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God's covenant with His servants is the religion of Islam, which they must follow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: {وأوفوا بعهدي} قال: عهده إلى عباده: دينه الإسلام أن يتبعوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p241#2/r8.claim: From Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak says fulfilling God's covenant means that God will be pleased with them and admit them to Paradise.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r1.speaker: السدي والضحاك وأبو العالية والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r1.claim: These authorities are said to share the preceding interpretation of God's fulfilling the covenant by being pleased with Israel and admitting them to Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r1.anchor: وكذا قال السدي، والضحاك، وأبو العالية، والربيع بن أنس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r2.speaker: أبو العالية والسدي والربيع بن أنس وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya, al-Suddi, al-Rabi ibn Anas, and Qatada explain فارهبون as fear Me.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r2.anchor: قاله أبو العالية، والسدي، والربيع بن أنس، وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas warns that fearing God means fearing punishment like the calamities inflicted on earlier ancestors, including their transformation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {وإياي فارهبون} أي أنزل بكم ما أنزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir describes a shift from encouragement to warning, intended to draw Israel back to truth, following the messenger, learning from Qur'anic warnings, obeying commands, and believing its reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p242/r4.anchor: وهذا انتقال من الترغيب إلى الترهيب، فدعاهم إليه بالرغبة والرهبة، لعلهم يرجعون إلى الحق واتباع الرسول والاتعاظ بالقرآن

NAHHAS:v1p216/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r6.claim: بني إسرائيل is a construct vocative: بني derives from ابن, yāʾ marks the accusative, and nūn is omitted for annexation; retaining it would give بنا like عصا.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r6.anchor: نداء مضاف علامة النصب فيه الياء وحذفت منه النون للإضافة الواحد ابن

NAHHAS:v1p216/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r7.claim: Deriving the deleted letter as wāw from البنوة is no proof, since الفتوة also has wāw; Abū Isḥāq says the deleted letter is yāʾ, from بنيت.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r7.anchor: فمن قال المحذوف منه واو احتج بقولهم البنوة وهذا لا حجة فيه لأنهم قد قالوا الفتوة

NAHHAS:v1p216/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p216/r8.claim: He says the deleted letter in بني is yāʾ, as though derived from بنيت.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r8.anchor: سمعت أبا إسحاق يقول المحذوف منه عندي ياء كأنه من بنيت

NAHHAS:v1p216/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r9.claim: إسرائيل is genitive but diptote because it is foreign; variants include إسرائل without yāʾ, إسراأل with a fatha hamza, and Tamim's إسرائين with nūn.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r9.anchor: ( إسرائيل ) في موضع خفض إلا أنه لا ينصرف لعجومته ويقال إسرائل بغير ياء

NAHHAS:v1p216/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r10.claim: اذكروا drops its nūn as an imperative and its alif because it is a connecting alif; it begins with ḍamma because it derives from يذكر.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r10.anchor: ( اذكروا ) حذفت النون منه لأنه أمر وحذفت الألف لأنها ألف وصل

NAHHAS:v1p216/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r11.claim: The yāʾ in نعمتي is usually vowelled before alif-lām; if left still it drops where two sukūns meet. التي is its adjective and أنعمت عليكم its relative clause.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r11.anchor: ( نعمتي التي ) بتحريك الياء أكثر في كلام العرب إذا لقيها ألف ولام

NAHHAS:v1p216/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r12.claim: أوفوا بعهدي is an imperative; أوف بعهدكم is its jussive response because the command carries conditional meaning, and وفى بالعهد is another verb form.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r12.anchor: ( وأوفوا بعهدي ) أمر ( أوف بعهدكم ) جواب الأمر مجزوم لأن فيه معنى المجازاة

NAHHAS:v1p216/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r13.speaker: الزهري
NAHHAS:v1p216/r13.claim: He reads أوف بعهدكم with a doubled fāʾ for intensive meaning.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r13.anchor: وقرأ الزهري ( أوف بعهدكم ) على التكثير ويقال وفى بالعهد أيضا

NAHHAS:v1p216/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p216/r14.claim: In وإياي فارهبون, the verb takes the nūn and yāʾ, with yāʾ omitted at the verse ending; إياي is accusative with an elided verb, preferred in commands, prohibitions, negatives, and questions.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r14.anchor: ( وإياي فارهبون ) وقع الفعل على النون والياء وحذفت الياء لأنه رأس آية

NAHHAS:v1p216/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p216/r15.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p216/r15.claim: He reads فارهبوني with the yāʾ retained, and similarly فاتقوني.
NAHHAS:v1p216/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( فارهبوني ) بالياء وكذا فاتقوني

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r1.claim: The common reading lengthens and hamzas Isrāʾīl, treating it as indeclinable; the author calls this the most eloquent and best form.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة إسرائيل ممدود مهموز ممتنع، وهو الأفصح والأحسن

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r2.speaker: الحسن والزهري
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī read Isrāʾīl without hamza or lengthening.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن والزهري إسرايل بغير همز، ولا مد

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r3.speaker: الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar lengthen after the yāʾ but omit hamza.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r3.anchor: وعن الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر إسراييل بمدة بعد الياء بغير همز

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r4.speaker: ورش
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r4.claim: Warsh pronounces the hamza with elision.

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash records forms without the yāʾ, imāla, and Qutrub records Isrāl without hamza or yāʾ, Israʾīn with nūn, and the common Israel.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r5.anchor: حكى الأخفش: إسرائل بكسر الهمزة من غير ياء، وحكى: إسراءل بفتح الهمزة من غير ياء

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r6.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r6.claim: All readers omit the yāʾ in farhabūn in conformity with the codex and ease; Yaʿqūb retains it according to the original form.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r6.anchor: وأجمعوا على حذف الياء من قوله: (فارهبون) اتباعا للمصحف، ولأنه أخف

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r7.claim: Israel is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham; alternatively the Hebrew compound means “servant of God,” or “God’s chosen one.”
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r7.anchor: إسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم عليهم السلام، وقيل: إن أصل الاسم مضاف

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r8.claim: Ibn is specific to a son, while walad includes sons and daughters; ibn derives from building because the father is the son’s foundation, and adoptive sonship is figurative.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r8.anchor: والابن والولد نظيران غير أن الابن تخصيص الذكور دون الإناث، والولد يجمعهما

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r9.claim: Dhikr can mean remembrance, spoken mention, renown, scripture detailing religion, or prayer; its root sense is directing attention to something.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r9.anchor: والذكر الحفظ للشيء، وضده النسيان، والذكر: جري الشيء على لسانك، والذكر: الشرف والصيت

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r10.claim: A blessing is a benefit that reaches someone with good intended; obligation, fulfillment, and completion are near-synonyms, and awfaytuhu is a Tihāma form used in the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r10.anchor: والنعمة: هي النفع الواصل إليه إذا قصد به الخير، أنعم عليه وأنعمت عليه

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r11.claim: ʿAhd means either a command or a testament; rahba is fear or apprehension, as in the proverb that fear is better than mercy.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r11.anchor: والعهد: الأمر، والعهد: الوصية. والرهبة: الخوف والخشية، ومنه الراهب

JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r12.claim: The author treats fear as rooted in belief: belief in harm prompts avoidance, while belief in benefit prompts action and desire.
JISHUMI:v1p347#2/r12.anchor: فمن اعتقد في شيء ضررا دعاه إلى اجتنابه، فهو رهبة، ومن اعتقد فيه نفعا دعاه إلى فعله، فهو رغبة

JISHUMI:v1p349/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r1.claim: The object pronoun iyyāya is not governed directly by farhabūn because the verb already contains a pronoun; an understood verb is supplied and explained by the expressed one.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r1.anchor: لا، لكن بما دل عليه لأنه مشغول بالضمير، كما لا يجوز: زيدا فاضربه

JISHUMI:v1p349/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r2.claim: The yāʾ in niʿmatī is vowelled before the article rather than dropped, preserving the original and fitting the resumed alif of waṣl; vocative yā ʿibādī normally drops the possessive attachment.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r2.anchor: فكان التحريك أولى؛ لأنه أدل على الأصل، وأشكل بما يلزم اللام في الاستئناف من فتح ألف الوصل

JISHUMI:v1p349/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p349/r3.claim: The verse was revealed about Jews and Christians living in the Prophet’s time; another report treats it as general, and another specifies Jews and Christians.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r3.anchor: قيل: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى الذين كانوا في عصر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقيل: هو عام

JISHUMI:v1p349/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p349/r4.claim: The address to the children of Israel means the children of Jacob and is directed to Jewish scholars around Medina.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r4.anchor: يعني يا بني يعقوب، نسبهم إلى الأب الأعلى، كما قال: يا بني آدم والمخاطب بهذا قيل: أحبار اليهود الذين كانوا حول المدينة

JISHUMI:v1p349/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r5.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p349/r5.claim: An alternative says the addressees are all Jews and Christians.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r5.anchor: وقيل: جميع اليهود والنصارى، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p349/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r6.claim: The singular niʿma denotes the whole class of blessings, as in the verse saying God’s blessings cannot be counted.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r6.anchor: أراد به النعم التي خصهم بها، وأراد الجنس وإن ذكر بلفظ الواحد

JISHUMI:v1p349/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r7.claim: One explanation includes blessings given to their ancestors: prophets, scriptures, and rescue from the flood and Pharaoh; Arabic can attribute ancestors’ deeds to descendants.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r7.anchor: ما أنعم به على أسلافهم من الرسل والكتب وأنجاهم من الغرق ومن فرعون وغير ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p349/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r8.claim: Another explanation lists blessings reaching them directly: preservation through their ancestors, creation, faculties and guidance to infer God’s unity, sound senses, continuing provision, protection from harm, and religious and worldly favors.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r8.anchor: النعم الواصلة إليهم نحو تبقية آبائهم حتى تناسلوا، وخلقهم لينفعهم ويمكنهم بالآلات والقدرة والهداية

JISHUMI:v1p349/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p349/r9.claim: The covenant is obedience to God and abstention from disobedience concerning the Prophet; God’s covenant is admission to Paradise, and the earlier scriptures made this commitment.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r9.anchor: ما أمرتكم به من طاعتي ونهيتكم عن معصيتي في النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أوف بعهدكم أدخلكم الجنة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p349/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p349/r10.claim: Another view identifies the covenant with the pledge in the verse about God’s covenant with Israel and appointment of twelve leaders.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r10.anchor: هو ما عهد إليهم في سورة المائدة في قوله: (ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا) الآية إلى آخرها، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v1p349/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p349/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p349/r11.claim: Another view takes the covenant as all commands and prohibitions; a further view says it was the Torah and Gospel’s prophecy about the Messenger that they concealed.
JISHUMI:v1p349/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو جميع الأوامر والنواهي، وقيل: هو ما عهد إليهم في التوراة والإنجيل في أمر رسول الله فكتموه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r1.claim: Israel is Jacob, peace be upon him; the name is his title and means God's chosen in their language.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r1.anchor: هو يعقوب عليه السلام لقب له ومعناه في لسانهم صفوة الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r2.claim: An alternative gloss gives Israel the meaning servant of God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r2.anchor: ومعناه في لسانهم صفوة الله وقيل عبد الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r3.claim: Israel follows the morphological pattern of Abraham and Ishmael and is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r3.anchor: وهو بزنة إبراهيم وإسماعيل غير منصرف مثلهما لوجود العلمية والعجمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r4.claim: Two variant pronunciations of Israel are read.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r5.claim: Remembering the blessing requires gratitude, recognition and magnification of it, and obedience to its giver.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r5.anchor: وذكرهم النعمة ان لا يخلو بشكرها ويعتدوا بها ويستعظموها ويطيعوا مانحها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r6.claim: The blessings include the ancestors' rescue from Pharaoh and drowning, forgiveness after the calf, and their repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r6.anchor: من الإنجاء من فرعون وعذابه ومن الغرق ومن العفو عن إتخاذ العجل والتوبة عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r7.claim: The blessing also includes their reaching Muhammad's time, since the Torah and Gospel had announced him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r7.anchor: وما أنعم به عليهم من إدراك زمن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم المبشر به في التوراة والإنجيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r8.claim: A covenant may be grammatically ascribed to either covenanting party: fulfilling one's covenant means fulfilling what one pledged, while fulfilling another's means the promise made to that person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r8.anchor: والعهد يضاف إلى المعاهد والمعاهد جميعا يقال أوفيت بعهدي أي عاهدت عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r9.claim: The Israelites must fulfill their pledge to believe in God and obey Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r9.anchor: واوفوا بما عاهدتموني عليه من الإيمان بي والطاعة لي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r10.claim: God's fulfillment of His covenant means granting the excellent reward for their good deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r10.anchor: بما عاهدتكم عليه من حسن الثواب على حسناتكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r11.claim: Fearing God means not breaking His covenant; the fronted object gives stronger exclusivity than in the expression You alone we worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r11.anchor: فلا تنقضوا عهدي وهو من قولك زيدا رهبته وهو اوكد في افادة الاختصاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r12.claim: A reading with a doubled f intensifies the promise: God will fulfill the covenant abundantly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r12.anchor: وقرىء ( واوف ) بالتشديد أي أبالغ في الوفاء بعهدكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r13.claim: The covenant may specifically mean their pledge to believe in the Prophet of Mercy and the miraculous Scripture, as the following command to believe indicates.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p159/r13.anchor: ما عاهدوا عليه ووعدوه من الإيمان بنبي الرحمة والكتاب المعجز ويدل عليه قوله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r1.claim: Israel is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r1.anchor: وإسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the Hebrew elements Isra as servant and Il as God, yielding the name Abd Allah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ( إسرا ) بالعبرانية : عبد , و ( إيل ) هو الله , فكان اسمه عبد الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r3.claim: Dhikr has several senses: recollection in the heart, speech by the tongue as opposed to silence, and honor; the verse means remembering God's favor inwardly, without neglecting or forgetting it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r3.anchor: والذكر اسم مشترك , فالذكر بالقلب ضد النسيان , والذكر باللسان ضد الإنصات , والذكر الشرف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r4.speaker: الكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says dhikr referring to the heart has a damma on its dhāl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي : ما كان بالقلب فهو مضموم الذال , وقال غيره : هو لغتان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r5.claim: Others treat dhikr and dhakr as two dialect forms with the same meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r5.anchor: وقال غيره : هو لغتان : ذكر وذكر , ومعناهما واحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r6.claim: Blessings may mean God's favors generally, or, according to al-Hasan, favors to the ancestors: rescue from Pharaoh, prophets, scripture, water from the rock, and manna and quails; their descendants inherit their ancestors' honor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r6.anchor: والثاني : وهو قول الحسن البصري , أنه أراد نعمه على آبائهم , إذ نجاهم من آل فرعون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r7.claim: One reading takes the blessings as God's favors to all His creatures, as in the verse saying His blessing cannot be counted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r7.anchor: أحدهما : عموم نعمه التي أنعم بها على خلقه , كما قال تعالى : ^ { وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها } ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r8.claim: Fulfilling the covenant may mean honoring the pact to believe God and affirm His messengers, in return for the promised Garden.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r8.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي الذي أخذت عليكم من الميثاق , أن تؤمنوا بي وتصدقوا رسلي , أوف بعهدكم على ما وعدتكم من الجنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the command as obeying what God ordered, with God fulfilling what He promised.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r9.anchor: والثاني : قاله عبد الله بن عباس : أوفوا بما أمرتكم , أوف بما وعدتكم إياه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r10.claim: The covenant is so called either because it was stipulated in earlier scriptures or because it resembles an oath, both requiring fulfillment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p110/r10.anchor: وفي تسمية ذلك عهدا قولان : أحدهما : لأنه عهده في الكتب السالفة . والثاني : أنه جعله كالعهد , الذي هو يمين

MUQATIL:2:40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:40/r1.claim: The favor recalled to Israel's ancestors includes rescue from Pharaoh, destruction of their enemy, the parted sea, manna and quails, shade, a night light, twelve springs, and the Torah's guidance to worship God alone.
MUQATIL:2:40/r1.anchor: فكانت النعمة حين أنجاهم من آل فرعون، وأهلك عدوهم، وحين فرق البحر لهم، وحين أنزل عليهم المن والسلوى،

MUQATIL:2:40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:40/r2.claim: Israel's covenant in the Torah required worshipping God without partners and believing in Muhammad, the prophets, and the Scripture; the cited covenant also enjoins prayer, almsgiving, supporting messengers, and a good loan.
MUQATIL:2:40/r2.anchor: عهد إليهم فى التوراة أن يعبدوه ولا يشركوا به شيئا، وأن يؤمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:2:40/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:40/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:40/r3.claim: If Israel fulfilled the covenant, God promised forgiveness and Paradise; the passage in 5:12 is cited as God's fulfillment of that promise.
MUQATIL:2:40/r3.anchor: يعنى المغفرة والجنة، فعاهدهم إن أوفوا له بما قال المغفرة والجنة،

MUQATIL:2:40/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:40/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:40/r4.claim: Israel instead disbelieved in Muhammad and Jesus, and fearing God means fearing Him concerning Muhammad, since whoever denies Muhammad faces Hell.
MUQATIL:2:40/r4.anchor: فكفروا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وبعيسى، عليه السلام،

MUQATIL:2:40/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:40/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:40/r5.claim: The command to fear God is specifically about Muhammad: whoever denies him will be in Hell.
MUQATIL:2:40/r5.anchor: وإياى فخافون فى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمن كذب به فله النار.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.claim: Israel is Jacob's title; in their language it means either God's chosen one or God's servant, with Israel formed from a word for servant/chosen and El for God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r1.anchor: هو يعقوب عليه السلام وهو لقب له ومعناه فى لسانهم صفوة الله أو عبد الله فإسرا هو العبد أو الصفوة وإيل هو الله بالعبرية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.claim: Israel is indeclinable because it combines proper-name status with foreign origin.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r2.anchor: وهو غير منصرف لوجود العليمة والعجمة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.claim: Recalling blessings should lead them to thank God and obey the giver; the blessings include their ancestors' rescue from Pharaoh and drowning, pardon for the calf, and acceptance of repentance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r3.anchor: ذكرهم النعمة أن لا يخلوا بشكرها ويطيعوا مانحها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.claim: A further blessing was that they lived to see Muhammad, whose coming was announced in the Torah and Gospel.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r4.anchor: وما أنعم به عليهم من إدراك زمن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم المبشر به فى التوراة والإنجيل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r5.claim: The chosen form of the verb means to discharge a covenant completely; although both forms are used, this one is the preferred usage and Qur'anic form.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.claim: The covenant to be fulfilled means either faith in God and obedience to Him or faith in the Prophet of mercy and the miraculous Book.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r6.anchor: من الإيمان بى والطاعة لى أو من الإيمان بنبى الرحمة والكتاب المعجز

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.claim: God's covenant in return is the good reward promised for good deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r7.anchor: بما عاهدتكم عليه من حسن الثواب على حسناتكم والعهد يضاف إلى المعاهد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.claim: Qatadah interprets the covenant as a promise: if you uphold it, God will forgive you.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r8.anchor: وعن قتادة هما لئن أقمتم ولأكفرن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.speaker: أهل الإشارة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.claim: The people of allusion read the covenant mystically: serve reverently in the abode of trial and receive the joy of divine vision in the abode of grace.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r9.anchor: وقال أهل الإشارة أوفوا فى دار محنتى على بساط خدمتى بحفظ حرمتى أوف فى دار نعمتى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r10.claim: Fear God alone and do not break the covenant; fronting the object gives stronger restriction than the wording of You alone we worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r10.anchor: فلا تنقضوا عهدى وهو من قولك زيدا رهبته وهو أوكد فى إفادة الاختصاص من إياك نعبد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r11.claim: An implied first verb governs the fronted object; it is omitted because the following verb indicates it, and that following verb already takes its object pronoun.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p40#2/r11.anchor: وإياي منصوب بفعل مضمر دل عليه ما بعده وتقديره فارهبوا إياي فارهبون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r1.claim: The vocative Banī Isrāʾīl has an accusative yāʾ and drops its nūn through annexation; ibn has disputed underlying yāʾ or wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r1.anchor: نداء مضاف، علامة النصب فيه الياء، وحذفت منه النون للإضافة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r2.speaker: الزجاج والأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the lost letter in ibn is yāʾ, from banaytu; al-Akhfash prefers wāw because it is more often deleted due to its heaviness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المحذوف منه عندي ياء كأنه من بنيت. الأخفش: اختار أن يكون المحذوف منه الواو لأن حذفها أكثر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r3.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records two dialect forms of the vocative, yā banī and yā bunayya, like yā abati; both were read.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: يا بني ويا بني لغتان، مثل يا أبت ويا أبت وقرىء بهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r4.claim: Ibn is derived from building: a son is a branch placed upon his father.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r4.anchor: وهو مشتق من البناء وهو وضع الشيء على الشيء والابن فرع للأب وهو موضوع عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r5.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r5.claim: Abū al-Faraj al-Jawzī says Israel is the only prophet besides Muḥammad to have two names, with Muḥammad having many names.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r5.anchor: قال أبو الفرج الجوزي: وليس في الأنبياء من له اسمان غيره، إلا نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن له أسماء كثيرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r6.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad lists five prophets with paired names: Muḥammad/Aḥmad, ʿĪsā/al-Masīḥ, Israel/Yaʿqūb, Yūnus/Dhū al-Nūn, and Ilyās/Dhū al-Kifl; Qurtubi notes multiple names for ʿĪsā and Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r6.anchor: عن الخليل بن أحمد: خمسة من الأنبياء ذوو اسمين، محمد وأحمد نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم، وعيسى والمسيح، وإسرائيل ويعقوب، ويونس وذو النون، وإلياس وذو الكفل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r7.claim: Israel is a foreign proper name and therefore indeclinable, here genitive through annexation; Qurtubi lists seven pronounced forms, including the Quranic form and a partly lengthened hamza variant transmitted by Shanbūdh from Warsh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r7.anchor: وإسرائيل: اسم أعجمي، ولذلك لم ينصرف وهو في موضع خفض بالإضافة. وفيه سبع لغات: إسرائيل، وهي لغة القرآن. وإسرائيل، بمدة مهموزة مختلسة، حكاها شنبوذ عن ورش.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r8.speaker: الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر والحسن والزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read Israʾīl with lengthened yāʾ and no hamza; al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī read without hamza or lengthening, alongside other hamza and Tamīm variants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r8.anchor: وإسراييل، بمدة بعد الياء من غير همز، وهي قراءة الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر وقرأ الحسن والزهري بغير همز ولا مد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains Israel as servant of God, taking Isra as servant and Īl as God; other etymologies make Isra mean God’s chosen or one tightly formed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r9.anchor: ومعنى إسرائيل: عبد الله. قال ابن عباس: إسرا بالعبرانية هو عبد، وإيل هو الله. وقيل: إسرا هو صفوة الله، وإيل هو الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r10.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r10.claim: Al-Suhaylī derives Israel from a night journey in migration toward God, making the name a partly Hebrew and partly Arabic formation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r10.anchor: وقال السهيلي: سمي إسرائيل لأنه أسرى ذات ليلة حين هاجر إلى الله تعالى فسمي إسرائيل أي أسرى إلى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r11.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r11.claim: Dhikr can mean remembrance of the heart or speech opposed to silence; al-Kisāʾī assigns ḍamma to inward remembrance and kasra to spoken remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40/r11.anchor: قال الكسائي: ما كان بالضمير فهو مضموم الذال، وما كان باللسان فهو مكسور الذال.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.claim: Dhikr with fatḥ means the opposite of female and can also mean honor, as in the verse calling the message an honor to the Prophet and his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r1.anchor: والذكر بفتح الذال خلاف الأنثى. والذكر أيضا الشرف ومنه قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says remember My favor means remember gratitude for it, with thanksgiving elided; another explanation, which Qurtubi finds good, means keep the favor in heart and do not forget it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: والمعنى في الآية اذكروا شكر نعمتي فحذف الشكر اكتفاء بذكر النعمة. وقيل: إنه أراد الذكر بالقلب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.claim: Niʿma is a generic singular with plural sense; Israel’s favors included rescue from Pharaoh, prophets, scripture, manna and quail, water from the rock, and Torah’s description of Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r3.anchor: والنعمة هنا اسم جنس، فهي مفردة بمعنى الجمع، قال الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.claim: Favors granted to the ancestors are favors to descendants because descendants share their ancestors’ honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r4.anchor: والنعم على الآباء نعم على الأبناء لأنهم يشرفون بشرف آبائهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.speaker: أرباب المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.claim: The people of spiritual meanings say Israel is led from favor to the Benefactor, while Muḥammad’s community is led from the Benefactor to the favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r5.anchor: قال أرباب المعاني: ربط سبحانه وتعالى بني إسرائيل بذكر النعمة وأسقطه عن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ودعاهم إلى ذكره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads ūfi with fatḥa on the wāw and a doubled fāʾ to express intensity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: «أوف» بفتح الواو وشد الفاء للتكثير.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the covenant with commands to take revelation firmly and the covenant taken from Israel’s twelve tribal leaders.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r7.anchor:
فقال الحسن: عهده قوله:
خذوا مآ آتيناكم بقوة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Israel’s covenant is to follow Muḥammad as described in the Torah, and God’s covenant in return is Paradise if they fulfill it.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.claim: Other views identify the covenant with explaining scripture, sincere performance of duties, worship and spiritual care, or preserving outward manners and adorning the inner self.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r9.anchor: وقيل هو قوله: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.claim: Qurtubi prefers the majority’s general reading: fulfillment of all God’s commands, prohibitions, and counsels, including recognition of Muḥammad, with God’s covenant being admission to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r10.anchor: هذا قول الجمهور من العلماء، وهو الصحيح. وعهده سبحانه وتعالى هو أن يدخلهم الجنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r11.claim: The covenant’s demand also applies to Muslims; their keeping it signals God’s fulfillment, not a cause of it, since His action is gracious favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#2/r11.anchor: قلت: وما طلب من هؤلاء من الوفاء بالعهد هو مطلوب منا قال الله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.claim: Fārbahūnī means fear Me; the command carries a threat, and the final yāʾ is omitted because it ends a verse; Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads it with yāʾ retained.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r1.anchor: أي خافون. والرهب والرهب والرهبة: الخوف. ويتضمن الأمر به معنى التهديد. وسقطت الياء بعد النون لأنها رأس آية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.claim: Iyyāya is accusative with an implied verb, as preferred in commands, prohibitions, and questions; a nominal construction is also possible with ‘I am your Lord’ understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:40#3/r2.anchor: «وإياي» منصوب بإضمار فعل، وكذا الاختيار في الأمر والنهي والاستفهام التقدير

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r1.claim: بني is a vocative with yāʾ marking accusative and its nūn deleted in the construct; because its singular changes, Arabs partly treat it like a broken plural and use feminine agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r1.anchor: بني " منادى وعلامة نصبه الياء لأنه جمع مذكر سالم وحذفت نونه للإضافة، وهو شبيه بجمع التكسير

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r2.claim: The feminine verb with بنو is illustrated by the poet's قالت بنو عامر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r2.anchor:
فألحقوا في فعله المسند إليه تاء التأنيث نحو: قالت بنو فلان، وقال الشاعر:
400 قالت بنو عامر

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r3.claim: بنو may also receive case endings like a broken plural; the cited line has the nūn of بنين in the nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r3.anchor:
الشاعر:
401 وكان لنا أبو حسن علي
أبا برا ونحن له بنين
برفع النون

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r4.claim: بني ends in yāʾ because it derives from البناء: a son is a branch built on his father; the alternative derives it from البنوة like الأبوة and الأخوة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r4.anchor: الصحيح الأول، وأما البنوة فلا دلالة فيها لأنهم قد قالوا: الفتوة، ولا خلاف أنها من ذوات الياء

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash favors the waw derivation because deleting waw is more frequent; the author answers that البنوة is no proof, since الفتوة is unquestionably from yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r5.anchor: إلا أن الأخفش رجح الثاني بأن حذف الواو أكثر. واختلف في وزنه

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r6.claim: The word بني is analyzed either with fatḥa or sukūn on its middle radical.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r6.anchor: واختلف في وزنه فقيل: بني بفتح العين وقيل بني بسكونها

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r7.claim: بني is one of ten nouns whose first radical is silent and whose lost final radical is compensated by initial hamzat al-waṣl.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم أنه أحد الأسماء العشرة التي سكنت فاؤها وعوض من لامها همزة الوصل

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r8.claim: إسرائيل is genitive by annexation and indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name, built as an iḍāfa: إسرا means servant and إيل means God.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r8.anchor: وإسرائيل: خفض بالإضافة، ولا ينصرف للعلمية والعجمة، وهو مركب تركيب الإضافة مثل: عبد الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r9.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r9.claim: Another derivation takes إسرا from strength, so Israel means one whom God strengthened.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r9.anchor: وقيل: " إسرا " مشتق من الأسر وهو القوة، فكأن معناه: الذي قواه الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r10.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r10.claim: One account says Israel was named because he traveled by night as a migrant to God.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r10.anchor: وقيل لأنه أسري بالليل مهاجرا إلى الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r11.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r11.claim: Another account says he captured a jinn that used to extinguish the lamp of Jerusalem.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r11.anchor: وقيل: لأنه أسر جنيا كان يطفئ سراج بيت المقدس

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r12.claim: On the jinn account, some say the name is partly Arabic and partly foreign.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r12.anchor: قال بعضهم: فعلى هذا يكون الاسم عربيا وبعضه أعجميا

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r13.claim: Arabic speakers used many forms of Israel, but the majority's Qur'anic form is the most eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r13.anchor: وقد تصرفت فيه العرب بلغات كثيرة أفصحها لغة القرآن وهي قراءة الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and al-Aʿmash read إسرائل with yāʾ after the alif and no hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r14.anchor:
وكان لنا أبو حسن علي
أبا برا ونحن

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r15.speaker: ورش
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r15.claim: Warsh is reported to read إسرائل with hamza after the alif but no yāʾ, and also اسرأل, اسرئل, and إسرال with differing hamza or alif forms.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r15.anchor: وروي عن ورش: إسرائل بهمزة بعد الألف دون ياء، واسرأل بهمزة مفتوحة بين الراء واللام

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r16.claim: The poem's form إسرال witnesses a reported Nafiʿ reading with a plain alif between rāʾ and lām.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r16.anchor:
وإسرال بألف محضة بين الراء واللام، قال الشاعر:
402 لا أرى من يعينني

SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r17.claim: The form إسرائين replaces lām with nūn, by analogy with أصيلان for أصيلال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40/r17.anchor: أبدلوا من اللام نونا كأصيلان في أصيلال

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r1.claim: The cited poem witnesses the form إسرائينا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r1.anchor:
قالت وكنت رجلا فطينا
هذا ورب البيت إسرائينا

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r2.claim: Israel's plural is أساريل; Kufans also allow أسارلة or أسارل, with or without compensatory letters, like فرازنة and فرازين.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r2.anchor: ويجمع على " أساريل ". وأجاز الكوفيون: أسارلة، وأسارل، كأنهم يجيزون التعويض وعدمه

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r3.speaker: الصفار
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r3.claim: Al-Saffar says he knows nobody who permits deleting the initial hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r3.anchor: قال الصفار: " لا نعلم أحدا يجيز حذف الهمزة من أوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r4.claim: اذكروا is a verb with an understood subject and نعمتي its object; Ibn al-Anbari instead supplies the omitted construct noun شكر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r4.anchor: اذكروا فعل وفاعل، ونعمتي مفعول، وقال ابن الأنباري: " لا بد من حذف مضاف تقديره: شكر نعمتي

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r5.claim: ذكر and ذِكر with kasra or ḍamma may mean the same and may refer to tongue or heart; al-Kisaʾi assigns kasra to tongue and ḍamma to heart, opposed respectively by silence and forgetfulness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r5.anchor: والذكر والذكر بكسر الذال وضمها بمعنى واحد، ويكونان باللسان وبالجنان. وقال الكسائي: " هو بالكسر للسان وبالضم للقلب

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r6.claim: Regardless of whether the vocalizations share a meaning, heart-remembrance opposes forgetfulness and tongue-remembrance opposes silence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r6.anchor: فالذكر الذي محله القلب ضده النسيان، والذي محله اللسان ضده الصمت

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r7.claim: نعمة is what is bestowed as favor, like passive-form nouns ذبح and رعي; as a generic noun it can denote favors collectively, as 14:34 does.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r7.anchor: والنعمة: اسم لما ينعم به وهي شبيهة بفعل بمعنى مفعول نحو: ذبح ورعي، والمراد بها الجمع لأنها اسم جنس

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r8.claim: التي is an adjective modifying نعمة with its resumptive pronoun omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r8.anchor: و { التي أنعمت } صفتها والعائد محذوف. فإن قيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r9.claim: Though deletion of a genitive resumptive usually requires matching preposition and governor, the author derives أنعمتها by first dropping the preposition and making its object accusative; compare one reading of 9:69.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r9.anchor: فإن الأصل: التي أنعمت بها، فالجواب أنه إنما حذف بعد أن صار منصوبا بحذف حرف الجر اتساعا فبقي: أنعمتها

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#2/r10.claim: عليكم attaches to أنعمت and على indicates that the favor comprehensively reaches them.

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r1.claim: وأوفوا بعهدي is an imperative clause coordinated with the preceding imperative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r1.anchor: هذه جملة أمرية عطف على الأمرية قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r2.claim: أوفى, وفى with shadda, and وفى without shadda are three synonymous forms; the poem combines أوفى and وفى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r2.anchor:
ويقال: أوفى ووفى ووفى مشددا ومخففا، ثلاث لغات بمعنى، قال الشاعر:
404 أما ابن طوق فقد أوفى بذمته
كما وفى

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r3.claim: Usage says أوفيت and وفيت بالعهد, but only أوفيت الكيل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r3.anchor: ويقال: أوفيت وفيت بالعهد وأوفيت الكيل لا غير

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r4.claim: Some say all three forms occur in the Qur'an: أوفى here, وفّى in 53:37, and ungeminated وفى inferred from 9:111 because the elative is normally built from a triliteral; the inference is attributed to al-Shatibi, though the rule is debated.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r4.anchor:
وعن بعضهم أن اللغات الثلاث واردة في القرآن، أما " أوفى " فكهذه الآية، وأما " وفى " بالتشديد فكقوله:
وإبراهيم الذي وفى

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r5.claim: أوفى can also mean rose or became elevated, as the cited line uses أوفيت.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r5.anchor:
ويجيء " أوفى " بمعنى ارتفع، قال:
405 ربما أوفيت في علم

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r6.claim: عهد is a verbal noun that may be annexed to the subject or object: either God's covenant that they accept obedience, like 36:60, or their pledge to God, like 48:10 and 33:23.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r6.anchor: والعهد مصدر، ويحتمل إضافته للفاعل أو المفعول. والمعنى: بما عاهدتكم عليه من قبول الطاعة

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r7.claim: أوف is jussive as the جواب to the command; grammarians differ whether the request itself triggers the jussive through conditional force or an elided شرط such as إن توفوا بعهدي does.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r7.anchor: أوف " مجزوم على جواب الأمر، وهل الجازم الجملة الطلبية نفسها لما تضمنته من معنى الشرط، أو حرف شرط مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r8.claim: بعهدكم attaches to أوف, and عهدكم likewise permits annexation to the subject or object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#3/r8.anchor: متعلق به، وهو محتمل للإضافة إلى الفاعل أو المفعول كما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r1.claim: إياي is a detached accusative pronoun, whose analysis was discussed in the treatment of al-Fatiha.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r1.anchor: ضمير منصوب منفصل، وقد عرف ما فيه من الفاتحة

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r2.claim: An omitted verb explained by فارهبون governs إياي; the author places that verb after the pronoun because placing it before would be awkward given the separation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r2.anchor: ونصبه بفعل محذوف يفسره الظاهر بعده، والتقدير: " وإياي ارهبوا فارهبون

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r3.claim: Some grammarians estimate ارهبوا before إياي, though the author prefers a postposed estimate.

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r4.claim: One analysis takes the fāʾ as the answer to an implied command such as تنبهوا; an analogy is زيدا فاضرب, with object fronting to avoid beginning the utterance with fāʾ and the fāʾ linking the clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r4.anchor: والفاء في " فارهبون " فيها قولان للنحويين، أحدهما: أنها جواب أمر مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r5.claim: A second grammatical analysis treats the fāʾ in فارهبون as extra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني في هذه الفاء: أنها زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r6.claim: The Sheikh's first refinement estimates وإياي ارهبوا تنبهوا فارهبون, so fāʾ directly answers the command rather than being displaced by fronting.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r6.anchor: وقال الشيخ بعد أن حكى القول الأول: " فتحتمل الآية وجهين أحدهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r7.claim: The Sheikh's second refinement begins with وتنبهوا فارهبون, omits the imperative, then fronts the object and shifts fāʾ to avoid its appearing first, yielding وإياي فارهبوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r7.anchor: زائدة. وقال الشيخ بعد أن حكى القول الأول

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r8.claim: On the second refinement, فإياي is governed by the following verb, and the repeated pronoun supplies emphasis and completes the verse ending; detached and attached pronouns may emphasize one another.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r8.anchor: زائدة. وقال الشيخ بعد أن حكى القول الأول

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r9.claim: The author raises an objection to the Sheikh's second construction, ending his discussion with وفيه نظر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r9.anchor:
المتصل بالمنفصل، وفيه نظر.
والرهب والرهب والرهبة: الخوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r10.claim: الرهب, الرهب, and الرهبة mean fear, from الرهابة, a chest bone affected by fear.
SAMIN-DURR:2:40#4/r10.anchor: والرهب والرهب والرهبة: الخوف، مأخوذ من الرهابة وهي عظم في الصدر يؤثر فيه الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r1.claim: After proving divine unity, prophethood, and resurrection and recalling universal favors, God recalls special favors to Israel’s ancestors to break Jewish obstinacy, win their hearts, and signal Muhammad’s prophethood through unseen knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r1.anchor: كسرا لعنادهم ولجاجهم بتذكير النعم السالفة واستمالة لقلوبهم بسببها

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r2.claim: The passage first recalls Israel’s favors generally, then derives a command to believe in Muhammad and discusses what blocks belief.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r2.anchor: وفرع على تذكيرها الأمر بالإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r3.claim: God repeats the general reminder because the Israelites are deeply heedless, then pairs the promise of preference above the worlds with a severe warning about the Day of Judgment.

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r4.claim: Rāzī regards this progression from general reminder to inducement and warning, then detailed blessings, as ideal ordering for invitation and establishing belief in the listener.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r4.anchor: هذا هو النهاية في حسن الترتيب لمن يريد الدعوة وتحصيل الإعتقاد في قلب المستمع

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r5.claim: The commentators agree that Israel is Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r5.anchor: اتفق المفسرون على أن إسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إسحاق بن إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r6.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r6.claim: They explain Israel as “servant of God,” deriving Isra as servant and El as God, as in the names Gabriel and Michael.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r6.anchor: إن معنى إسرائيل عبد الله لأن ( إسرا ) في لغتهم هو العبد و ( إيل ) هو الله

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl offers a different etymology: in Hebrew Isra means “human,” so Israel means “man of God.”
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r7.anchor: قال القفال : قيل إن ( إسرا ) بالعبرانية في معنى إنسان فكأنه قيل رجل الله

RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r8.claim: The address is to the Jews in Medina during Muhammad’s time, descendants of Jacob.
RAZI-FULL:v3p27#2/r8.anchor: خطاب مع جماعة اليهود الذين كانوا بالمدينة من ولد يعقوب عليه السلام في أيام محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r1.claim: Razi defines a blessing as a benefit conferred kindly; he rejects requiring moral goodness, since gratitude for beneficence can coexist with blame for wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r1.anchor: والحق أن هذا القيد غير معتبر لأنه

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r2.claim: Pure harm cannot count as a blessing because a blessing must be beneficial.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r2.anchor: المضرة المحضة لا يجوز أن تكون نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r3.claim: A benefit counts as a blessing only when intended as kindness to its recipient; self-serving help or poisoned food meant to destroy the recipient fails this test.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r3.anchor: كمن أطعم خبيصا مسموما ليهلكه لم يكن ذلك ، نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r4.claim: Every benefit and removal of harm reaching people in this world and the next comes from God.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r4.anchor: كل ما يصل إلينا آناء الليل والنهار في الدنيا والآخرة من النفع ودفع الضرر فهو من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r5.claim: One class of blessings is given by God directly, such as creation and provision.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r5.anchor: نعمة تفرد الله بها نحو أن خلق ورزق

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r6.claim: A blessing may arrive through another person, but God created the benefit, giver, capacity, motive, and guidance; the human agent is thanked while God is ultimately thanked.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r6.anchor: بأن خلقها وخلق المنعم ومكنه من الإنعام وخلق فيه قدرة الأنعام وداعيته

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r7.claim: The Prophet says that one who does not thank people does not thank God.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r7.anchor: لا يشكر الله من لا يشكر الناس

RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r8.claim: Blessings received through acts of obedience still come from God, who enables, guides, and removes impediments to those acts.
RAZI-FULL:v3p28/r8.anchor: نعمة وصلت إلينا من الله تعالى بواسطة طاعاتنا وهي أيضا من الله تعالى لأنه لولا أنه سبحانه وتعالى وفقنا

RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r1.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted: bodily faculties and pleasures, useful things in the world, and means of avoiding harm all furnish benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r1.anchor: كل ما أودع فينا من المنافع واللذات التي ننتفع بها والجوارح والأعضاء التي نستعملها في جلب المنافع ودفع المضار

RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r2.claim: Even what gives no immediate pleasure or protection can point to the wise Creator and lead to knowledge, obedience, and everlasting pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r2.anchor: والذي لا يكون جالبا للنفع الحاضر ولا دافعا للضرر الحاضر فهو صالح لأن يستدل به على الصانع الحكيم

RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r3.claim: Although blessings are innumerable in kinds and individual instances, their kinds are finite, which is enough to remind people and establish knowledge of the wise Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r3.anchor: إلا أنها متناهية بحسب الأجناس ، وذلك يكفي في التذكير

RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r4.claim: Because praise and obedience are due for bestowing blessings, God alone deserves praise; idols cannot hear, benefit, or harm their worshippers.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r4.anchor: واعلم أنه لما ثبت أن استحقاق الحمد والثناء والطاعة لا يتحقق إلا على إيصال النعمة ثبت أنه سبحانه وتعالى هو المستحق لحمد الحامدين

RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r5.claim: The first blessing is being created alive: the cited sequence first names life, then the remaining blessings, and directs worldly life toward the life and reward of the hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29/r5.anchor: الفرع الثالث : أن أول ما أنعم الله به على عبيده هو أن خلقهم أحياء

RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r1.claim: The Mu'tazilites divide creation into a beneficiary and something from which benefit is taken; Sunnis answer that God creates both benefits and harms without being challenged.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r1.anchor: وبين أن جميع ما خلق قسمان منتفع ومنتفع به ، هذا قول المعتزلة .

RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r2.claim: The Mu'tazilites say God gave accountable people equal religious and worldly blessings: every possible religious aid was supplied, while worldly obligation to provide the best is specifically the Baghdadi Mu'tazilite position, not the Basran one.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى قد أنعم على المكلفين بنعمة الدنيا ونعمة الدين ، وسوى بين الجميع في النعم الدينية والدنيوية

RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r3.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r3.claim: Sunnis hold that God created disbelievers for the Fire, then disagree whether worldly benefits count as blessings for them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r3.anchor: إن الله تعالى خلق الكافر للنار ولعذاب الآخرة ثم اختلفوا في أنه هل لله نعمة على الكافر في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r4.speaker: بعض أهل السنة
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r4.claim: Some Sunnis deny that worldly benefits are blessings to disbelievers when they lead to lasting punishment, comparing them to poisoned sweetmeat and citing delayed worldly ease as an increase in sin.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r4.anchor: هذه النعم القليلة في الدنيا لما كانت مؤدية إلى الضرر الدائم في الآخرة لم يكن ذلك نعمة على الكافر

RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r5.claim: Al-Baqillani's view is sounder: God gave disbelievers worldly blessings even if He did not give them the blessing of religion; Razi adduces scriptural accounts of creation, provision, rescue, security, livelihood, and other favors.
RAZI-FULL:v3p29#2/r5.anchor: إنه تعالى وإن لم ينعم على الكافر بنعمة الدين فلقد أنعم عليه بنعمة الدنيا وهو قول القاضي أبي بكر الباقلاني رحمه الله ، وهذا القول أصوب

RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r1.claim: The dispute is verbal: all agree that life, reason, hearing, sight, provision, and benefits come from God; they differ over whether worldly benefits followed by eternal harm are called blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r1.anchor: لا نزاع في أن هذه الأشياء أعني الحياة والعقل والسمع والبصر وأنواع الرزق والمنافع من الله تعالى إنما الخلاف

RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r2.claim: Creation also serves as evidence for the Creator and His kindness: human development from a drop to an articulate disputant is itself a proof, and diverse crops and livestock refute materialists and naturalists.
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r2.anchor: فبين أن حدوث العبد مع ما فيه من الكفر من أعظم الدلائل على وجود الصانع وهو انقلابه من حال إلى حال

RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r3.claim: The same water and soil yield differing colors, tastes, and smells, and the sun and moon's uniform subjection show that natural processes and celestial bodies are created rather than self-sufficient.
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r3.anchor: بين بذلك الرد على الدهرية وأصحاب الطبائع لأنه تعالى بين أن الماء واحد والتراب واحد ومع ذلك اختلفت الألوان والطعوم والروائح

RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r4.claim: Every created thing apart from the accountable person either gives pleasure or comfort, removes a burden, or provides a lesson; harmful creatures such as snakes and scorpions recall punishment and point to the greatest Benefactor.
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r4.anchor: كل ما في العالم مما يغاير ذات المكلف ليس يخلو من أن يلتذ به المكلف ويستروح إليه فيحصل له به سرور أو يتحمل عنه كلفة

RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r5.claim: Razi adds that scripture presents worldly prosperity as a blessing for disbelieving people too, including a secure town, God's favor, human reproduction, and the repeatedly named signs in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.
RAZI-FULL:v3p31/r5.anchor: كل ما في هذه السورة فهو من النعم ، إما في الدين أو في الدنيا فهذا ما يتعلق بهذا الباب .

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r1.speaker: بعض العارفين
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r1.claim: A gnostic says many serve blessings, while few serve the Bestower; Razi infers that the address recalling blessings to Israel and the address recalling God Himself to Muhammad's community indicate the latter community's superiority.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r1.anchor: عبيد النعم كثيرون وعبيد المنعم قليلون ، فالله تعالى ذكر بني إسرائيل بنعمه عليهم ولما آل الأمر إلى أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r2.claim: God rescued Israel from Pharaoh's oppression, freed them from servitude, and established them in the land.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r2.anchor: استنقذهم مما كانوا فيه من البلاء من فرعون وقومه وأبدلهم من ذلك بتمكينهم في الأرض وتخليصهم من العبودية

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r3.claim: God made them prophets and kings after their enslavement to the Copts, destroyed their enemies, and gave them their lands, homes, and wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r3.anchor: جعلهم أنبياء وملوكا بعد أن كانوا عبيدا للقبط فأهلك أعداءهم وأورثهم أرضهم وديارهم وأموالهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r4.claim: God bestowed great revealed books on Israel, a distinction Razi says no other community received in the same way.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r4.anchor: أنزل عليهم الكتب العظيمة التي ما أنزلها على أمة سواهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas lists Israel's rescue from Pharaoh, cloud shade in the wilderness, manna and quails, a stone supplying water on demand, a nighttime pillar of light, hair that did not tangle, and clothes that did not wear out.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r5.anchor: روى هشام عن ابن عباس أنه قال : من نعمة الله تعالى على بني إسرائيل أن نجاهم من آل فرعون وظلل عليهم في التيه الغمام

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r6.claim: Remembering Israel's blessings points to the truth of Muhammad through the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms, makes disobedience more serious, and evokes shame at opposing the call to believe in Muhammad and the Quran.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r6.anchor: أن في جملة النعم ما يشهد بصدق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو التوراة والإنجيل والزبور

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r7.claim: Recalling past blessings can give hope of future blessings, since one who has bestowed many favors is expected to continue them; that hope restrains opposition.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r7.anchor: ومن خص أحدا بنعم كثيرة فالظاهر أنه لا يزيلها عنهم لما قيل : إتمام المعروف خير من ابتدائه

RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r8.claim: Though the blessings were given to Israel's ancestors, their descendants benefited because they would not exist without them, their lineage is itself a favor, and hearing of the ancestors' obedience can encourage children to follow their example.
RAZI-FULL:v3p32/r8.anchor: لولا هذه النعم على آبائهم لما بقوا فما كان يحصل هذا النسل فصارت النعم على الآباء كأنها نعم على الأبناء

RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r1.claim: Covenant can refer to either side of a mutual compact; Razi presents two readings, beginning with the interpretation that it encompasses all divine commands rather than a subset of duties.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r1.anchor: فاعلم أن العهد يضاف إلى المعاهد والمعاهد جميعا وذكروا في هذا العهد قولين : الأول : أن المراد منه جميع ما أمر الله به

RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r2.claim: One report says God's disclosure of His blessings constituted His covenant requiring gratitude, while His covenant with Israel meant the promised reward and forgiveness, which cannot be broken.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى جعل تعريفه إياهم نعمه عهدا له عليهم من حيث يلزمهم القايم بشكرها

RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the covenant as the pledge taken from Israel through the twelve chiefs: if they pray, give alms, and obey, God will admit them to gardens.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r3.anchor: ثانيها : قال الحسن : المراد منه العهد الذي أخذه الله تعالى على بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r4.claim: Most exegetes understand the command as fulfilling all obligations and avoiding sins, with God fulfilling His covenant by being pleased with them and admitting them to Paradise; al-Dahhak transmits this from Ibn Abbas.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33/r4.anchor: وهو قول جمهور المفسرين أن المراد أوفوا بما أمرتكم به من الطاعات ونهيتكم عنه من المعاصي أوف بعهدكم

RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r1.claim: The second interpretation makes the covenant the earlier scriptures' description of Muhammad and his coming; God's promise to Israel is to remove the burdens and shackles imposed on them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r1.anchor: أن المراد من هذا العهد ما أثبته في الكتب المتقدمة من وصف محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنه سيبعثه

RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Torah promised an unlettered prophet from Ishmael: whoever followed him and believed the Quran would be forgiven, enter Paradise, and receive two rewards for following the earlier prophets and Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إن الله تعالى كان عهد إلى بني إسرائيل في التوراة أني باعث من بني إسماعيل نبيا أميا

RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r3.speaker: علي بن عيسى
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r3.claim: Ali ibn Isa cites the promise of two shares of mercy as corroboration for the double-reward teaching.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r3.anchor: وكان علي بن عيسى يقول تصديق ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r4.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet named three people who receive double reward: a person of the Book who believes in Jesus and then Muhammad, one who educates and frees a female slave before marrying her, and a person who obeys both God and his master.
RAZI-FULL:v3p33#2/r4.anchor: تصديقه أيضا فيما روى أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r1.claim: Asked how Israel could deny the prophecy, Razi answers that its knowledge may have belonged only to a small number of learned people, who could conceal it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r1.anchor: أن هذا العلم كان حاصلا عند العلماء بكتبهم لكن لم يكن لهم العدد الكثير فجاز منهم كتمانه

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r2.claim: A second answer is that the scriptural wording was obscure rather than explicit, allowing doubts and objections.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r2.anchor: أن ذلك النص كان نصا خفيا لا جليا فجاز وقوع الشكوك والشبهات فيه

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r3.claim: Razi frames the difficulty: explicit, widely transmitted details about the person's time and place could not be hidden and should be necessary knowledge, while an unspecified prophecy would let Jews claim the promised figure was still to come, as most Jews do.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r3.anchor: فإن كان ذلك النص نصا جليا واردا في كتب منقولة إلى أهل العلم بالتواتر فكان يمتنع قدرتهم على الكتمان

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r4.claim: Those who read the covenant as a general command to examine evidence of God's oneness and prophethood chose that interpretation because this objection is strong.

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r5.claim: Defenders of the prophecy reading answer that the time and place were not stated plainly for everyone, so the prediction need not have been universally certain knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r5.anchor: بأن تعيين الزمان والمكان لم يكن منصوصا عليه نصا جليا يعرفه كل أحد بل كان منصوصا

RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r6.claim: Razi quotes a Torah story in which an angel tells Hagar to return to Sarah, promises many descendants, and says she will bear Ishmael because God heard her humility; Ishmael will be strong among peoples and honored despite his brothers.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34/r6.anchor: جاء في الفصل التاسع من السفر الأول من التوراة

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r1.claim: Razi treats the wording as glad tidings whose fulfillment shows the Prophet's truth: God would not announce through a messenger an unjust outcome or one that required falsehood about God.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r1.anchor: أن هذا الكلام خرج مخرج البشارة وليس يجوز أن يبشر الملك من قبل الله بالظلم والجور

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r2.claim: Ishmael's descendants had been confined to the desert and feared entering Iraq or Syria; Islam enabled them to spread east and west and mingle with nations.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r2.anchor: كانوا قبل الإسلام محصورين في البادية لا يتجاسرون على الدخول في أوائل العراق وأوائل الشام

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r3.claim: If the Prophet were false, the resulting contact between his people and other nations would be disobedience; God cannot give glad tidings of an outcome that is disobedience.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r3.anchor: فلو لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صادقا لكانت هذه المخالطة منهم للأمم ومن الأمم لهم معصية لله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r4.claim: Razi cites Deuteronomy's promise of a prophet like Moses from the people's brothers as indicating a prophet outside Israel, just as an imam from the brothers of Banu Hashim would not be a Hashimite.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r4.anchor: إن الرب إلهكم يقيم لكم نبيا مثلي من بينكم ومن إخوانكم

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r5.claim: Jacob (Israel) had only Esau as a brother, and Esau's only prophetic descendant, Job, preceded Moses; prophets after Moses were Israelites, so the promised later prophet cannot be an Israelite.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r5.anchor: ثم إن يعقوب عليه السلام هو إسرائيل ولم يكن له أخ إلا العيص

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r6.claim: Muhammad is the promised prophet from the brothers of Israel because Ishmael, his ancestor, was Isaac's brother.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r6.anchor: لكنه كان من إخوانهم لأنه من ولد إسماعيل الذي هو أخو إسحق

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r7.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r7.claim: An objection says the phrase from among you excludes Muhammad because he did not arise among the Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r7.anchor: فإن قيل قوله : ( من بينكم ) يمنع من أن يكون المراد محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r8.claim: Razi replies that Muhammad arose among them geographically: he appeared in the Hijaz, was sent in Mecca, and migrated to Medina among nearby Jewish communities and near the Jews of Syria.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r8.anchor: بل قد قام من بينهم لأنه عليه السلام ظهر بالحجاز فبعث بمكة وهاجر إلى المدينة

RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r9.claim: The phrase from among you also fits through kinship: since Muhammad was their brother by descent, his arising among them was not remote.
RAZI-FULL:v3p34#2/r9.anchor: وأيضا فإنه إذا كان من إخوانهم فقد قام من بينهم فإنه ليس ببعيد منهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r1.claim: Razi's third proof cites a passage saying God came from Sinai and appeared from Seir and Paran; Paran is in the Hijaz because the Torah says Ishmael practiced archery in Paran and he lived in Mecca.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r1.anchor: أن جبل فاران هو بالحجاز لأن في التوراة أن اسماعيل تعلم الرمي في برية فاران

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r2.claim: The passage's grant of glory cannot refer to Ishmael, who gained no glory after settling there and was not surrounded by tens of thousands of saints; Razi therefore identifies the figure as Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r2.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون المراد إسماعيل عليه السلام لأنه لم يحصل عقيب سكنى إسماعيل عليه السلام هناك عز

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r3.speaker: اليهود
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r3.claim: The Jews interpret the passage as fire appearing at Sinai, Seir, and Paran.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r3.anchor: قالت اليهود : المراد أن النار لما ظهرت من طور سيناء ظهرت من ساعير نار أيضا ومن جبل فاران أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r4.claim: Razi rejects the fire reading: God's coming from a place denotes an accompanying revelation, speech, punishment, or similar event, which the Jews acknowledge occurred only at Sinai.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r4.anchor: لو خلق نارا في موضع فإنه لا يقال جاء الله من ذلك إذا تابع ذلك الواقعة وحي نزل في ذلك الموضع

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r5.claim: A cited passage in Habakkuk supports the reading by saying God came from Sinai and the Holy One from Paran, then describing Muhammad and his community's triumph.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r5.anchor: جاء الله من طور سيناء والقدس من جبل فاران ، وانكشفت السماء من بهاء محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r6.speaker: ابن رزين الطبري
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r6.claim: Ibn Razin al-Tabari transmits a version of the Paran prophecy that names Muhammad and depicts his armies, arrows, and deliverance of his nation and ancestral land.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r6.anchor: هكذا نقل عن ابن رزين الطبري .

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r7.speaker: أبو الحسين
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r7.claim: Abu al-Husayn says he saw Christian transmissions that explicitly name Muhammad al-Mahmud in the prophecy from Paran and speak of his people's salvation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r7.anchor: فقال أبو الحسين رحمه الله في كتاب الغرر قد رأيت في نقولهم :

RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r8.claim: Razi concludes that the Torah's appearance of the Lord from Paran means the appearance of a person with these traits, namely Muhammad, rather than fire.
RAZI-FULL:v3p35/r8.anchor: فظهر بما ذكرنا أن قوله تعالى في التوراة : ( ظهر الرب من جبال فاران ) ليس معناه ظهور النار منه

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r1.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r1.claim: An objection takes the passage to mean God's own coming because it ends by mentioning the rescue of the Messiah.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r1.anchor: فإن قالوا المراد مجيء الله تعالى ولهذا قال في آخر الكلام : ( وإنقاذ مسيحك )

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r2.claim: Razi says the figure cannot be God, since the passage describes riding horses, a radiant appearance, and crossing ancient mountains; Muhammad rescued Jesus from Jewish and Christian falsehoods.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r2.anchor: لا يجوز وصف الله تعالى بأنه يركب الخيول وبأن شعاع منظره مثل النور

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
