RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r3.claim: Razi's fourth proof cites Isaiah's prophecy about a city identified as Mecca, to which nations and kings come and whose light attracts them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r3.anchor: يريد مكة ، فقد دناوقتك وكرامة الله تعالى طالعة عليك

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r4.claim: Razi says the prophecy's details fit Mecca: the armies of nations pilgrimage there and the sea's treasures flow toward it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r4.anchor: فوجه الاستدلال أن هذه الصفات كلها موجودة لمكة فإنه قد حج إليها عساكر الأمم

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r5.claim: He interprets the renewed praise for the house as Islam's replacement of the pre-Islamic talbiya, which admitted a partner, with the declaration that God has no partner.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r5.anchor: ثم صار في الإسلام : لبيك اللهم لبيك ، لا شريك لك لبيك ، فهذا هو الحمد الذي جدده الله لبيت محمدته

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r6.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r6.claim: An objection says Isaiah's prophecy concerns Jerusalem and will be fulfilled in the future.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r6.anchor: فإن قيل المراد : بذلك بيت المقدس وسيكون ذلك فيما بعد

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r7.claim: Razi responds that it is incoherent to say the time is near if the event is distant, especially when the approaching event is displeasing; Isaiah's many references to the desert also disprove the Jerusalem reading.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r7.anchor: لا يجوز أن يقول الحكيم : ( قد دنا وقتك ) مع أنه ما دنا بل الذي دنا أمر لا يوافق رضاه

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r8.speaker: السمان
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r8.claim: Al-Samman transmits from the Torah's first book God's promise to Abraham that Ishmael is answered, blessed, greatly increased, and will father twelve chiefs and a great nation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r8.anchor: روى السمان في تفسيره في السفر الأول من التوراة أن الله تعالى أوحى إلى إبراهيم

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r9.claim: Razi infers that Muhammad is the only descendant of Ishmael who became the leader of a great nation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r9.anchor: أنه لم يكن في ولد إسماعيل من كان كان لأمة عظيمة غير نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r10.claim: Abraham and Ishmael's prayer after building the Kaaba was for Muhammad, asking God to send a messenger from among them to recite revelation and teach and purify them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r10.anchor: فأما دعاء إبراهيم عليه السلام وإسماعيل فكان لرسولنا عليه الصلاة والسلام لما فرغا من بناء الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r11.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r11.claim: The Prophet said he was Abraham's prayer and Jesus' glad tidings, linking the latter to Jesus' announcement of a messenger named Ahmad.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r11.anchor: ولهذا كان يقول عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم وبشارة عيسى )

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r12.claim: Razi says Ahmad derives from praise, as do Muhammad and Mahmoud, and thus fits the Prophet in particular.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r12.anchor: فإنه مشتق من الحمد والاسم المشتق من الحمد ليس إلا لنبينا فإن اسمه محمد وأحمد ومحمود

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r13.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r13.claim: A report says the Torah describes the Prophet as born in Mecca, residing in Tayba, ruling in Syria, and belonging to a community of praisers.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r13.anchor: قيل إن صفته في التوراة أن مولده بمكة ومسكنه بطيبة وملكه بالشام وأمته الحمادون

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r14.speaker: المسيح
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r14.claim: Jesus told the apostles that after he left, the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, would come and speak only what he was told; Razi compares this with Muhammad's declarations that he follows revelation alone.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r14.anchor: قال المسيح للحواريين : ( أنا أذهب وسيأتيكم الفار قليط روح الحق الذي لا يتكلم من قبل نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r15.claim: Razi gives two readings of Paraclete: an accepted intercessor, a description of Muhammad, or, according to some Christians, one who distinguishes truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r15.anchor: أما ( الفارقليط ) ففي تفسيره وجهان : أحدهما أنه الشافع المشفع

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r16.speaker: بعض النصارى
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r16.claim: Some Christians explain Paraclete as the one who separates truth from falsehood, deriving it from Faruq and an intensive form; Razi says this too describes Islam's law.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r16.anchor: قال بعض النصارى : الفار قليط هو الذي يفرق بين الحق والباطل وكان في الأصل فاروق

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r17.claim: Razi's seventh proof recounts Daniel's interpretation of a king's dream: successive metal kingdoms are struck by an uncut stone that becomes an everlasting kingdom filling the earth and abolishing the others.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r17.anchor: ويقيم إله السماء في تلك الأيام مملكة أبدية لا تتغير ولا تزول وإنها تزيل جميع الممالك

RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r18.claim: Razi presents these passages from earlier scriptures as glad tidings of Muhammad's mission.
RAZI-FULL:v3p36/r18.anchor: فهذه هي البشارات الواردة في الكتب المتقدمة بمبعث رسولنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r1.claim: The Mu'tazilites say God's covenant is the rational obligation to give reward to the obedient, called a covenant because fulfillment is binding and stronger than an oath or vow.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r1.anchor: ذلك العهد هو ما دل العقل عليه من أن الله تعالى يجب عليه إيصال الثواب إلى المطيع

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r2.claim: Razi's Ash'ari school denies that anything is owed by a servant upon God; since prior blessings ground the servant's duty, obedience does not generate a further duty of reward, contrary to the Mu'tazilites.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r2.anchor: وقال أصحابنا : إنه لا يجب للعبد على الله شيء

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r3.claim: Razi says the proper account is that God's promised reward must occur: otherwise His truthful report would become a lie, which is impossible, making the promise more certain than an oath or vow.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r3.anchor: الأول : أنه تعالى لما وعد بالثواب وكل ما وعد به استحال أن لا يوجد ، لأنه لو لم يوجد لانقلب خبره الصدق كذبا

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r4.claim: Alternatively, covenant means command: a servant may be commanded, while God cannot, and reciprocal wording is used similarly when God is called a deceiver or plotter.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r4.anchor: أن يقال العهد هو الأمر والعبد يجوز أن يكون مأمورا إلا أن الله تعالى لا يجوز أن يكون مأمورا

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r5.claim: Razi defines reverence or dread as fear, and the theologians define fear of God as fear of His punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r5.anchor: فاعلم أن الرهبة هي الخوف قال المتكلمون : الخوف منه تعالى هو الخوف من عقابه

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r6.claim: A person may fear with certainty or with conjecture: one certain of having fulfilled every command and avoided every prohibition fears only what lies ahead.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r6.anchor: أما العلم فإذا كان على يقين من أنه أتى بكل ما أمر به واحترز عن كل ما نهى عنه

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r7.claim: Prophets and angels can be described as fearing God in this future-oriented sense.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا نصف الملائكة والأنبياء عليهم السلام بالخوف والرهبة

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r8.claim: When someone is unsure whether they obeyed fully or avoided prohibitions, fear arises from uncertainty about deserving reward.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r8.anchor: وأما الظن فإذا لم يقطع بأنه فعل المأمورات واحترز عن المنهيات فحينئذ يخاف

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r9.claim: Razi says the greater one's fear in this world, the greater one's safety on Judgment Day, and vice versa.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r9.anchor: أن كل من كان خوفه في الدنيا أشد كان أمنه يوم القيامة أكثر وبالعكس

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r10.speaker: راوٍ غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r10.claim: A report says God swears He will not combine two fears or two securities for a servant: the one secure from Him in this world will fear on Judgment Day, while the one who feared Him here will be secure then.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r10.anchor: ينادي مناد يوم القيامة وعزتي وجلالي إني لا أجمع على عبدي خوفين ولا أمنين

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r11.speaker: العارفون
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r11.claim: The gnostics distinguish fear of punishment, belonging to outward adherents, from fear of divine majesty, belonging to people of the heart; the first ends and the second never does.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r11.anchor: وقال العارفون : الخوف خوفان خوف العقاب وخوف الجلال ، والأول : نصيب أهل الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r12.claim: The verse indicates that abundant blessings make disobedience graver and that a covenant stated beforehand makes its breach more serious.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r12.anchor: واعلم أن في الآية دلالة على أن كثرة النعم تعظم المعصية ، ودلالة على ما تقدم العهد يعظم المخالفة

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r13.claim: The passage indicates that the Messenger was sent to Israelites as well as Arabs.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r13.anchor: ودلالة على أن الرسول كما كان مبعوثا إلى العرب كان مبعوثا إلى بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r14.claim: The command to fear God alone extends also to hope and expectation, and Razi takes this exclusivity to support that all things occur by God's decree.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r14.anchor: وكما يجب ذلك في الخوف فكذا في الرجاء والأمل وذلك يدل على أن الكل بقضاء الله وقدره

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r15.claim: If a servant acted independently, one would have to fear the servant as one fears God, and indeed fear oneself because control of reward and punishment would be in one's own hands; this would defeat the verse's exclusive command.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r15.anchor: لو كان العبد مستقلا بالفعل لوجب أن يخاف منه كما يخاف من الله تعالى وحينئذ يبطل الحصر

RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r16.claim: The verse also indicates that a morally responsible person must perform obedience through fear and hope, which are necessary to its validity.
RAZI-FULL:v3p37/r16.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أنه يجب على المكلف أن يأتي بالطاعات للخوف والرجاء وأن ذلك لا بد منه في صحتها

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r1.claim: The Blessing is commonly understood as deliverance from Pharaoh, followed by manna, quails, and the promised land.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r1.anchor: The Blessing (niʿmah; see also vv. 47, 122) is usually understood to be the deliverance from Pharaoh (vv. 49–50) and the subsequent heavenly gifts of manna, quails, and the promised land;

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Blessing as God's placing prophets among the Israelites and sending them Divine books.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r2.anchor: or that God placed prophets among them and sent them Divine books;

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r3.claim: Some understand the Blessing as Islam's coming, since the verse addresses Jews living in and around Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r3.anchor: or the coming of Islam, since this verse addresses the Jews in and around Madinah.

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r4.claim: Niʿmah can also have its broadest sense, beginning with creation, consistent with the universal commands that follow.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r4.anchor: Niʿmah is understood in the most general sense as well, beginning with the gift of creation, in keeping with the universal commands of the following verses.

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r5.claim: The covenant can broadly mean the people's gratitude and, on God's side, His forgiveness and reward.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r5.anchor: which is understood broadly as people’s gratitude, on the one hand, and God’s Forgiveness and Reward, on the other.

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r6.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r6.claim: The covenant may be the pact in 5:12, in which God made a covenant with Israel and raised twelve chieftains among them.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r6.anchor: Another interpretation is that it refers to the mīthāq (“covenant” or “pact”) of 5:12: God had made a covenant with the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve chieftains.

STUDYQURAN:2:40/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r7.claim: The covenant may require fidelity to the foretold coming of the Prophet, described in the Torah and Gospel available to them.
STUDYQURAN:2:40/r7.anchor: Some interpret it to mean that they should be true to the predicted coming of the Prophet, whom they find inscribed in the Torah and the Gospel that is with them

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says God calls them children of Israel because they descend from Jacob, just as Adam's descendants are called children of Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r1.anchor: فنسبهم جل ذكره إلى يعقوب، كما نسب ذرية آدم إلى آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Israel as equivalent to the name Abd Allah.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " إن إسرائيل كقولك: عبد الله "

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r3.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Harith says El means God in Hebrew.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث، قال: " إيل: الله بالعبرانية "

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r4.claim: The address “children of Israel” specifically targets Jewish scholars living in Medina, descendants of Jacob, as the audience for the following reminders.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r4.anchor: أحبار اليهود من بني إسرائيل الذين كانوا بين ظهراني مهاجر رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says the early surah recounts ancestral reports particularly known to Jews; Muhammad's accurate knowledge despite little study of their books demonstrates revelation, as in the analogous address to Adam's descendants.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r5.anchor: مع بعد قومه وعشيرته من معرفتها، وقلة مزاولة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم دراسة الكتب التي فيها أنباء ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p593/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the addressees as the People of the Book, the Jewish scholars.
TAB-FULL:v1p593/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " قوله: {يا بني إسرائيل} [البقرة: 40] قال: يا أهل الكتاب للأحبار من يهود

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r1.claim: Al-Tabari lists God's favors to Israel: prophets and scriptures, rescue from Pharaoh, settlement in the land, water from the rock, and manna and quail; descendants must remember them lest they incur punishment for ingratitude.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r1.anchor: وتفجير عيون الماء من الحجر، وإطعام المن والسلوى

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the favors included rescuing Israel and their ancestors from Pharaoh and his people.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم} [البقرة: 40] أي آلائي عندكم وعند آبائكم لما كان نجاهم به من فرعون وقومه

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the favors as making prophets and messengers among them and sending them scriptures.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {اذكروا نعمتي} [البقرة: 40] قال: نعمته أن جعل منهم الأنبياء والرسل، وأنزل عليهم الكتب

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r4.claim: Mujahid includes the favors named in the verse and others: water from the rock, manna and quail, and deliverance from Pharaoh's enslavement.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم} [البقرة: 40] يعني نعمته التي أنعم على بني إسرائيل فيما سمى وفيما سوى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God's favors are general, with Islam the greatest and all other favors subordinate to it; he cites the rebuke against claiming Islam as a favor to the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم} [البقرة: 40] قال: نعمه عامة، ولا نعمة أفضل من الإسلام

TAB-FULL:v1p595/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r6.claim: Al-Tabari connects this reminder through Muhammad with Moses' earlier reminder that God made prophets and rulers among Israel and gave them unmatched favors.
TAB-FULL:v1p595/r6.anchor: نظير تذكير موسى صلوات الله عليه أسلافهم على عهده الذي أخبر الله عنه أنه قال لهم

TAB-FULL:v1p596/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r1.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the covenant as God's Torah command to Israel to explain that Muhammad is God's Messenger, found in their scripture, and to believe and follow him; fulfilling their side earns Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r1.anchor: للناس أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه رسول، وأنهم يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة أنه نبي الله، وأن يؤمنوا به

TAB-FULL:v1p596/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Israel had pledged to follow the Prophet when he came; God would fulfill His promise by removing their burdens and shackles caused by their sins.
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وأوفوا بعهدي} [البقرة: 40] الذي أخذت في أعناقكم للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جاءكم {أوف بعهدكم}

TAB-FULL:v1p596/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies God's covenant as the religion of Islam for people to follow and God's promised reward as Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {أوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] قال: عهده إلى عباده: دين الإسلام أن يتبعوه. و {أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] يعني الجنة

TAB-FULL:v1p596/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Israel must obey what God commanded in scripture, and God promises Paradise to those who obey.
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] أما أوفوا بعهدي: فما عهدت إليكم في الكتاب، وأما أوف بعهدكم: فالجنة

TAB-FULL:v1p596/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the covenant with the pledge in 5:12 and says it applies to the community too: whoever fulfills God's covenant will receive God's fulfillment.
TAB-FULL:v1p596/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج: " في قوله: {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] قال: ذلك الميثاق

TAB-FULL:v1p598/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Israel must obey and avoid disobedience regarding the Prophet and others; God will be pleased with them and admit them to Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] يقول: أوفوا بما أمرتكم به من طاعتي ونهيتكم عنه

TAB-FULL:v1p598/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the command as obeying God and receiving what He promised, citing God's pledge to believers in 9:111.
TAB-FULL:v1p598/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " في قوله: {وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم} [البقرة: 40] قال: أوفوا بأمري، أوف بالذي وعدتكم

TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reads “fear Me” as warning Israel for neglecting God's covenant and denying His Messenger: unless they repent by following him and affirming revelation, they risk the punishment inflicted on earlier disobedient peoples.
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r1.anchor: إن لم تنيبوا وتتوبوا إلي باتباعه والإقرار بما أنزلت إليه

TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning is to fear punishments such as the transformations inflicted on Israel's ancestors.
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وإياي فارهبون} [البقرة: 40] أن أنزل بكم ما أنزلت بمن كان قبلكم من آبائكم من النقمات التي قد عرفتم من المسخ وغيره

TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya simply glosses the phrase as “fear Me.”
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " في قوله: {وإياي فارهبون} [البقرة: 40] يقول: فاخشون

TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi likewise glosses the phrase as “fear Me.”
TAB-FULL:v1p598#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {وإياي فارهبون} [البقرة: 40] بقول: وإياي فاخشون

TABATABAI:2:40-41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r1.claim: Across more than a hundred verses, God rebukes the Jews by recalling His favors and their rejection, covenant-breaking, disobedience, ingratitude, sins, and crimes.
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r1.anchor: وذلك في طي نيف ومائة آية يذكر فيها نعمه التي أفاضها عليهم، وكراماته التي حباهم بها، وما قابلوها من الكفر والعصيان ونقض الميثاق

TABATABAI:2:40-41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r2.claim: The passage recalls twelve episodes, including rescue from Pharaoh through the parted sea, Pharaoh's drowning, the Sinai appointment, the calf, commanded self-killing, a demand to see God, the thunderbolt, and revival; these display divine care.
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r2.anchor: يذكرهم بالإشارة إلى اثنتي عشرة قصة من قصصهم، كنجاتهم من آل فرعون بفرق البحر، وغرق فرعون وجنوده، ومواعدة الطور،

TABATABAI:2:40-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r3.claim: The reminders include covenants they broke and sins and crimes committed despite their scripture's prohibitions and their own reason, reflecting hard hearts and wayward souls.
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r3.anchor: ويذكرهم أيضا المواثيق التي أخذ منهم ثم نقضوها ونبذوها وراء ظهورهم، ويذكرهم أيضا معاصي ارتكبوها وجرائم اكتسبوها

TABATABAI:2:40-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r4.claim: The root sense of عهد is preservation, from which come its senses of covenant, oath, testament, encounter, and abode.
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r4.anchor: أصل العهد الحفاظ، ومنه اشتقت معانيه كالعهد بمعنى الميثاق واليمين والوصية واللقاء والمنزل

TABATABAI:2:40-41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:40-41/r5.claim: Rahbah means fear and stands in contrast to رغبة, desire.

ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r1.claim: “Banī Isrāʾīl” is accusative as a genitive vocative; vocatives take the accusative because their sense is “I called” or “I summoned.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r1.anchor: نصب (بني إسرائيل) لأنه نداء مضاف، وأصل النداء النصب لأن

ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r2.claim: “Isrāʾīl” is genitive in position but has a final fatḥa because it is indeclinable as a foreign proper name longer than three letters.
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r2.anchor: وإسرائيل في موضع خفض إلا إنه فتح آخره لأنه لا ينصرف، وفيه شيئان يوجبان منع الصرف، وهما إنه أعجمي

ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r3.claim: The yāʾ in “niʿmatī” may be elided at the word boundary, but keeping it and opening it is preferred for stronger Arabic form, fuller sound, and the reward for each recited letter.
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تحذف الياء في اللفظ لالتقاء الساكنين فتقرأ - (نعمت التي) أنعمت بحذف الياء، والاختيار إثبات الياء

ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r5.claim: The Israelites are reminded of blessings granted both to them and to their ancestors; the contemporaries were not prophets, as the cited verse about prophets and kings shows.
ZAJJAJ:v1p119#2/r5.anchor: فإنهم ذكروا بما أنعم به على آبائهم من قبلهم، وأنعم به عليهم، والدليل على ذلك قوله: (إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا)،

ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r1.claim: Arabic speakers attribute ancestors’ deeds to descendants: “we defeated you” or “we killed you” can mean that their forebears defeated or killed the other side’s forebears.
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r1.anchor: ويقول قتلناكم يوم كذا، معناه قتل آباؤنا آباءكم.

ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r2.claim: Fulfilling the covenant means making clear what the People of the Book were charged to disclose, including the prophecy of Muḥammad.
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r2.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم - قوله: (وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب لتبيننه للناس ولا تكتمونه) فتمام تبيينه

ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r3.claim: “Iyyāya fa-rhabūn” is accusative after an implied imperative equivalent to “fear me”; the following expression explains that suppressed verb.
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r3.anchor: نصب بالأمر كأنه في المعنى " أرهبوني " ويكون الثاني تفسير هذا الفعل المضمر

ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r4.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from “fa-rhabūnī” at the verse ending for cadence; Arabic linguists call verse endings fawāṣil and poem endings qawāfī.
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r4.anchor: ولكن الاختيار في الكلام والقرآن والشعر (وإياي فارهبون) حذفت الياء

ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r5.claim: Both “wafaytu” and “awfaytu” mean fulfilling a covenant, but he prefers “awfaytu,” the form consistently used in the Qur’an; Ibn ʿAwf’s verse attests both forms together.
ZAJJAJ:v1p120/r5.anchor: أما ابن عوف فقد أوفى بذمته. . . كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها

TABRISI:2:40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r1.speaker: القراءة المشهورة
TABRISI:2:40/r1.claim: The standard reading of Isrāʾīl has hamza and full lengthening and is the eloquent form.
TABRISI:2:40/r1.anchor: القراءة المشهورة إسرائيل مهموز ممدود مشبع وهو الفصيح

TABRISI:2:40/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r2.speaker: الحسن والزهري
TABRISI:2:40/r2.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī says Isrāʾīl without hamza or lengthening.
TABRISI:2:40/r2.anchor: وروي في الشواذ عن الحسن والزهري إسرايل بلا همز ولا مد

TABRISI:2:40/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r3.speaker: الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر
TABRISI:2:40/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar are also reported to read it without hamza or lengthening.
TABRISI:2:40/r3.anchor: وعن الأعمش وعيسى بن عمر كذلك

TABRISI:2:40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r4.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:2:40/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash reports a form with kasra on hamza and no yāʾ.
TABRISI:2:40/r4.anchor: وحكي عن الأخفش إسرائل بكسر الهمزة من غير ياء

TABRISI:2:40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r5.speaker: قطرب
TABRISI:2:40/r5.claim: Quṭrub reports forms without hamza or yāʾ, including one ending in nūn.
TABRISI:2:40/r5.anchor: وحكى قطرب إسرال من غير همز ولا ياء و إسرئين بالنون

TABRISI:2:40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:40/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Arabs freely alter foreign words, illustrating this with a verse that means ‘al-muzarjan,’ wine, from al-zarjūn.
TABRISI:2:40/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي العرب إذا نطقت بالأعجمي خلطت فيه وأنشد

TABRISI:2:40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:40/r7.claim: He explains that the nūn in zarjūn is a root letter, like the sīn in qurbūs; if Arabs alter even native words, they may do so more with foreign ones.
TABRISI:2:40/r7.anchor: قال والنون في زرجون أصل كالسين في قربوس فإذا جاز للعرب أن تخلط فيما هو لغتها

TABRISI:2:40/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r8.claim: Vocalizing the yāʾ in ‘My favor’ before the definite article is preferable to deleting it, because the vowel better reflects the original form and parallels the fatḥa on hamzat al-waṣl at resumption.
TABRISI:2:40/r8.anchor: واختير تحريك الياء في قوله نعمتي التي أنعمت لأنه لقيها ألف الوصل واللام

TABRISI:2:40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r9.claim: Deletion is better in ‘O My servants who have transgressed,’ since a possessive yāʾ should not remain in direct address and cannot then be vocalized.
TABRISI:2:40/r9.anchor: أي الإسقاط ههنا أجود لأن من حق ياء الإضافة ألا تثبت في النداء

TABRISI:2:40/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r10.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from ‘So give good news to My servants’ because it ends a verse, where pause is intended as at poetic line endings.
TABRISI:2:40/r10.anchor: حذف الياء لأنه رأس آية ورؤوس الآية لا تثبت فيها الياء

TABRISI:2:40/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r11.claim: Readers agree to omit the yāʾ in ‘so fear Me’ except Ibn Kathīr, who retains it in connected speech; deletion avoids pausing on yāʾ and is signaled by the nūn's kasra.
TABRISI:2:40/r11.anchor: وأجمعوا على إسقاط الياء من قوله فارهبون إلا ابن كثير فإنه أثبتها في الوصل دون الوقف

TABRISI:2:40/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r12.claim: Ibn is male offspring; walad can be male or female, while nasl and dhurriyya cover either. Ibn derives from building because a son is built upon the father, the root.
TABRISI:2:40/r12.anchor: إلا أن الابن للذكر والولد يقع على الذكر والأنثى والنسل

TABRISI:2:40/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r13.claim: Israel is Jacob son of Abraham; another etymology parses it as ‘servant of God,’ like ʿAbd Allāh, Jibrīl, and Mīkāʾīl.
TABRISI:2:40/r13.anchor: وإسرائيل هو يعقوب بن إبراهيم وقيل أصله مضاف لأن أسر معناه عبد وايل هو الله بالعبرانية

TABRISI:2:40/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40/r14.claim: Dhikr can mean remembering, speaking of something, honor, scripture, prayer, or supplication; its underlying sense is calling attention to something.
TABRISI:2:40/r14.anchor: والذكر الحفظ للشيء بذكره وضده النسيان والذكر جري الشيء على لسانك والذكر الشرف

TABRISI:2:40/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40/r15.speaker: صاحب العين
TABRISI:2:40/r15.claim: The lexicon gives both wafaytu and awfaytu for keeping a covenant, with awfaytu identified as a Tihāma dialect form; Ibn ʿAwf's verse uses both.
TABRISI:2:40/r15.anchor: صاحب العين تقول وفيت بعهدك وأوفيت لغة تهامة

TABRISI:2:40#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r1.claim: The verse uses awfā for Ibn ʿAwf keeping his pledge and wafā for his fulfillment of another obligation, illustrating the two forms.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r1.anchor: أما ابن عوف فقد أوفى بذمته كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها

TABRISI:2:40#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r2.claim: ʿAhd means a pledge or testament; rahba means fear, opposite of desire. The saying ‘rahbūt is better than raḥmūt’ favors fear over mercy.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r2.anchor: والعهد الوصية والرهبة الخوف وضدها الرغبة وفي مثل رهبوت خير من رحموت

TABRISI:2:40#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r3.claim: In the grammar, yāʾ is the vocative particle and Isrāʾīl is a genitive annexation, with fatḥa because it is a proper name of foreign origin and thus diptote.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r3.anchor: يا حرف النداء وهي في موضع نصب لأنه منادى مضاف واسرائيل في موضع جر لأنه مضاف إليه

TABRISI:2:40#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r4.claim: Iyyāya cannot be governed by ‘fear Me,’ because that verb is already occupied; an unspoken verb, ‘fear,’ governs it, and the following phrase explains that verb.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بقوله فارهبون لأنه مشغول

TABRISI:2:40#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r5.claim: A raised topic reading requires an omitted phrase, as in Sībawayh's verse; the same analysis supplies ‘as recited to you’ before the thief and adulteress in 5:38 and 24:2.

TABRISI:2:40#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r6.claim: After addressing all creatures with proofs of God's oneness and reminding them of favors to Adam, God singles out Israel for proofs and favors to them and their ancestors.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r6.anchor: لما عم الله تعالى جميع الخلق بالحجج الواضحة على توحيده وذكرهم ما أنعم به عليهم في أبيهم آدم

TABRISI:2:40#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r7.claim: ‘Children of Israel’ means descendants of Jacob and addresses Jews and Christians; Ibn ʿAbbās narrows the addressees to Jews in and around Medina.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r7.anchor: يعني يا بني يعقوب نسبهم إلى الأب الأعلى كما قال يا بني آدم والخطاب لليهود والنصارى

TABRISI:2:40#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#2/r8.claim: One interpretation recalls favors to their ancestors: many prophets and scriptures, rescue from Pharaoh and drowning, manna and quails, and kingship under Solomon; descendants inherit their ancestors’ honor.
TABRISI:2:40#2/r8.anchor: أراد بذلك النعم التي أنعم بها على أسلافهم من كثرة الأنبياء فيهم والكتب وإنجائهم من فرعون

TABRISI:2:40#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#3/r1.claim: The singular ‘favor’ can denote a whole class of blessings, as 14:34 shows: the blessings of God cannot be counted.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r1.anchor: والواحد لا يمكن عده وقيل المراد بها النعم

TABRISI:2:40#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#3/r2.claim: The two interpretations differ: the first recalls favors bestowed on ancestors, while the second recalls favors bestowed directly on Israel.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r2.anchor: فعلى القول الأول تكون الآية تذكيرا بالنعم عليهم في أسلافهم وعلى القول الثاني تكون تذكيرا بالنعم عليهم

TABRISI:2:40#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#3/r3.claim: Moses lists God's favors to Israel as making them prophets and kings and giving them what no other people received, in 5:20.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r3.anchor: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قومي اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا

TABRISI:2:40#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
TABRISI:2:40#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the favor is the Torah knowledge entrusted to them and its description of Muhammad; failing to follow the Prophet when he came made them like people who forgot it.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري أراد اذكروا ما أنعمت به عليكم فيما استودعتكم من علم التوراة

TABRISI:2:40#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:40#3/r5.claim: One view says the covenant was God's prior promise in the Torah to send Muhammad: believers who follow him receive two rewards, for following Moses and Muhammad, while rejecters face the Fire.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس فسمى ذلك عهدا لأنه تقدم به إليهم في الكتاب السابق

TABRISI:2:40#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:40#3/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the covenant as God's command to take the revealed book firmly and remember what it contains.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r6.anchor: بجد واذكروا ما فيه أي ما في الكتاب عن الحسن

TABRISI:2:40#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#3/r7.claim: A second interpretation recalls favors shared by Israel and their ancestors: their survival and descent, capacity to reason toward God and know him, provision, protection, and religious and worldly blessings.
TABRISI:2:40#3/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد بها النعم الواصلة إليهم مما اختصوا به دون آبائهم واشتركوا فيه مع آبائهم

TABRISI:2:40#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r1.claim: The covenant argument continues: denying real human acts would nullify divine promises and threats and undermine messengers and scriptures.

TABRISI:2:40#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:40#4/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the covenant with the pledge in 5:12: God would be with Israel if they prayed, gave alms, and believed in His messengers.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r2.anchor: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا

TABRISI:2:40#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the covenant to mean all divine commands and prohibitions.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r3.anchor: ورابعها: أنه أراد جميع الأوامر والنواهي

TABRISI:2:40#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r4.claim: Another interpretation says that making His favors known itself created a binding covenant to thank God for them.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r4.anchor: وخامسها: أنه جعل تعريفه إياهم نعمه عهدا عليهم وميثاقا

TABRISI:2:40#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r5.claim: The first covenant interpretation is strongest because most exegetes hold it and the Qur'an supports it.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r5.anchor: والأول أقوى لأن عليه أكثر المفسرين وبه يشهد القرآن

TABRISI:2:40#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r6.claim: ‘Fear Me alone’ means fear God in breaking the covenant.

TABRISI:2:40#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:2:40#4/r7.claim: The hadith says that speaking about blessings is gratitude; no grading is stated.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r7.anchor:
وفي الحديث:
" التحدث بالنعم شكر "
وفيها دلالة على عظم المعصية

TABRISI:2:40#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r8.claim: The verse establishes that gratitude for blessings is obligatory and that denying or concealing blessings is a grave sin subject to severe threat.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على وجوب شكر النعمة

TABRISI:2:40#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:40#4/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:40#4/r9.claim: The verse affirms that human acts are real: otherwise covenants, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, messengers, and scriptures would be invalid.
TABRISI:2:40#4/r9.anchor: ويدل أيضا على ثبوت أفعال العباد إذ لو لم تكن لهم أفعال لما صح العهد والأمر والنهي

THALABI:v1p185/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p185/r1.claim: Banu Isra’il are Jacob’s children; Isra’il is explained as ‘God’s chosen,’ with El meaning God, or alternatively as ‘servant of God.’
THALABI:v1p185/r1.anchor: يا بني إسرائيل أولاد يعقوب، ومعنى إسرائيل: صفوة الله، وإيل هو الله عز وجل، وقيل: معناه: عبد الله

THALABI:v1p185/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r2.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p185/r2.claim: A narrative says Jacob and Esau were twins who fought in the womb; Jacob waited to avoid Esau’s threat to kill their mother, then emerged holding Esau’s heel.
THALABI:v1p185/r2.anchor: قيل: سمي بذلك لأن يعقوب وعيصا كانا توأمين واقتتلا في بطن أمهما

THALABI:v1p185/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p185/r3.claim: The narrative derives Esau’s name from his coming out before Jacob, after Jacob had caught up with his heel.
THALABI:v1p185/r3.anchor: وسمي عيص لما عصى فخرج قبل يعقوب، وكان عيص أحبهما الى أبيه

THALABI:v1p185/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p185/r4.claim: In the story, Isaac favors Esau and Rebecca favors Jacob; Isaac, blind and seeking game, promises a blessing to Esau, who is hairy while Jacob is smooth.
THALABI:v1p185/r4.anchor: وكان عيص أحبهما الى أبيه وكان يعقوب أحبهما الى أمه

THALABI:v1p185/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r5.speaker: أم يعقوب
THALABI:v1p185/r5.claim: Jacob’s mother tells him to slaughter a sheep, wear its skin, and bring the food to Isaac pretending to be Esau; Isaac notices Esau’s touch but Jacob’s scent.
THALABI:v1p185/r5.anchor: فقالت أمه ليعقوب: يا بني اذهب إلى الغنم فاذبح منه شاة ثم اشوه والبس جلدها

THALABI:v1p185/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p185/r6.speaker: إسحاق
THALABI:v1p185/r6.claim: Isaac eats Jacob’s food and blesses his descendants to include prophets and kings; Esau returns angry and threatens to kill Jacob, then receives a blessing of numerous descendants whom none will rule.
THALABI:v1p185/r6.anchor: فدعا له أن يجعل في ذريته الأنبياء والملوك. وقام يعقوب وجاء عيص

THALABI:v1p186/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p186/r1.claim: The Prophet says gratitude for little is a condition of gratitude for much, thanking people is part of thanking God, publicizing God’s favor is gratitude, and unity is mercy while division is punishment.
THALABI:v1p186/r1.anchor: روى الشعبي عن النعمان بن بشير قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من لم يشكر القليل لم يشكر الكثير

THALABI:v1p186/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p186/r2.claim: The singular ni‘ma here means God’s many favors; Thalabi cites the statement that people cannot enumerate God’s favors.
THALABI:v1p186/r2.anchor: نعمتي أراد نعمي أعطها وهي واحد [بمعنى الجمع] وهو قوله تعالى وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها

THALABI:v1p186/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p186/r3.claim: The favors were bestowed on Israel’s ancestors: the sea’s parting, rescue from Pharaoh, inheritance of enemy property, shade and night light in the wilderness, manna and quails, twelve springs, and the Torah.
THALABI:v1p186/r3.anchor: التي أنعمت عليكم أي على أجدادكم، وذلك أن الله تعالى فلق لهم البحر وأنجاهم من فرعون

THALABI:v1p186/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p186/r4.claim: Keeping God’s covenant means God will admit them to Paradise and fulfill what He promised them.
THALABI:v1p186/r4.anchor: أوفوا بعهدي الذي عهدت إليكم أوف بعهدكم أدخلكم الجنة وأنجز لكم ما وعدتكم

THALABI:v1p186/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r5.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v1p186/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri reads awfi with a doubled f for emphasis; waffa and awfa both mean completion.
THALABI:v1p186/r5.anchor: فقرأ الزهري: أوف بالتشديد على التأكيد يقال: ووفى وأوفى كلها بمعنى [واحد] وأصلها الإتمام

THALABI:v1p186/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v1p186/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says God covenanted through Moses to send an unlettered prophet from Ishmael; followers would be forgiven, admitted to Paradise, and given a double reward, linking this to the People of Scripture’s duty to disclose Muhammad’s coming.
THALABI:v1p186/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي: عهد الى بني إسرائيل على لسان موسى: إني باعث من بني إسماعيل نبيا أميا

THALABI:v1p186/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v1p186/r7.claim: Qatada identifies the covenant with the pledges to worship God alone and to offer a goodly loan, followed by God’s promise to expiate sins.
THALABI:v1p186/r7.anchor: قتادة: هو العهد الذي أخذ الله عليهم في قوله: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وقوله تعالى: قرضا حسنا

THALABI:v1p186/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p186/r8.claim: Thalabi quotes the covenant that Israel worship none but God as an example of the pledge meant by ‘fulfill My covenant.’
THALABI:v1p186/r8.anchor: فقال: وإذ أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل لا تعبدون إلا الله الآية

THALABI:v1p186/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p186/r9.claim: Hasan says the covenant was the pledge taken when the mountain was raised above them.
THALABI:v1p186/r9.anchor: الحسن: هو قوله: وإذ أخذنا ميثاقكم ورفعنا فوقكم الطور الآية

THALABI:v1p186/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p186/r10.speaker: إسماعيل بن زياد
THALABI:v1p186/r10.claim: Isma‘il ibn Ziyad identifies the covenant as not fleeing battle, citing the pledge not to turn their backs.
THALABI:v1p186/r10.anchor: إسماعيل بن زياد: ولا تفروا من الزحف أدخلكم الجنة

ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r1.claim: This passage continues the preceding discussion of the ongoing guidance given to humanity through revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r1.anchor: continuous guidance vouchsafed to man through divine revelation

ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r2.claim: Israel is invoked because its religious beliefs were an earlier monotheistic phase, culminating in the Qur'anic revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:2:40#n31/r2.anchor: their religious beliefs represented an earlier phase of the monotheistic concept which culminates in the revelation of the Qur'an

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد، الكسائي، أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd, citing al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubayda, says wafaytu and awfaytu both mean that one fulfilled a covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r1.anchor: أبو عبيد عن الكسائي وأبي عبيدة: وفيت بالعهد وأوفيت به سواء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r2.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r2.claim: Shammar distinguishes wafaa as a statement or measure reaching completion, while awfaa means fully paying another's right or measure without shortfall.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r2.anchor: يقال: وفى وأوفى، فمن قال: (وفى) فإنه يقول تم، كقولك: وفى لنا فلان، أي: تم لنا قوله ولم يغدر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r3.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r3.claim: Abu al-Haytham rejects Shammar's distinction: both forms mean fulfilling a covenant, and Quranic examples use the form with alif.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم فيما رد على شمر: الذي قال شمر (¬5) في (وفى) و (أوفى): باطل، إنما يقال: أوفيت بالعهد ووفيت بالعهد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r4.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r4.claim: The cited line combines awfa and wafa, illustrating both forms in use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r4.anchor: وقال الشاعر (¬4) في الجمع بين اللغتين:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the covenant as the Torah's promise of Muhammad: believers receive two rewards for following Moses and Muhammad, while rejecters face accumulated sins and Hell; God promises Paradise for fulfilling it regarding Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p430/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا العهد هو أن الله عز وجل (¬6) عهد إليهم في التوراة أنه باعث نبيا يقال له: محمد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r1.claim: Iyyaya is accusative under an implicit verb, explained by the following farhabun; the explicit verb cannot govern it because that verb is occupied by its object pronoun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r1.anchor: موضع (إياي) نصب بإضمار فعل (¬1) تفسيره (¬2) المذكور بعده (¬3) كأنه قيل: (إياي فارهبوا (¬4) فارهبون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r2.claim: The final ya is omitted from farhabun to preserve the verse ending's cadence; language scholars call verse endings fawasil and poetic line endings qawafi.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r2.anchor: وحذفت (الياء) من {فارهبون} لأنها فاصلة أي رأس آية، ليكون النظم على لفظ متسق،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p432/r3.claim: The command means to fear God by breaking the covenant.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r1.claim: The Children of Israel are Jacob's descendants; remembering God's blessing means thanking Him for favors such as the sea's parting, rescue from Pharaoh, and cloud shade, bestowed on their ancestors and therefore also blessings for them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r1.anchor: أولاد يعقوب عليه السلام { اذكروا } اشكروا، وذكر النعمة هو شكرها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r2.claim: The blessings included the sea's parting, rescue from Pharaoh, cloud shade, and all other favors; benefits to their ancestors count as benefits to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r2.anchor: فلق البحر، والإنجاء من فرعون، وتظليل الغمام، إلى سائر ما أنعم الله تعالى به عليهم،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r3.claim: Giving thanks for these favors requires obeying God by believing in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r3.anchor: وشكر هذه النعم طاعته في الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r4.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant means keeping faith concerning Muhammad; God's fulfillment is admitting them to Paradise, and they must fear Him over breaking the covenant.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:40-41/r4.anchor: أي: في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { أوف بعهدكم } أدخلكم الجنة { وإياي فارهبون } فخافوني في نقض العهد.

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r1.claim: “I seek refuge in God” has the form of a report but functions as a prayer meaning “O God, protect me”; “I seek forgiveness” works the same way.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r1.anchor: قوله { أعوذ بالله } لفظه الخبر ومعناه الدعاء والتقدير : اللهم أعذني ألا ترى أنه قال : ^ { وإني أعيذها بك

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r2.claim: A report about one's own act of seeking refuge has no benefit by itself; its purpose is for God to grant protection.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r2.anchor: وهذا القدر لا فائدة فيه إنما الفائدة في أن يعيذه الله فما السبب في أنه قال أعوذ بالله ولم يقل أعذني

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r3.claim: The wording invokes a covenant between Lord and servant: after the servant fulfills the covenant of servitude, God's greater generosity calls Him to fulfill the covenant of lordship and protect the servant from Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r3.anchor: وقال ^ { وأوفوا بعهدي أوف بعهدكم } ^ [ البقرة : 40 ] فكأن العبد يقول أنا مع لؤم الإنسانية ونقص البشرية

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r4.claim: Rāzī holds that the present verb is literal for the present and figurative for the future; future reference is marked by sa- or sawfa.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r4.anchor: والحق أنه حقيقة في الحال مجاز في الاستقبال وإنما يختص به بحرف السين وسوف

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r5.claim: Rāzī raises questions about why the present is shared with the future rather than the past, how the imperfect resembles a noun, and what governs it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r5.anchor: لم وقع الاشتراك بين الحاضر والمستقبل ولم يقع بين الحاضر والماضي ؟ ( ه ) كيف المشابهة بين المضارع وبين الاسم .

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r6.claim: “I seek refuge” describes the speaker's present refuge and all future refuge, which Rāzī calls perfection, then asks whether it implies that refuge remains in Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r6.anchor: قوله { أعوذ } يدل على أن العبد مستعيذ في الحال وفي كل المستقبل وهو الكمال فهل يدل على أن هذه الاستعاذة باقية في الجنة .

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r7.claim: Rāzī notes that the first-person formula is self-narration and must contain four elements, as in the cited phrase from 33:33.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r7.anchor: قوله { أعوذ } حكاية عن النفس ولا بد من الأربعة المذكورة في قوله ﴿ أتين ﴾ [ الأحزاب : 33 ] .

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r8.claim: Basrans call the bāʾ in bi-llāh the attachment bāʾ, Kufans call it instrumental, and others call it the bāʾ of implication.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r8.anchor: الباء في قوله بالله باء الإلصاق وفيه مسائل : المسألة الأولى : البصريون يسمونه باء الألصاق والكوفيون يسمونه باء الآلة

RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r9.claim: The bāʾ attaches to a verb: the verb cannot attach directly to itself, so the bāʾ's object supplies the means through which attachment occurs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p85#2/r9.anchor: حاصل الكلام أن هذه الباء متعلقة بفعل لا محالة ؛ والفائدة فيه أنه لا يمكن إلصاق ذلك الفعل بنفسه إلا بواسطة الشيء

BURHAN:v1p159/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p159/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p159/r9.claim: Israel is used instead of Jacob when addressing the Israelites to recall God and their ancestors’ religion; the name is interpreted as connected to God.
BURHAN:v1p159/r9.anchor: سموا بالاسم الذى فيه تذكرة بالله فإن إسرائيل اسم مضاف إلى الله سبحانه فى التأويل

BURHAN:v1p159/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p159/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p159/r10.claim: When addressing converts called sons of Abdullah, the Prophet used their father’s name to urge the servitude it implies; the source uses this as a parallel.
BURHAN:v1p159/r10.anchor: يحرضهم بذلك على ما يقتضيه اسمه من العبودية

BURHAN:v2p192/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p192/r4.speaker: العلماء
BURHAN:v2p192/r4.claim: Scholars explain the covenant by the conditions in 5:12: if Israel fulfills its obligations, God fulfills His promise to forgive their sins.

BURHAN:v3p197/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r5.claim: When the described noun is definite, its accusative cannot be governed by an implied أعني; estimate أذكر or أمدح instead.
BURHAN:v3p197/r5.anchor: إذا كان المنعوت متعينا لم يجز تقديره ناصب نعته بأعنى

BURHAN:v3p197/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r8.claim: Where praise is absent, the governing verb must be elided; spelling out أحلف بالله would make the oath a promise instead.
BURHAN:v3p197/r8.anchor: والذي لا مدح فيه فاختزال العامل فيه واجب كاختزاله في والله لأفعلن

BURHAN:v3p197/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.claim: The general omitted-governor category covers accusatives licensed by an expressed, understood, or estimated verb; the cited constructions illustrate its varied triggers.
BURHAN:v3p197/r9.anchor: والعام كل منصوب دل عليه الفعل لفظا أو معنى أو تقديرا ويحذف لأسباب

BURHAN:v3p197/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.claim: One reason to omit the verb is that another expression explains it; examples include إياي فارهبون, والسماء رفعها, and conditional clauses.
BURHAN:v3p197/r10.anchor: أحدها أن يكون مفسرا كقوله تعالى

ITQAN:v3p50/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p50/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p50/r1.claim: Qur’anic clarification may occur in the same passage or in another verse; the covenant in 2:40 is explained by the duties and promise in 5:12.

ITQAN:v4p380/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p380/r3.claim: Israel is Jacob’s title; proposed meanings include servant of God, God’s chosen one, and God traveled by night because Jacob journeyed at night during migration.
ITQAN:v4p380/r3.anchor: إسرائيل لقب يعقوب ومعناه عبد الله وقيل صفوة الله وقيل سرى الله لأنه أسرى لما هاجر

ITQAN:v4p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p380/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report transmitted by Ibn Jarir through ʿUmayr, glosses Israel as equivalent to Abdullah.
ITQAN:v4p380/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير من طريق عمير عن ابن عباس أن إسرائيل كقولك عبد الله

ITQAN:v4p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
ITQAN:v4p380/r5.claim: Abu Mujliz relates that Jacob wrestled an angel, who struck his thighs; Jacob demanded a name from him and was called Israel, which Abu Mujliz says is among angelic names.
ITQAN:v4p380/r5.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال كان يعقوب رجلا بطيشا فلقى ملكا فعالجه فصرعه الملك فضرب على فخذيه

ITQAN:v4p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p380/r6.claim: Israel is most commonly spelled with yaʾ after the hamza and a lam; a reading without hamza is also reported.
ITQAN:v4p380/r6.anchor: وفيه لغات أشهرها بياء بعد الهمزة ولام وقرئ إسراييل بلا همز

ITQAN:v4p380/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v4p380/r7.claim: Some explain that the Qur’an addresses Jews as Children of Israel rather than Children of Jacob to remind them of their ancestors’ religion and of God through Israel’s interpreted name.
ITQAN:v4p380/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم ولم يخاطب اليهود في القرآن إلا

ITQAN:v4p380/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p380/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v4p380/r8.claim: The name Jacob is used when recounting the gift to Abraham because Jacob was followed by a successor, so it better signals succession.
ITQAN:v4p380/r8.anchor: ولما ذكر موهبته لإبراهيم وتبشيره به قال يعقوب وكان أولى من إسرائيل لأنها موهبة بمعقب آخر فناسب ذكر اسم يشعر بالتعقيب

DAMGHANI:v1p460/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r1.claim: Niʿmah can mean God's favor or blessing bestowed on people.
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r1.anchor: عليكم أي منته مثلها في سورة الأحزاب والمائدة كقوله تعالى في سورة البقرة يا بني اسرائيل اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم

NASHR:v2p169#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p169#2/r3.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v2p169#2/r3.claim: Readers agree to keep the yāʾ quiescent in bi-ahdi uwfi and atuni afrigh, the author explaining this by their many letters.
NASHR:v2p169#2/r3.anchor: (واتفقوا) على إسكان ياءين من هذا الفصل، وهما في البقرة بعهدي أوف

NASHR:v2p236/r28.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r28.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p236/r28.claim: Yaʿqūb affirms the yāʾs in فارهبون, فاتقون, and تكفرون both at pause and in continuation.
NASHR:v2p236/r28.anchor: فارهبون، فاتقون. تكفرون أثبتهن في الحالتين يعقوب

NASHR:v2p211#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p211#2/r1.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p211#2/r1.claim: Yaʿqub retains the final yāʾ in both forms in connected and paused recitation.
NASHR:v2p211#2/r1.anchor: وتقدم مذهب يعقوب في إثبات ياء فارهبون وفاتقون في الحالين مجملا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p595/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p595/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p595/r5.claim: This is the third address to Israel by the name linking them to their forefather, honoring them through descent from him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p595/r5.anchor: وكان ثالث نداء نودي به بنو إسرائيل، بالإضافة إلى أبيهم الأعلى، وتشريفهم بولادتهم منه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: Exegetes often use concise idioms that attribute actions to God—such as addressing believers or recounting speech—though the verse or wording is the actual subject; he gives the primordial covenant as an example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: وقف الله ذرية آدم على ربوبيته بقوله: ألست بربكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r2.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r2.claim: Some legal theorists prohibit saying “God narrated” and similar expressions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض الأصوليين أنه لا يجوز أن يقال: حكى الله ولا ما جرى مجراه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya permits such wording as common Arabic when it means that a verse or expression recounts something; he avoids it where possible and explains why it may appear in his commentary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: وأما إذا استعمل ذلك في سياق الكلام والمراد منه حكت الآية أو اللفظ فذلك استعمال عربي شائع وعليه مشى الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r4.speaker: أبو عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r4.claim: Abū ʿĀmir’s poetic appeal to the Prophet says forgive, may I be your ransom, what we have done, an idiomatic example involving divine action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r4.anchor: فمن ذلك قول أبي عامر يرتجز بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فاغفر فداء لك ما اقتفينا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r5.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r5.claim: Umm Salama’s report about Abū Salama’s death and God giving her the Prophet as a replacement illustrates such Arabic phrasing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r5.anchor: وقول أم سلمة: فعزم الله لي في الحديث في موت أبي سلمة وإبدال الله لها منه رسول الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r6.claim: The idiom God knows applies dirāya, though that word can imply working toward knowledge until it is attained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك قولهم: الله يدري كذا وكذا والدراية إنما هي التأتي للعلم بالشيء حتى يتيسر ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r7.speaker: بعض أهل النظر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r7.claim: Some thinkers cite al-Jawharī’s line No, Lord, I do not know, while You are the knower to defend this idiom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r7.anchor: واحتج بعض أهل النظر على جواز هذا الإطلاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī says that poetic evidence is inconclusive because the line may contain a grammatical error.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: «وهذا لا ثبت فيه لأنه يجوز أن يكون من غلط الاعراب»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards the whole idiomatic practice as valid Arabic and says critical scrutiny does not disprove it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r9.anchor: وكذلك أقول إن الطريقة كلها عربية لا يثبت للنظر المنخول شيء منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r10.speaker: العجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r10.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line says my Lord was pleased and means He had mercy on me, another Arabic example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54/r10.anchor: وقد قال العجاج: فارتاح ربي وأراد رحمتي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r18.speaker: معترك الأقران
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r18.claim: The cited work contrasts Baqara’s reminder of blessings to the Children of Israel with Araf’s reproach for asking for an idol and later worshipping the calf; each narrative frame shapes its wording.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#3/r18.anchor: جاء في (معترك الأقران) : "إن آية البقرة في معرض ذكر النعم علهيم حيث قال:

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r1.speaker: أحمد بن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r1.claim: These transmitters report Nāfiʿ leaving the yāʾ still in several further forms before a cut hamza and a non-jussive verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r1.anchor: وهو مع فعل غير مجزوم فيما ذكر أحمد بن جماز وإسماعيل بن جعفر قوله: بعهدي أوف

NASHR:v1p399/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p399/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p399/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar facilitates the hamza in إسرائيل wherever it occurs; the other readers verify it.
NASHR:v1p399/r3.anchor: فسهل الهمزة فيهما أبو جعفر، وحققها الباقون
